grammar.countability: uncountable (art or display) / countable (individual shaped plant or figure)
patterns: clip + a shrub + into + a shape

usage.counting: Use topiary without an article for the art. For individual pieces, a topiary figure and topiary figures are useful, and a topiary and topiaries are also used.

en: the art of shaping living shrubs or trees into decorative forms, usually by clipping them
shrubs or trees shaped in this way, or an individual decorative plant figure
ja: 低木や樹木を刈り込み、動物や幾何学模様などの装飾的な形に仕立てる技法、トピアリー
その技法で仕立てた植栽や、個々の植物の造形物

nuance.en: Topiary suggests deliberate ornamental shaping. Forms range from simple spheres and spirals to elaborate animals. The word can refer to the craft, the shaped plants in a garden as a whole, or an individual figure.
nuance.ja: 鑑賞できる形に意図的に仕立てるという含みがある。球やらせんのような幾何学形から、手の込んだ動物の姿までさまざま。技法そのもの、庭の刈り込み植栽全体、個々の造形のいずれにも使える。

en: pruning. The general practice of cutting parts off a plant, for example to maintain health or control growth. Topiary is shaping a plant for decorative effect.
hedge trimming. Often means keeping a hedge tidy or at a set height. A hedge can also be clipped into ornamental forms as part of topiary.
bonsai. The art of cultivating miniature trees in containers. Topiary emphasizes making a decorative outline or figure with living plants.
ja: pruning は、植物の健康を保ったり成長を調整したりするための剪定全般。topiary は装飾的な形に仕立てることに重点がある。
hedge trimming は、生け垣の高さや輪郭を整える刈り込み。生け垣を装飾的な形に仕立てる場合は topiary にも当たる。
bonsai は、鉢の中で小さな樹木を育てて鑑賞する技法。topiary は、生きた植物で装飾的な輪郭や像を形づくることに重点がある。

note.en: A descriptive paraphrase for the traditional technique.
note.ja: 伝統的な技法を説明する「装飾的な刈り込み」という言い換え。

etymology.en: From French topiaire, ultimately from Latin topiarius, ‘ornamental gardener’.
etymology.ja: フランス語 topiaire を経て、ラテン語 topiarius（装飾庭園を手入れする庭師）にさかのぼる。

en: a topiary garden
the art of topiary
a topiary figure
a boxwood topiary
animal-shaped topiaries
a topiary display
ja: a topiary garden — 刈り込みで仕立てた植栽のある庭園
the art of topiary — トピアリーの技法
a topiary figure — 植物で作った装飾的な像
a boxwood topiary — ツゲを刈り込んで作ったトピアリー
animal-shaped topiaries — 動物の形に仕立てたトピアリー
a topiary display — トピアリーの展示

en: The topiary garden is full of yew trees clipped into cones, spirals, and birds.
Two boxwood topiaries in matching pots frame the front door.
She took a course in topiary and learned to shape a boxwood shrub into a sphere.
ja: The topiary garden is full of yew trees clipped into cones, spirals, and birds. — その庭園には、円すい形やらせん形、鳥の姿に刈り込まれたイチイの木が並んでいる。
Two boxwood topiaries in matching pots frame the front door. — 玄関の両脇には、おそろいの鉢に植えられたツゲのトピアリーが置かれている。
She took a course in topiary and learned to shape a boxwood shrub into a sphere. — 彼女はトピアリーの講座を受け、ツゲを球形に仕立てる方法を学んだ。

patterns: it is / was considerate of + person + to + verb
be considerate of + someone's needs / feelings

usage.of: In It was considerate of Maya to call, of introduces the person who acted. In be considerate of other people's needs, of introduces what deserves consideration.
usage.towards: Use toward or towards to introduce the person or group receiving that consideration.

en: showing care for other people's feelings, needs, or convenience
done with attention to how it will affect other people
ja: 人の気持ちや必要、都合によく気を配る、思いやりのある
相手への影響を考えて行われた、配慮の行き届いた

nuance.en: Considerate often describes small practical choices that make life easier or more comfortable for others, such as lowering your voice or giving advance notice. It can praise a single action or describe a person's usual behavior.
nuance.ja: 声を落とす、予定が変わったら早めに知らせるなど、他人が困らないようにする日常的な気遣いを表す。一度の行動をほめる場合にも、その人の普段の振る舞いを表す場合にも使える。

en: thoughtful. Often highlights a gesture that shows someone has thought about you. Considerate is especially apt when the gesture takes your needs or convenience into account.
kind. Broadly describes warmth or helpfulness. Considerate emphasizes awareness of how one's actions affect others.
polite. Typically concerns manners or courtesy. Considerate also covers practical choices, such as keeping noise down.
considerable. Means large or significant in amount or degree. Considerate describes regard for other people.
ja: thoughtful は、相手のことを考えてした気の利いた行動をほめるときによく使う。considerate は特に相手の都合や必要に配慮することを表す。
kind は親切さや優しさを広く表す。considerate は、自分の言動が相手にどう影響するかへの気遣いに重点がある。
polite は礼儀正しさが中心。considerate は、物音を抑えるなど、相手に負担をかけない実際の行動にも使う。
considerable は、量や程度が「かなりの」という意味。considerate は人に対する配慮を表す。

note.en: Close when praising a gesture that shows care for others.
note.ja: 人への気遣いが表れた行動をほめる用法で近い。

etymology.en: From Latin consideratus, the past participle of considerare ‘to examine or consider’. An early English sense was ‘showing careful thought’.
etymology.ja: ラテン語 considerare（検討する）の過去分詞 consideratus に由来する。初期の英語では「よく考えた」という意味で使われた。

en: a considerate neighbor
a considerate gesture
be considerate toward your roommates
be considerate of other people's time
try to be more considerate
it was considerate of you to let me know
ja: a considerate neighbor — 周囲に気を配る近所の人
a considerate gesture — 気遣いのある行動
be considerate toward your roommates — ルームメイトに配慮する
be considerate of other people's time — 他の人の時間を大切にする
try to be more considerate — もう少し周りに気を配るようにする
it was considerate of you to let me know — 知らせてくれるなんて気が利いていた

en: It was considerate of you to let me know before I left home.
Please be considerate of other passengers and keep your voice down.
Our upstairs neighbors are considerate about noise and always warn us before a party.
She's considerate toward new team members and gives them time to ask questions.
ja: It was considerate of you to let me know before I left home. — 私が家を出る前に知らせてくれて助かったよ。
Please be considerate of other passengers and keep your voice down. — ほかの乗客に配慮して、声を落としてください。
Our upstairs neighbors are considerate about noise and always warn us before a party. — 上の階の住人は騒音に気を配っていて、パーティーを開く前にはいつも知らせてくれる。
She's considerate toward new team members and gives them time to ask questions. — 彼女は新しいチームメンバーに気を配り、質問する時間を設けている。

patterns: keep / place + someone or something + under surveillance

usage.article: In the usual sense use surveillance without an indefinite article, as in under surveillance. A surveillance operation is countable because operation is the head noun.
usage.verb: Say keep someone under surveillance or monitor someone. The noun itself does not function as a verb.

en: close and often sustained observation of a person, place, or activity, especially for security or investigation
systematic tracking of health events or trends through ongoing data collection and analysis
ja: 警備や捜査などのために、人・場所・活動を注意深く見張ること、監視
公衆衛生などで、データを継続的に集めて分析し、発生状況や動向を把握すること、サーベイランス

nuance.en: In security contexts, surveillance evokes organized watching, often by police, security staff, or cameras. It can be overt or covert. In public health, the same word refers to tracking patterns across a population, such as changes in the number of reported cases.
nuance.ja: 警備・捜査の文脈では、警察や警備員、カメラなどによる組織的な見張りを連想させる。公然と行う場合にも、ひそかに行う場合にも使える。公衆衛生では集団全体が対象で、報告された症例数の推移などを継続的に把握することを指す。

en: monitoring. A broader term for checking a condition or process over time, such as temperature or system performance. Surveillance often suggests organized observation for security or early detection.
observation. A broad term for watching or studying. Surveillance usually implies a specific purpose and some continuity or organization.
spying. Suggests secretly gathering information. Surveillance can be publicly disclosed, and its purpose can be routine security.
ja: monitoring は温度やシステムの稼働状況などを継続して確認することにも使える広い語。surveillance は警備や異変の早期把握を目的とする組織的な観察を連想させやすい。
observation は観察や観測全般を指す。surveillance は特定の目的を持ち、継続的または組織的に行うという含みが出やすい。
spying はひそかに情報を集めること。surveillance は実施を公表した日常的な警備にも使える。

note.en: A broader term for ongoing observation or checking.
note.ja: 継続的な観察や確認を表す、より広い語。

note.en: A plain paraphrase in the sense of watching someone or something carefully.
note.ja: 人や物を注意深く観察する意味での平易な言い換え。

etymology.en: Borrowed from French surveillance. Its elements are sur- ‘over’ and veiller ‘to keep watch’, from Latin vigilare.
etymology.ja: フランス語 surveillance から借用された。sur-（上から）と veiller（見張る）からなり、veiller はラテン語 vigilare にさかのぼる。

en: be under surveillance
keep a building under surveillance
a surveillance camera
review surveillance footage
covert surveillance
mass surveillance
public health surveillance
disease surveillance

patterns: a canvass of + voters / election results

usage.preposition: Canvass for votes means to seek votes. In U.S. election administration, canvass the votes can mean to review and verify the vote totals.
usage.spelling: Canvass and canvas sound alike. Canvass ends in -ss. Canvas, the cloth or painting surface, ends in one s.

en: to talk to people, often door to door, to seek votes or support
to ask a group of people for information or opinions
to put forward or discuss an idea for consideration, especially in British English
to review and verify vote totals, especially in U.S. election administration
an organized effort to contact people for support or information, or an official review of election results
ja: 戸別訪問などで人に接触し、票や支持を求める
人々に聞いて回り、意見や情報を集める
案を検討に付す、話し合う（特に英国）
投票結果を照合・確認する（特に米国の選挙実務）
支持や情報を求めて人々に接触する活動、または選挙結果の公式な確認（名詞）

nuance.en: Canvass often suggests actively contacting people one by one. If campaigners canvass for votes, they are seeking support. If a committee canvasses members' views, it is trying to find out what members think. The U.S. administrative sense refers to checking election results after voting.
nuance.ja: 一人ひとりに働きかけたり、聞いて回ったりする感じがある。選挙運動員が canvass for votes するなら票を求めている。委員会が canvass members' views するなら、会員の意見を集めている。米国の選挙実務では、投票後に結果を照合・確認することも指す。

en: survey. Often suggests a structured effort to gather answers, for example using a questionnaire. Canvass highlights actively seeking views or support.
campaign. Covers the wider effort to promote a candidate or cause. Canvassing is one way of campaigning.
solicit. Means actively asking for something such as donations or feedback. Canvass often suggests reaching out to a number of people.
canvas. A homophone for sturdy cloth or the surface on which someone paints.
ja: survey は質問票などで情報を体系的に集めることを指す場合が多い。canvass は、意見や支持を求めて人々に働きかける点が焦点。
campaign は候補者や大義を支持して行う運動全体。canvassing はその手段の一つ。
solicit は寄付や意見などを積極的に求めること。canvass は複数の人に聞いて回る感じが出やすい。
canvas は同音異綴りで、丈夫な布地や絵を描く画布を指す。

note.en: Close for seeking votes or support.
note.ja: 票や支持を求める場合に近い。

note.en: Close for finding out what someone thinks.
note.ja: 相手の考えを探る場合に近い。

etymology.en: Historically related to canvas. Early uses referred to tossing someone in a canvas sheet. The modern senses developed later.
etymology.ja: 歴史的には canvas（帆布）と同じ語に由来する。初期には帆布に人を載せて放り上げる意味で使われ、現在の意味は後に発達した。

equivalents.it: andare a caccia di voti / sondare le opinioni
equivalents.es: hacer campaña entre los votantes / sondear la opinión

Before changing the opening hours, the library canvassed regular users about the proposal. — 開館時間を変更する前に、図書館は常連の利用者に案について意見を聞いた。
The idea of sharing an office was canvassed at the meeting. — オフィスを共同で使う案が会議で検討に付された。
The board canvassed the vote totals before the results were certified. — 選挙結果が正式に認定される前に、委員会は集計結果を照合・確認した。

grammar.countability: countable (achievement or skill) / uncountable (completion or sense of achievement)

usage.counting: An accomplishment refers to one result or skill. In a sense of accomplishment, the article belongs to sense. The formal expression the accomplishment of a task means carrying it out successfully.

en: something successfully done, often through effort or skill
successful completion or fulfillment of a task or aim
a skill someone has acquired, especially in a traditional or somewhat formal description
ja: 成し遂げたこと、成果、実績
課題をやり遂げること、目標の達成・遂行
身につけた技能や特技（やや改まった用法）

nuance.en: Accomplishment often draws attention to what someone managed to get done and the work or skill it took. A sense of accomplishment is the satisfaction of having done something worthwhile, whether it was a major project or a small task you had been putting off. In formal biographical writing, someone's accomplishments can include cultivated skills such as playing an instrument.
nuance.ja: 何を成し遂げたか、そのためにどんな努力や技量が必要だったかに目を向ける語。a sense of accomplishment は、大きな仕事でも、後回しにしていた小さな用事でも、やり終えたときの満足感を表す。改まった人物紹介では、楽器の演奏など身につけた技能を accomplishments と呼ぶこともある。

en: achievement. Often interchangeable for a result earned through effort. Achievement also fits milestones such as winning an award. Accomplishment can draw attention to the work that went into getting something done.
feat. Often highlights how difficult or unusual the action was. An accomplishment can also be an ordinary task that matters to the person who completed it.
completion. Focuses on reaching the end of a task. Accomplishment can frame the result as something worth recognizing.
ja: achievement は、努力して得た成果について入れ替えられることが多い。受賞などの節目にもよく合う。accomplishment は、やり遂げるまでの取り組みに目を向ける場合にも使いやすい。
feat は、難しいことや並外れたことをした点を強調する。accomplishment は、本人にとって意味のある日常の小さな達成にも使える。
completion は作業が終わったことに重点がある。accomplishment には、その成果を評価したり誇りに思ったりする含みが出ることがある。

note.en: The closest general equivalent for a result attained through effort.
note.ja: 努力して得た成果を表す最も近い一般語。

note.en: A formal equivalent when referring to reaching a goal or standard.
note.ja: 目標や基準に到達する意味で近い改まった語。

etymology.en: From Old French acomplissement ‘completion’, from acomplir ‘to carry out or fulfill’. It shares its root with accomplish.
etymology.ja: 古フランス語 acomplissement（完遂）に由来し、acomplir（遂行する、果たす）にさかのぼる。accomplish と同じ語根を持つ。

equivalents.it: il risultato / il traguardo / il senso di realizzazione
equivalents.fr: la réalisation / l’accomplissement / le sentiment d’accomplissement
equivalents.es: el logro / la consecución / la sensación de logro

a feeling of accomplishment
a major accomplishment

quite an accomplishment
celebrate someone's accomplishments

ja: Finishing the first draft gave me a real sense of accomplishment. — 初稿を書き上げて、確かな達成感があった。

Playing the harp was one of her many accomplishments. — ハープの演奏は、彼女が身につけた数々の特技の一つだった。

grammar.countability: countable (usually singular in the figurative sense)
patterns: the pinnacle of + career / profession / field
be at the pinnacle of + something

usage.article: The figurative sense usually takes the: the pinnacle of her career. For individual rock formations or architectural elements, use a pinnacle or the plural pinnacles.
usage.preposition: Reach the pinnacle takes a direct object. Use at to describe a position already held: She is at the pinnacle of her profession.

en: the highest point of success, achievement, or standing in a career or field
a tall, pointed rock or peak
a small decorative pointed structure on a building, especially in Gothic architecture
ja: 経歴や分野などでの成功・評価の頂点、最高峰
高く突き出た尖った岩、岩峰
建物の上部などに設ける小さな尖塔・尖塔状の装飾、特にゴシック建築のもの

nuance.en: Pinnacle presents something as the highest level of achievement or prestige. The pinnacle of her career is her most successful period or moment. The pinnacle of mechanical watchmaking can be a watch or an achievement regarded as the finest example of the craft.
nuance.ja: 成功や評価の最も高いところを指し、称賛を込めることが多い。the pinnacle of her career は経歴で最も成功した時期や瞬間。the pinnacle of mechanical watchmaking なら、機械式時計製造の最高峰と見なされる作品や成果を指しうる。

en: peak. A broad word for a high point, including a measurable maximum such as peak demand. Pinnacle often highlights prestige or achievement.
summit. Commonly names the highest point of a mountain. A rock pinnacle can be a pointed formation along a ridge.
apex. Often describes the top of a hierarchy or an angular point. Pinnacle can add a sense of admiration for the achievement.
spire. Often refers to the main tall, pointed structure on a church or tower. A pinnacle is typically one of the smaller pointed architectural features.
ja: peak は山頂や需要のピークなど、高い点や最大値を広く指す。pinnacle は成功や評価の高さを強調する場合が多い。
summit は山の最高地点を指す一般的な語。岩の pinnacle は尾根から突き出た個々の岩峰も指せる。
apex は階層の最上位や形の頂点にも使う。pinnacle は到達した成果への称賛を込めやすい。
spire は教会などの大きく高い尖塔を指すことが多い。建築の pinnacle は、小さな尖塔状の装飾を指すのが一般的。

note.en: A more general equivalent for the highest point of a career or activity.
note.ja: 経歴や活動の頂点を指す、より一般的な語。

note.en: A formal equivalent for the height of success, power, or influence.
note.ja: 成功・権力・影響力の絶頂を表す改まった語。

etymology.en: From Old French, ultimately from Late Latin pinnaculum, a diminutive of pinna ‘wing’ or ‘point’.
etymology.ja: 古フランス語を経て後期ラテン語 pinnaculum に由来する。pinna（翼、尖った先端）の指小形。

equivalents.de: der Gipfel / der Höhepunkt / die Fiale (Architektur)
equivalents.es: la cima / la cúspide / el pináculo

the carved pinnacles of a cathedral — 大聖堂の彫刻が施された小尖塔

en: Conducting the orchestra she had admired since childhood was the pinnacle of her career.
Collectors regard the watch as the pinnacle of the maker’s craftsmanship.
A narrow rock pinnacle rose above the ridge.
The restoration team repaired several of the cathedral’s carved stone pinnacles.
ja: Conducting the orchestra she had admired since childhood was the pinnacle of her career. — 子どもの頃から憧れていたオーケストラを指揮したことが、彼女のキャリアの頂点だった。
Collectors regard the watch as the pinnacle of the maker’s craftsmanship. — 収集家たちはその時計を、作り手の技術の粋を極めたものと見ている。
A narrow rock pinnacle rose above the ridge. — 尾根の上に細く尖った岩峰がそびえていた。
The restoration team repaired several of the cathedral’s carved stone pinnacles. — 修復チームは、大聖堂の石造りの小尖塔のうち、彫刻が施された数基を修復した。

patterns: overstate + the importance / impact / risk of + something
cannot / can't overstate how + adjective + clause

usage.emphasis: I can't overstate how important this is means that it is extremely important. The negative form emphasizes the importance.
usage.passive: The benefits were overstated criticizes the description. The importance of checking the figures cannot be overstated emphasizes how important the check is.

en: to describe or report something in terms that make it seem greater, more important, more serious, or more certain than the facts justify
ja: 実際や根拠が示す以上に大きく、重要に、深刻に、または確かなものとして述べる、誇張して述べる

nuance.en: Overstate is often used to assess a claim, report, or argument against the evidence. It can describe an honest mistake as well as deliberate exaggeration. Cannot overstate turns the idea into emphasis: the speaker considers the point so important that even strong wording is justified.
nuance.ja: 主張や報告の言い方が、根拠に見合うかを評価するときによく使う。意図的な誇張にも、悪気のない過大な記述にも使える。cannot overstate は「いくら強調してもしすぎることはない」という強調表現。

en: exaggerate. Common in everyday speech and covers making a story or detail sound more dramatic. Overstate is especially natural with claims, figures, effects, or the strength of an argument.
overestimate. Means to form too high an estimate or judgment. Overstate focuses on what someone states or reports.
emphasize. Means to draw attention to a point. Overstate implies going beyond what the facts justify, except in the emphatic formula cannot overstate.
understate. Means to present something as smaller, less important, or less serious than it is.
ja: exaggerate は話や描写を大げさにする場合にも広く使える。overstate は主張・数値・影響・論拠の強さを実際以上に述べる場面になじむ。
overestimate は見積もりや判断を過大にすること。overstate は、それをどう述べたか、どう報告したかに焦点を当てる。
emphasize は注意を向けさせる、強調するという意味。overstate は根拠以上に大きく述べることを表し、cannot overstate の形では強調になる。
understate は、程度や重要性、深刻さを実際より控えめに述べること。

note.en: A broader equivalent for presenting something as greater than it is.
note.ja: 事実以上に大きく見せるという意味で広く使える。

note.en: Close when giving a factor or argument more weight than it deserves.
note.ja: 要因や論拠を必要以上に重く扱う場合に近い。

etymology.en: Formed from over- ‘too much’ and state ‘to express or declare’.
etymology.ja: over-（過度に）と state（述べる、明言する）からなる。

equivalents.es: exagerar / presentar como más importante de lo que es

en: overstate the impact
overstate the benefits
overstate the risk
overstate the case for a change
overstate what the evidence shows
be greatly overstated
cannot overstate the importance of something
ja: overstate the impact — 影響を実際以上に大きく述べる
overstate the benefits — 利点を誇張する
overstate the risk — リスクを実際以上に大きく述べる
overstate the case for a change — 変更を支持する論拠を実際以上に強く述べる
overstate what the evidence shows — 証拠から言えることを実際以上に述べる
be greatly overstated — 大幅に誇張されている
cannot overstate the importance of something — 何かの重要性はいくら強調してもしすぎることはない

en: The report overstates what can be concluded from such a small sample.
The presentation overstated the savings by leaving out maintenance costs.
I can't overstate how helpful your feedback was.
The importance of checking the figures before publication cannot be overstated.
ja: The report overstates what can be concluded from such a small sample. — その報告書は、これほど少数の標本から導ける結論を、実際よりも強く述べている。
The presentation overstated the savings by leaving out maintenance costs. — その発表は維持費を計算に入れず、削減額を実際より大きく示した。
I can't overstate how helpful your feedback was. — あなたのフィードバックがどれほど役に立ったか、いくら強調しても足りないくらいです。
The importance of checking the figures before publication cannot be overstated. — 公開前に数値を確認することの重要性は、いくら強調してもしすぎることはない。

patterns: understate + the extent / scale / severity of + something
to say that + clause + is to understate the case

usage.subject: The subject can be a person, a report, or the figures themselves: The figures understate the cost.
usage.wordFamily: Understatement is the noun. Understated can also be an adjective meaning restrained or subtle, as in understated elegance.

en: to describe or report something as smaller, less important, or less serious than it really is
ja: 実際より小さく、重要でない、または深刻でないものとして述べる。控えめに述べる、過小に示す

nuance.en: Understate focuses on how something is presented. A person might deliberately use mild language, or a report might give too low a figure because some costs were omitted. To say it was difficult is to understate the case suggests that difficult does not fully convey how hard it was.
nuance.ja: 焦点は、物事がどう述べられたり示されたりするか。意図的に穏やかな言葉を使う場合にも、一部の費用が漏れて報告書の数値が低く出る場合にも使える。To say it was difficult is to understate the case. は、「難しかった」では実際の大変さを言い表せない、という意味。

en: underestimate. Form too low an estimate or judgment. Understate concerns what a statement, report, or figure conveys.
downplay. Give something less attention or weight, often deliberately. Understate can also apply to figures that are too low because of incomplete data.
underreport. Report fewer cases or lower amounts than the actual total. Understate can also describe language that softens the seriousness of something.
overstate. Present something as greater, more important, or more serious than the facts justify.
ja: underestimate は見積もりや判断を過小にすること。understate は発言や報告、数値がどう伝えるかに焦点を当てる。
downplay は、意図的に注目や重要性を抑えるという響きが出やすい。understate は、データが不完全で数値が低く出る場合にも使える。
underreport は、件数や金額などを実際より少なく報告する場合に使う。understate は、深刻さを弱める言葉選びにも使える。
overstate は、実際より大きく、重要に、深刻に述べるという反対語。

note.en: Close when making a problem or concern seem less important.
note.ja: 問題や懸念を軽く見せる場合に近い。

note.en: Close when the reported number omits part of the actual total.
note.ja: 報告値が実際の総数の一部を取りこぼしている場合に近い。

etymology.en: Formed from under- ‘below the proper level’ and state ‘to express or declare’.
etymology.ja: under-（本来の水準より下に）と state（述べる、明言する）からなる。

equivalents.es: restar importancia / declarar por debajo del valor real

en: understate the severity of the problem
understate the true cost
understate the extent of the damage
grossly understate the risks
understate the case
understate how serious it was
ja: understate the severity of the problem — 問題の深刻さを実際より軽く述べる
understate the true cost — 実際の費用を過小に示す
understate the extent of the damage — 被害の規模を過小に示す
grossly understate the risks — リスクを実際より大幅に小さく伝える
understate the case — 実情を控えめに述べすぎる
understate how serious it was — 実際の深刻さを十分に伝えない

en: The estimate understates the true cost because it leaves out maintenance.
I underestimated the risk at first, and my report understated how serious it was.
To say that the negotiations were difficult is to understate the case.
Her calm account understated the impact the closure had on local businesses.
ja: The estimate understates the true cost because it leaves out maintenance. — その見積もりには維持費が入っていないため、実際の費用より低く出ている。
I underestimated the risk at first, and my report understated how serious it was. — 私は当初リスクを過小評価し、報告書でも実際の深刻さを十分に伝えなかった。
To say that the negotiations were difficult is to understate the case. — 交渉が難しかったと言うだけでは、実際の大変さは伝わらない。
Her calm account understated the impact the closure had on local businesses. — 彼女の落ち着いた説明からは、閉鎖が地元企業に与えた影響の大きさが十分には伝わらなかった。

patterns: surpass + someone or something + in + respect

usage.comparison: In introduces the respect in which something is better. By introduces the margin.
usage.reflexive: Surpass yourself means to do even better than you have done before or better than your usual high standard.

en: to be or do better than someone or something in quality, performance, or achievement
to go beyond a benchmark, previous level, or what people expected
ja: 質・成績・成果などで人や物を上回る、しのぐ
基準・従来の水準・期待などを超える

nuance.en: Surpass often highlights a result that has gone beyond an existing standard or achievement. It sounds somewhat formal and is natural with expectations, records, and comparisons between two things. For a required or permitted maximum, such as a speed limit, exceed is the usual choice.
nuance.ja: すでにある基準や成果を上回った点を際立たせる、やや改まった語。期待や記録を超える場合や、二つのものの質を比べる場合に自然。制限速度のように定められた上限を超える場合は、通常 exceed を使う。

en: exceed. Common for numerical limits and thresholds; exceed expectations also overlaps with surpass expectations.
outperform. Emphasizes better performance than a competitor or benchmark. Surpass also fits broader judgments of quality or achievement.
outdo. Often suggests competition or doing better than one's own past efforts. Surpass has a more formal tone.
overtake. Often describes moving ahead of someone in a race, ranking, or time series. Surpass can express superiority in quality even without a change of position.
ja: exceed は数値上の上限やしきい値を超えるときによく使う。exceed expectations は surpass expectations と意味が重なる。
outperform は競合や指標よりよい成績を出すことが焦点。surpass は、質や成果が上回るという幅広い評価にも使える。
outdo は競争相手や過去の自分よりうまくやるという響きがあり、surpass のほうが改まっている。
overtake は競走や順位の推移で「追い抜く」動きに焦点がある。surpass は、順位が入れ替わる場面以外でも、質が上回ることを表せる。

note.en: Close when going beyond expectations, a target, or a measurable level.
note.ja: 期待や目標、測定できる水準を上回る場合に近い。

note.en: Close when the comparison is about measurable performance.
note.ja: 測定できる成績や性能を比べる場合に近い。

etymology.en: Borrowed from French surpasser, from sur- ‘above’ and passer ‘to pass’.
etymology.ja: フランス語 surpasser に由来する。sur-（上に）と passer（通り過ぎる）からなる。

en: surpass all expectations
surpass the previous record
surpass a sales target
far surpass
surpass a rival in reliability
surpass the target by 10 percent
surpass oneself
ja: surpass all expectations — あらゆる期待を上回る
surpass the previous record — 従来の記録を上回る
surpass a sales target — 売上目標を上回る
far surpass — はるかにしのぐ
surpass a rival in reliability — 信頼性で競合を上回る
surpass the target by 10 percent — 目標を10％上回る
surpass oneself — 自分のこれまでの水準を上回る

en: Demand for the first production run surpassed our expectations.
The new model surpasses its predecessor in battery life.
The team surpassed its fundraising target by 10 percent.
With her latest novel, she's surpassed herself.
ja: Demand for the first production run surpassed our expectations. — 初回生産分への需要は、私たちの予想を上回った。
The new model surpasses its predecessor in battery life. — 新型モデルはバッテリーの持ちで旧型を上回る。
The team surpassed its fundraising target by 10 percent. — チームは資金調達の目標額を10％上回った。
With her latest novel, she's surpassed herself. — 最新作で、彼女はこれまでの自分を超えた。

usage.countability: Use some experimentation or a period of experimentation for the activity. Use an experiment or several experiments for individual tests.
usage.preposition: With introduces the method or material being tried. On can introduce the subject being experimented on.

en: the process of carrying out experiments to test an idea or find out how something works
the practice of trying new approaches, techniques, or materials to see what results they produce
ja: 仮説を検証したり仕組みを調べたりするために実験を行うこと、実験活動
新しい方法・技法・素材などを試して結果を見ること、実験的な試み、試行錯誤

nuance.en: Experimentation puts the focus on an activity or process. In science, that can mean carrying out controlled tests. In art, cooking, or design, it can mean exploring possibilities. It need not involve a failed attempt or even a fixed goal.
nuance.ja: 実験や試みを行う活動・過程に焦点がある。科学では条件をそろえた検証、芸術や料理、デザインでは新しい可能性を探る試みを指せる。「試行錯誤」と訳せる場面もあるが、失敗を繰り返したり、最初から目標が決まっていたりするとは限らない。

en: experiment. A countable noun for a particular test or trial. Experimentation describes the activity that one or more such trials form part of.
trial and error. Emphasizes making successive attempts and learning from mistakes or failures. Experimentation can emphasize testing or open-ended exploration.
testing. Often focuses on checking how something performs or whether it meets a requirement. Experimentation can also involve discovering new approaches.
ja: experiment は、個々の実験や試みを数えるときに使う。experimentation は、そうした試みを行う活動全体を指す。
trial and error は、何度か試し、うまくいかなかった点から学ぶ「試行錯誤」。experimentation は検証や、答えを決めずに可能性を探る活動にも使える。
testing は性能や要件への適合を確かめることに焦点が当たりやすい。experimentation には、新しい方法そのものを探る用法もある。

note.en: Close when the focus is on checking a hypothesis or method.
note.ja: 仮説や方法を検証する用法で近い。

note.en: Close when trying new techniques to discover what they can do.
note.ja: 新しい技法を試し、その可能性を探る場合に近い。

etymology.en: From the verb experiment and the noun-forming suffix -ation.
etymology.ja: 動詞 experiment（実験する、試す）に、活動や過程を表す名詞を作る接尾辞 -ation が付いた語。

en: scientific experimentation
further experimentation
experimentation with new materials
musical experimentation
encourage experimentation
allow room for experimentation
learn through experimentation
ja: scientific experimentation — 科学的な実験活動
further experimentation — さらなる実験
experimentation with new materials — 新しい素材を使った試み
musical experimentation — 音楽での実験的な試み
encourage experimentation — 新しい試みを奨励する
allow room for experimentation — 自由に試す余地を設ける
learn through experimentation — 実際に試しながら学ぶ

en: Further experimentation is needed to determine whether the effect is reproducible.
The studio encourages experimentation with different materials and textures.
After a little experimentation, I found a way to keep the pastry crisp.
The album grew out of years of experimentation with unusual instruments.
ja: Further experimentation is needed to determine whether the effect is reproducible. — その効果が再現できるかどうかを確かめるには、さらなる実験が必要だ。
The studio encourages experimentation with different materials and textures. — その工房では、さまざまな素材や質感を試すことを奨励している。
After a little experimentation, I found a way to keep the pastry crisp. — いろいろ試してみて、パイ生地をサクサクに保つ方法が見つかった。
The album grew out of years of experimentation with unusual instruments. — そのアルバムは、珍しい楽器を使った長年の試みから生まれた。

patterns: outperform + someone or something + on + metric / test
outperform + someone or something + in + area

usage.object: The direct object is the person, thing, or benchmark you compare against. In outperform the previous model on battery life, battery life is the criterion.
usage.margin: Use by to give the margin, as in outperform the index by two percentage points.

en: to achieve better results or work better than a person, competitor, product, or benchmark
in finance, to deliver a higher return than the market, an index, or a comparable investment
ja: 人・競合・製品・比較基準などを、成績や性能で上回る
金融で、市場や指数、比較対象の投資商品より高いリターンを上げる

nuance.en: Outperform focuses on results in a given task or over a given period. A device can outperform another on battery life and still lag behind it on speed. In finance, outperformance is relative. A fund can outperform its benchmark even when both lose value.
nuance.ja: ある課題や期間での成績・性能に焦点を当てる。電池持ちで別の機種を上回っていても、処理速度では劣ることがある。金融では相対的な成績を表すため、ファンドと比較指数の両方が下落しても、下落幅が小さいファンドは指数を outperform したと言える。

en: surpass. Covers a wider range of comparisons, including exceeding expectations or bettering an earlier achievement. Outperform is particularly natural when comparing results on a shared task or metric.
exceed. Common when the object is a limit, target, or numerical threshold. Outperform typically compares a performer or product with a rival or benchmark.
outdo. Often highlights getting the better of someone in a feat or competitive situation. Outperform is at home in comparisons based on tests or measured results.
beat. A common, flexible word for doing better than a rival or benchmark. Outperform puts the focus on comparative performance.
ja: surpass は期待を超える、過去の成果をしのぐなど、幅広い比較に使う。outperform は同じ課題や指標で成績・性能を比べる場合によく合う。
exceed は上限・目標値・しきい値などを超えるときによく使う。outperform は競合や比較指標を相手に成績を比べる場合に自然。
outdo は、ある行為や競争で相手をしのぐという響きが出やすい。outperform は試験や測定結果による比較になじむ。
beat は競合や基準を上回るという意味で幅広く使える日常語。outperform は成績・性能の比較に焦点を当てる。

note.en: A plain equivalent in general comparisons.
note.ja: 一般的な比較での平易な言い換え。

note.en: Close when one result or product is better than another.
note.ja: 成果や製品が別のものより優れている場合に近い。

etymology.en: Formed from out-, in the sense of doing better than another, and perform.
etymology.ja: out-（相手を上回る）と perform（実行する、成績を上げる）を組み合わせた語。

en: outperform the competition
outperform the previous model
outperform on battery life
outperform in benchmark tests
consistently outperform one's peers
outperform the market
outperform the index by two percentage points
ja: outperform the competition — 競合を成績や性能で上回る
outperform the previous model — 旧型モデルを性能で上回る
outperform on battery life — 電池持ちで上回る
outperform in benchmark tests — ベンチマークテストで上回る
consistently outperform one's peers — 同業他社や同じ集団の仲間を安定して上回る
outperform the market — 市場全体の成績を上回る
outperform the index by two percentage points — 指数の成績を2パーセントポイント上回る

en: In our tests, the new laptop outperformed its predecessor on battery life.
The smaller team outperformed its rivals in the final round.
The fund fell 3 percent, but it still outperformed its benchmark, which fell 5 percent.
ja: In our tests, the new laptop outperformed its predecessor on battery life. — 今回のテストでは、新型ノートPCは電池持ちで旧型を上回った。
The smaller team outperformed its rivals in the final round. — 決勝ラウンドでは、人数の少ないチームがライバルよりよい成績を収めた。
The fund fell 3 percent, but it still outperformed its benchmark, which fell 5 percent. — ファンドは3％下落したが、比較指数は5％下落したため、成績では指数を上回った。

patterns: the handover of + responsibility / power / keys
the handover from + outgoing person + to + incoming person

usage.spelling: Use one word for the noun, a handover, and two for the phrasal verb, hand over. With a pronoun, put it between the verb and particle: hand it over.
usage.perspective: Hand over focuses on the person giving up control or passing something on. Take over focuses on the person receiving responsibility.

en: the transfer of responsibility, control, or power to another person or group
the planned transfer of an object or person to someone else
the period or meeting during which duties and relevant information are passed on
ja: 責任・業務・権限を別の人や組織に引き継ぐこと、移譲
物や人を別の相手に引き渡すこと
業務や必要な情報を引き継ぐ期間や打ち合わせ

nuance.en: In the workplace, a handover can mean the process of passing on duties, current work, and information to a successor or the next shift. In a property context, it can mean the formal delivery of keys or possession. A handover of power focuses on the transfer from one authority to another.
nuance.ja: 職場では、後任者や次のシフトの担当者に、仕事・進捗・必要な情報を伝える引き継ぎを指す。物件の文脈では鍵や物件の引き渡し、政治では政府や当局から別の主体への権限の移譲を表す。

en: hand over. The two-word verb: They handed over the keys. Handover names the event or process.
handoff. A close alternative for passing work or information between people or teams, especially in American workplace usage.
transfer. A broad word for moving something between people, places, or systems. Handover often highlights a change of responsibility or a formal delivery.
transition. The wider period of change. A handover is the transfer of duties, control, or possession during that change.
ja: hand over は二語で書く動詞。They handed over the keys. は「鍵を引き渡した」。handover はその行為や過程を指す名詞。
handoff は、特に米国の職場などで、担当者やチーム間で仕事や情報を渡す場合に近い。
transfer は人・場所・システムの間で移すことを広く表す。handover は担当の交代や正式な引き渡しを意識させやすい。
transition は変化や移行の過程全体。handover はそのなかで責任・権限・物などを渡すことに焦点がある。

note.en: Broad equivalent when responsibility, control, or possession changes hands.
note.ja: 責任・権限・占有などが移る場合の広い言い換え。

note.en: Close for transfers of work or information between people or teams.
note.ja: 人やチームの間で仕事や情報を引き継ぐ場合に近い。

etymology.en: Formed from the phrasal verb hand over, ‘to pass something to another person’.
etymology.ja: 句動詞 hand over（相手に渡す、引き渡す）を一語にした名詞。

equivalents.it: il passaggio di consegne / la consegna

en: a smooth handover
an orderly handover of power
the handover of the keys
handover notes
a handover meeting
a shift handover
a two-week handover period
ja: a smooth handover — 円滑な引き継ぎ
an orderly handover of power — 秩序立った権限移譲
the handover of the keys — 鍵の引き渡し
handover notes — 引き継ぎメモ
a handover meeting — 引き継ぎの打ち合わせ
a shift handover — 勤務交代時の申し送り
a two-week handover period — 2週間の引き継ぎ期間

en: Before going on leave, I wrote handover notes for the colleague covering my cases.
The outgoing manager scheduled a meeting to ensure a smooth handover.
The keys will be handed over on Friday, and both parties will sign a form at the handover.
The election was followed by an orderly handover of power to the new government.
ja: Before going on leave, I wrote handover notes for the colleague covering my cases. — 休暇に入る前に、担当案件を引き受けてくれる同僚向けに引き継ぎメモを書いた。
The outgoing manager scheduled a meeting to ensure a smooth handover. — 退任するマネージャーは、円滑に引き継げるよう打ち合わせを設定した。
The keys will be handed over on Friday, and both parties will sign a form at the handover. — 鍵は金曜日に引き渡され、その際に双方が書類に署名する。
The election was followed by an orderly handover of power to the new government. — 選挙後、新政府への権限移譲は混乱なく行われた。

patterns: the identifiability of + person / parameter / model

usage.counting: Use identifiability for the property and an identifiability problem for one instance of difficulty. Identifiable is the adjective: the parameters are identifiable from the distribution of the observations.

en: the extent to which a person or thing can be identified from available information
in statistics, the property that a parameter or quantity is uniquely determined by the probability distribution of the observable data under the model
ja: 手掛かりとなる情報から人や物を識別・特定できること、その程度
統計学で、モデルのもとで観測データの確率分布からパラメータや対象の量が一意に定まる性質。識別可能性、同定可能性

nuance.en: In privacy discussions, identifiability is about whether available clues can reveal who a record concerns. In statistics, it asks whether the observable distribution fixes the parameter in principle. If a model depends on two parameters only through their sum, the two values cannot be identified separately from that distribution, even if the sum can be identified.
nuance.ja: プライバシーの文脈では、利用できる手掛かりから記録が誰のものかを特定できるかが焦点。統計では、観測値の分布がパラメータを原理的に一意に決めるかが焦点。たとえば、分布が二つのパラメータの和だけで決まるモデルでは、和を識別できても、個々の値を分けて識別することはできない。

en: identification. The act or result of identifying someone or something. Identifiability is the property that makes identification possible.

estimability. Concerns whether a quantity can be estimated under a model and, in some contexts, under a specified statistical criterion. Identifiability specifically asks whether the observable distribution uniquely determines the quantity.
distinctiveness. The quality of standing out or being distinguishable, also used of trademarks. Identifiability focuses on whether available information lets you establish what or who something is.
ja: identification は人や物を特定する行為やその結果。identifiability は特定できるという性質。
estimability は、モデルのもとで、場合によっては所定の統計的な基準を満たす形で推定できるかを表す。identifiability は、観測値の分布が対象の量を一意に決めるかに焦点がある。
distinctiveness は、際立っていることや他と区別できる性質を指し、商標の識別力にも使われる。identifiability は、手元の情報から対象が何か、あるいは誰かを特定できるかに焦点がある。

note.en: A plain paraphrase in general contexts.
note.ja: 一般的な文脈での平易な言い換え。

etymology.en: Formed from identifiable and the noun-forming suffix -ity, giving the ending -ability.
etymology.ja: identifiable（識別・特定できる）に名詞を作る接尾辞 -ity が加わり、語尾が -ability になった形。

en: the identifiability of individuals
assess identifiability
parameter identifiability
establish identifiability
an identifiability problem
lack of identifiability
ja: the identifiability of individuals — 個人の特定可能性
assess identifiability — 識別可能性を評価する
parameter identifiability — パラメータの識別可能性
establish identifiability — 識別可能性を示す
an identifiability problem — 識別可能性に関わる問題
lack of identifiability — 一意に識別できないこと

en: The study examined the identifiability of individuals from combinations of demographic details.
If two distinct parameter values produce the same distribution of observations, global identifiability fails.
Even if we know the sum exactly, that does not resolve the identifiability problem for the two parameters separately.
ja: The study examined the identifiability of individuals from combinations of demographic details. — その研究は、人口統計上の属性を組み合わせることで個人を特定できるかを調べた。
If two distinct parameter values produce the same distribution of observations, global identifiability fails. — 異なる二つのパラメータ値から同じ観測値の分布が生じるなら、大域的な識別可能性は成り立たない。
Even if we know the sum exactly, that does not resolve the identifiability problem for the two parameters separately. — 和が正確に分かっても、二つのパラメータを個別に識別できるわけではない。

grammar.countability: usually uncountable; countable for a specific finding, as in a positive identification
patterns: identify + someone or something + by + feature

usage.prepositions: Of names what is identified. With names a person, group, or character whose feelings, experiences, or values someone relates to.
usage.article: For a document, use some identification, a form of identification, or an ID. Use a positive identification for a specific finding made with confidence.

en: the process or result of determining who someone is or what something is
a document or other proof of a person's identity
a sense of connection with a person, character, or group, often through shared feelings, experiences, or values
ja: 人や物が誰・何であるかを突き止めること、識別・特定・同定
本人であることを示す書類など、身分証明・身分証明書
人・登場人物・集団に自分を重ねること、同一視・感情移入・一体感

nuance.en: Identification of a species means determining which species it is. Identification with a character means relating to the character or seeing part of yourself in them. At a counter or entrance, show identification usually means to present a document proving who you are.
nuance.ja: identification of a species は種が何かを特定すること。identification with a character は登場人物に自分を重ねたり、感情移入したりすることを表す。窓口や入り口で show identification と言われたら、通常は身分証明書を提示すること。

en: identifiability. Whether the available information makes identification possible. Identification is the process or result of establishing who or what something is.
identity. Who a person is, or the characteristics that define a person or group. Identification can be the act of establishing that identity or the document used as proof.
recognition. Often means noticing that someone or something is familiar. Identification can involve establishing an exact name or category, even for something unfamiliar.
verification. Checks whether a claim, detail, or stated identity is correct. Identification focuses on establishing who or what the subject is.
ja: identifiability は手元の情報から特定できるかという性質。identification は実際に誰・何であるかを特定することや、その結果を指す。
identity はその人が誰かということや、人・集団を特徴づけるもの。identification は本人であることを確かめる行為や、その証明書を指せる。
recognition は、見覚えがある人や物に気づく場合によく使う。identification は見慣れない対象でも、具体的な名前や分類を突き止めることを指せる。
verification は申告や情報が正しいかを確認すること。identification は対象が誰・何であるかを特定することが焦点。

note.en: Common in everyday speech for a document or card proving identity.
note.ja: 身分証明書を指す日常的な略語。

note.en: Close in some contexts involving recognizing a person, object, or feature.
note.ja: 人や物、特徴を見分ける文脈で意味が重なる場合がある。

etymology.en: Belongs to the same word family as identify and identifiable and ends in the noun-forming suffix -ification.
etymology.ja: identify（特定する）、identifiable（特定できる）と同じ語族。語尾の -ification は行為や過程などを表す名詞を作る。

equivalents.de: die Identifizierung / der Ausweis / die Identifikation mit
equivalents.it: l’identificazione / il documento d’identità / l’identificazione con
equivalents.fr: l’identification / la pièce d’identité / l’identification à
equivalents.es: la identificación / el documento de identidad / la identificación con

en: the identification of a species
early identification of a problem
make a positive identification
show identification
photo identification
a form of identification
an identification number
identification with a character
ja: the identification of a species — 種の同定
early identification of a problem — 問題の早期発見
make a positive identification — 対象を確実に特定する
show identification — 身分証明書を提示する
photo identification — 顔写真付きの身分証明書
a form of identification — 身分を証明できるもの
an identification number — 識別番号
identification with a character — 登場人物への感情移入

en: The identification of the bird species was based on its distinctive call.
Please bring a form of photo identification when you collect your visitor badge.
The witness was unable to make a positive identification from the photographs.
Her identification with the main character grew as she read the novel.
ja: The identification of the bird species was based on its distinctive call. — その鳥の種は、特徴的な鳴き声を手掛かりに同定された。
Please bring a form of photo identification when you collect your visitor badge. — 来訪者用の入館証を受け取る際は、顔写真付きの身分証明書をお持ちください。
The witness was unable to make a positive identification from the photographs. — 目撃者は写真から人物を確実には特定できなかった。
Her identification with the main character grew as she read the novel. — 小説を読み進めるにつれ、彼女は主人公にますます自分を重ねるようになった。

grammar.transitivity: mainly transitive; also intransitive in identify with / as
patterns: identify + someone or something + by + clue

usage.as: Identify A as B states who or what A is taken to be. In identify as B with no object, the subject describes their own identity.
usage.with: Identify with someone means to relate to them, often through a shared feeling or experience.

en: to establish or recognize who someone is or what something is
to find and specify a cause, need, risk, or other point of interest
to give one's name or role, or describe one's own identity
in identify with, to relate to or feel a connection with someone
ja: 人や物が誰・何であるかを特定する、見分ける、同定する
原因・必要なこと・リスクなどを見つけて明らかにする、洗い出す
名乗る、身分や立場を明かす、自らを～と認識する
identify with の形で、人に共感する、自分を重ねる

nuance.en: Identify often answers who or what exactly. You can identify a caller by their voice or identify a problem by reading the available evidence. In reports and meetings, identify risks often means to work out what the risks are and name them. Identify oneself concerns giving one's name or role, while identify as often concerns self-description.
nuance.ja: identify は「具体的に誰か・何か」を明らかにする語。声で電話の相手を特定したり、資料を読んで問題を突き止めたりできる。報告書や会議では identify risks が「どんなリスクがあるかを把握し、具体的に挙げる」という意味になる。identify oneself は名や立場を明かすこと、目的語のない identify as は自分のアイデンティティーを述べることが多い。

en: recognize. Often means realizing that someone or something is familiar. Identify can involve determining exactly what an unfamiliar object is.
detect. Often means noticing the presence of something, such as a leak. Identify can go further by establishing the type, source, or cause.
verify. Means checking that something already stated is correct. Identify focuses on establishing who or what it is.
pinpoint. Emphasizes locating or determining something with great precision. Identify is broader and can involve several possible problems or risks.
ja: recognize は見覚えや聞き覚えのあるものだと気づくときにも使う。identify は、初めて見る物が具体的に何かを特定する場合にも使う。
detect は漏れなどの存在に気づくことが焦点。identify は種類・発生源・原因まで特定する場合にも使う。
verify は、すでに示されている情報が正しいかを確認すること。identify は、対象が誰・何かを突き止めることが焦点。
pinpoint は位置や原因などをピンポイントで突き止める正確さを強調する。identify は複数の問題やリスクを洗い出す場合にも自然。

note.en: Close for finding out what the cause, nature, or identity of something is.
note.ja: 原因や性質、正体を突き止める場合に近い。

note.en: Close when identifying someone or something familiar.
note.ja: 見覚えや聞き覚えのある人・物を見分ける場合に近い。

etymology.en: Borrowed from French identifier, related to identité ‘identity’. An early English sense was ‘regard as the same’.
etymology.ja: フランス語 identifier に由来し、identité（同一性）と関係する。初期の英語では「同じものとみなす」という意味があった。

equivalents.de: identifizieren / feststellen / sich mit jemandem identifizieren

en: identify the root cause
identify potential risks
identify areas for improvement
identify someone by their voice
identify a bird as a heron
identify oneself as a member of staff
identify with the main character
identify as bilingual
ja: identify the root cause — 根本原因を突き止める
identify potential risks — 潜在的なリスクを洗い出す
identify areas for improvement — 改善点を見つける
identify someone by their voice — 声で人を特定する
identify a bird as a heron — 鳥をサギだと同定する
identify oneself as a member of staff — 職員だと名乗る
identify with the main character — 主人公に感情移入する
identify as bilingual — 自分はバイリンガルだと認識している

en: We detected a leak but couldn't identify its source.
The curator identified the sketch as an early work by the artist.
Before we revise the agreement, we need to identify which provisions are causing confusion.
The caller identified herself as a member of the support team.
I identified with the main character because I'd faced a similar choice myself.
ja: We detected a leak but couldn't identify its source. — 漏れがあることには気づいたが、どこから漏れているかは特定できなかった。
The curator identified the sketch as an early work by the artist. — 学芸員は、その素描をその画家の初期作品と特定した。
Before we revise the agreement, we need to identify which provisions are causing confusion. — 契約書を修正する前に、どの条項が混乱を招いているかを特定する必要がある。
The caller identified herself as a member of the support team. — 電話の相手は、サポートチームの一員だと名乗った。
I identified with the main character because I'd faced a similar choice myself. — 自分も似たような選択を迫られたことがあったので、主人公に感情移入した。

usage.document: Identity means who someone is. For a document proving it, use ID, identification, or an identity document.
usage.number: Use identities for distinct personas, different forms of group or personal identity, or more than one mathematical identity.

en: who a person is, especially as established by their name or other identifying information
a person's or group's sense of who they are, or the qualities that make a person, group, or organization distinctive
the state of being the same (formal or philosophical)
in mathematics, an equality that holds for all allowed values of its variables
ja: ある人が誰であるか、身元・素性
自分や集団が何者かという認識、または人・集団・組織を特徴づける性質、アイデンティティー
同じものであること、同一性（改まった用法・哲学）
数学で、変数に許されるすべての値について成り立つ等式、恒等式

nuance.en: The identity of the caller asks who called. A sense of identity is how a person or group understands who they are. A brand's visual identity is the recognizable system of design choices, such as its colors and typography. In philosophy, identity can concern whether two references pick out one and the same thing.
nuance.ja: the identity of the caller は電話の相手が誰かを指す。a sense of identity は、人や集団が自分たちをどう捉えるかを表す。ブランドの visual identity は、配色や書体など、そのブランドだと分かる視覚表現全体を指す。哲学では、二つの呼び方が同じ一つの対象を指しているか、という同一性の議論にも使う。

en: identification. The act of determining who or what something is, or a document used as proof. Identity is what is being established or proved.
identifiability. Whether someone or something can be identified from the available information. Identity concerns who or what they are.
personality. A person's characteristic traits and ways of behaving. Identity also includes how they define themselves and where they feel they belong.
similarity. The quality of being alike in certain respects. In the strict sense of sameness, identity means being one and the same.
ja: identification は誰・何であるかを特定する行為や、身元を証明する書類。identity は、そこで特定・証明する身元や同一性を指す。
identifiability は、手元の情報から特定できるかどうか。identity は、対象が誰・何であるかに関わる。
personality は性格や振る舞いの傾向。identity は自分をどう位置づけ、どこに帰属すると感じるかも含む。
similarity は、ある点で似ていること。厳密な意味での identity は、同じ一つのものであること。

note.en: Close in the personal, psychological sense.
note.ja: 個人の自己認識を指す心理的な用法で近い。

note.en: Close in the strict sense of being the same.
note.ja: 同一性という厳密な用法で近い。

etymology.en: From French identité and Medieval Latin identitas ‘sameness’, ultimately from Latin idem ‘the same’.
etymology.ja: フランス語 identité と中世ラテン語 identitas（同一性）に由来し、ラテン語 idem（同じもの）にさかのぼる。

en: verify someone's identity
reveal the identity of a source
a case of mistaken identity
identity theft
a sense of identity
cultural identity
a brand's visual identity
a mathematical identity
ja: verify someone's identity — 本人であることを確認する
reveal the identity of a source — 情報源が誰かを明かす
a case of mistaken identity — 人違いのケース
identity theft — 個人情報を使ったなりすまし
a sense of identity — 自分が何者かという感覚
cultural identity — 文化的アイデンティティー
a brand's visual identity — ブランドの視覚的なアイデンティティー
a mathematical identity — 数学の恒等式

en: The journalist refused to reveal the identity of her source.
The festival is an important part of the town's cultural identity.
The company kept its familiar colors when it updated its visual identity.
The equation 2(x + 1) = 2x + 2 is an identity because it holds for every real number x.
ja: The journalist refused to reveal the identity of her source. — その記者は、情報提供者が誰かを明かすことを拒んだ。
The festival is an important part of the town's cultural identity. — その祭りは、町の文化を特徴づける大切な要素だ。
The company kept its familiar colors when it updated its visual identity. — その会社は視覚的なブランド表現を刷新する際、なじみのある配色を残した。
The equation 2(x + 1) = 2x + 2 is an identity because it holds for every real number x. — 等式 2(x + 1) = 2x + 2 は、実数 x のどの値についても成り立つので恒等式だ。

patterns: questions / concerns + in relation to + subject
evaluate + A + in relation to + B
where + A + is + in relation to + B

usage.complement: To is a preposition here. Common complements include a noun phrase or pronoun, as in in relation to the cost or in relation to it.
usage.register: About is a simpler option when introducing a topic. In relation to is useful when the relationship, comparison, or point of reference matters.

en: concerning or in connection with a particular subject
considered or measured against something else as a reference point
located or oriented with respect to another thing or place
ja: ～に関して、～に関連して
～と比べて、～を基準にして
～に対して、～との位置関係で

nuance.en: In relation to can introduce the topic of a question or concern. In comparisons, it makes the following noun the benchmark or context for interpreting something. In spatial descriptions, it locates one object by reference to another.
nuance.ja: 質問や懸念の対象を示すほか、比較では後ろに来る名詞が評価や測定の基準になる。位置を述べるときは、ある物の場所や向きを別の物を基準にして示す。

en: about. A common, direct way to introduce a topic. In relation to can sound more formal and can point to a specific connection.
with regard to. Introduces what a statement or request concerns. In relation to also works for comparisons and relative position.
relative to. Especially apt for measurements, proportions, or positions. It overlaps with the reference-point senses of in relation to.
in connection with. Often stresses a link between an event, issue, or activity and something else. In relation to can also set a benchmark for comparison.
ja: about は話題を示す一般的で簡潔な前置詞。in relation to はより改まった響きがあり、具体的な関連を示す場合にも使える。
with regard to は発言や依頼が何に関するかを示す。in relation to には比較や位置関係を示す用法もある。
relative to は測定、比率、位置を述べるのに特に適しており、基準を示す in relation to と意味が重なる。
in connection with は出来事や問題、活動と別の事柄との関連を示すことが多い。in relation to は比較の基準も設定できる。

note.en: Close when introducing the topic under discussion.
note.ja: 話題や検討対象を示す用法で近い。

note.en: Close when specifying what something is compared with or located against.
note.ja: 比較対象や位置の基準を示す用法で近い。

etymology.en: Built from the noun relation in the construction in relation to. The noun contributes the idea of a connection or reference point.
etymology.ja: 名詞 relation（関係）を含む定型表現。何かとのつながりや、何かを基準にした関係を表す。

equivalents.de: in Bezug auf / im Verhältnis zu
equivalents.fr: en ce qui concerne / par rapport à
equivalents.es: en relación con / con respecto a

en: questions in relation to the agreement
concerns raised in relation to the proposal
high in relation to income
small in relation to the overall budget
assess the price in relation to the quality
the position of A in relation to B
ja: questions in relation to the agreement — 契約に関する質問
concerns raised in relation to the proposal — 提案に関して示された懸念
high in relation to income — 所得に比べて高い
small in relation to the overall budget — 予算全体に比べて小さい
assess the price in relation to the quality — 品質を基準に価格を評価する
the position of A in relation to B — Bを基準にしたAの位置

en: The client raised two questions in relation to the draft agreement.
The fee is modest in relation to the amount of work involved.
The map shows where the hotel is in relation to the station.
The diagram shows the position of the sensor in relation to the door frame.
ja: The client raised two questions in relation to the draft agreement. — 依頼人は契約書案について二つ質問した。
The fee is modest in relation to the amount of work involved. — その料金は、必要な作業量に比べて控えめだ。
The map shows where the hotel is in relation to the station. — 地図を見ると、駅を基準にホテルがどこにあるか分かる。
The diagram shows the position of the sensor in relation to the door frame. — 図は、ドア枠を基準にしたセンサーの位置を示している。

patterns: the position of + A + relative to + B

usage.reference: The noun after to provides the reference point. In small relative to the original, the original is what the size is compared with.
usage.dependence: When used after be, the phrase can also mean that a value depends on another factor. The phrase alone does not imply a constant ratio.

en: in comparison with, or measured or judged against, a reference point
with respect to a reference point for location or movement
depending on or varying with a factor, especially after be
concerning or in connection with a subject, in some formal contexts
ja: ～と比べて、～を基準に評価・測定して
～を基準とした位置や動きについて、～に対して
～に応じて決まる・変わる。特に be relative to の形
～に関して、～に関連して（一部の改まった文脈）

nuance.en: Relative to often tells you what a number, judgment, or position is measured against. A cost can be high relative to income, and a moving point can be described relative to a fixed edge. In a statement such as Fees are relative to project size, the phrase means that fees vary with size. It can also introduce a topic in formal writing.
nuance.ja: 数値・評価・位置を何に照らして見るかを示すときによく使う。費用を所得と比べたり、動く点の位置を固定された端から測ったりする場面になじむ。Fees are relative to project size. なら「料金は案件の規模に応じて変わる」。改まった文章で話題を示す用法もある。

en: in relation to. Also sets a reference point for comparison or position and commonly introduces a subject. Relative to is especially useful for compact statements of how something is measured or judged.
compared with. Directly signals a comparison. Relative to can also establish a spatial reference point or express dependence.
in proportion to. Often suggests that the quantities change in corresponding proportions. Relative to can simply express comparison or dependence.
with regard to. Introduces what a statement concerns. For a comparison or spatial reference, relative to is the natural choice.
ja: in relation to は比較・位置の基準にも、話題を示す「～に関して」にも使う。relative to は、何を基準に測ったり評価したりするかを簡潔に示すのに向く。
compared with は比較していることを明示する。relative to は位置の基準や、ある値が別の要因に応じて変わることも示せる。
in proportion to は、量が対応する割合で変わるという含みが強い。relative to は比較や依存関係を示すだけの場合もある。
with regard to は発言や文章の話題を示す。比較や位置の基準を示す場合は relative to が自然。

note.en: Close when setting a reference point for a comparison or position.
note.ja: 比較や位置の基準を示す場合に近い。

note.en: Close when the point is a direct comparison.
note.ja: 直接比較する用法で近い。

etymology.en: Built from the adjective relative, which is related to the noun relation, and the preposition to.
etymology.ja: 名詞 relation（関係）と同じ語族の形容詞 relative に、前置詞 to が続く表現。

equivalents.fr: par rapport à / en fonction de
equivalents.es: con respecto a / en relación con

en: high relative to income
low relative to last year's figures
large relative to its weight
relative to the baseline
measure position relative to a fixed point
move relative to the frame
ja: high relative to income — 所得に比べて高い
low relative to last year's figures — 昨年の数値より低い
large relative to its weight — 重さのわりに大きい
relative to the baseline — 基準値に対して
measure position relative to a fixed point — 固定点を基準に位置を測る
move relative to the frame — 枠を基準に移動する

en: Rent is high relative to local wages.
The new model is light relative to its size.
The drawing shows the position of each screw relative to the edge of the panel.
The delivery fee is relative to the size of the order.
ja: Rent is high relative to local wages. — 家賃は地元の賃金水準に比べて高い。
The new model is light relative to its size. — 新型モデルは大きさのわりに軽い。
The drawing shows the position of each screw relative to the edge of the panel. — 図面はパネルの端を基準に、各ネジの位置を示している。
The delivery fee is relative to the size of the order. — 配送料は注文の規模に応じて変わる。

grammar.countability: countable / uncountable, depending on sense; plural for dealings between parties
patterns: the relation between + A + and + B
bear + little / no relation to + something

usage.number: Use relation or relationship for a connection between things. Use relations with a plural verb when describing dealings between countries, groups, or people: Relations between the two countries have improved.
usage.family: A relation of mine means a member of my family. A relative of mine is another common way to say this.

en: a connection, correspondence, or way in which two things are linked
in the plural, the way that people, groups, or countries deal with each other
a member of one's family, especially in British English
in mathematics, a specified association between elements, such as ‘less than’ between numbers
ja: 物事のつながり、対応関係、関連
複数形で、人・集団・国家の間の関係や付き合い方
親族、親戚。特にイギリス英語でよく使う
数学の関係。例えば、数における「より小さい」という関係

nuance.en: The relation between A and B often appears in analytical or technical descriptions. Relationship also works there and is the ordinary choice for a personal bond. Plural relations is common in diplomatic or workplace contexts, as in diplomatic relations and labor relations. Bear no relation to means that two things have no relevant connection or resemblance.
nuance.ja: the relation between A and B は、二つの事柄のつながりを分析的に述べるときによく使う。relationship も同じ場面で使え、人同士の個人的な関係には relationship が一般的。複数形の relations は diplomatic relations（外交関係）や labor relations（労使関係）などに使う。bear no relation to は、関係がない、または似てもいないという意味。

en: relationship. Often interchangeable for a link between two things. It is also the usual word for a personal or romantic bond.
connection. An everyday word for a link. Relation is natural when describing how two factors correspond or are linked.
relative. The ordinary countable noun for a family member. Relation has the same family sense, as in a distant relation.
correlation. In statistics, describes a specific kind of association. Relation is a broader term and can describe a logical, functional, or other link.
ja: relationship は二つの物事の関連について relation と入れ替えられることが多い。個人的な付き合いや恋愛関係を指すときにもよく使う。
connection はつながりを表す一般的な語。relation は、二つの要因がどう対応し、結びつくかを述べるのに向く。
relative は親族を指す一般的な可算名詞。relation にも同じ用法があり、a distant relation は「遠い親戚」。
correlation は統計で特定の種類の関連を表す。relation はより広く、論理的・関数的なつながりなども指す。

note.en: Close when discussing a link between two things.
note.ja: 二つの事柄のつながりを指す場合に近い。

note.en: Equivalent in the family sense.
note.ja: 親族・親戚を指す用法で同義。

etymology.en: From Anglo-French relacioun and Latin relatio, from relatus, a form of referre ‘to bring back or report’.
etymology.ja: アングロフランス語 relacioun とラテン語 relatio に由来する。relatio は referre（持ち帰る、報告する）の形の一つである relatus にさかのぼる。

equivalents.de: die Beziehung / der Zusammenhang / der oder die Verwandte
equivalents.it: la relazione / il rapporto / il parente
equivalents.fr: la relation / le rapport / un membre de la famille
equivalents.es: la relación / el vínculo / el pariente

en: the relation between two variables
bear little relation to reality
have no relation to the issue
diplomatic relations
maintain good relations with neighbors
a distant relation
a relation by marriage
in relation to the budget
ja: the relation between two variables — 二つの変数の関係
bear little relation to reality — 現実とほとんど関係がない
have no relation to the issue — その問題とは関係がない
diplomatic relations — 外交関係
maintain good relations with neighbors — 近隣と良好な関係を保つ
a distant relation — 遠い親戚
a relation by marriage — 婚姻による親族
in relation to the budget — 予算に関して、または予算と比べて

en: The report examines the relation between housing costs and commuting distance.
The estimate bears little relation to what we actually spent.
Relations between the two countries improved after the talks.
I stayed with a distant relation when I first moved to London.
‘Less than’ is a relation between numbers.
ja: The report examines the relation between housing costs and commuting distance. — その報告書は、住居費と通勤距離の関係を検討している。
The estimate bears little relation to what we actually spent. — その見積もりは、私たちが実際に使った金額とは大きくかけ離れている。
Relations between the two countries improved after the talks. — 協議のあと、両国の関係は改善した。
I stayed with a distant relation when I first moved to London. — ロンドンに引っ越したばかりの頃は、遠い親戚の家に泊めてもらった。
‘Less than’ is a relation between numbers. — 「より小さい」は数と数の間の関係だ。

patterns: have / build / maintain a relationship with + person / organization
the relationship between + A + and + B

usage.prepositions: With introduces the other party in have a good relationship with someone. Between names both sides in the relationship between A and B.
usage.article: Use a relationship for one particular bond or connection. On its own, be in a relationship usually means to have a romantic partner.

en: the way two people, groups, or organizations interact or feel about each other
a romantic or intimate connection between people
a connection between two or more things, factors, or events
the family connection between people
ja: 人・集団・組織の間の関係、付き合い方
恋愛関係、交際
物事・要因・出来事の間のつながり、関連
家族・親族としての続柄

nuance.en: Relationship can describe ties between family members, colleagues, or organizations. Be in a relationship usually has a romantic meaning, while have a good relationship with someone leaves the type of connection to context. In analytical writing, a relationship between two factors can be an association whose cause is still unknown.
nuance.ja: 家族や同僚、組織の間の関係を広く表せる。be in a relationship だけで使うと、ふつう「交際相手がいる」という意味。have a good relationship with someone では、相手との関係の種類は文脈で決まる。分析の文脈では、二つの要因の間に関連があって、その原因がまだ分かっていない場合にも使える。

en: relation. Often overlaps with relationship when describing a connection between things. Relationship is the ordinary choice for an ongoing personal bond.
relations. Common for diplomatic or institutional dealings, as in diplomatic relations. A working relationship describes how particular parties work together.
connection. Broadly names any link. Relationship can describe the way the parties interact or how two variables change together.
correlation. In statistics, refers to a specific kind of association. Relationship covers a wider range of links, including causal or nonlinear ones.
ja: relation は、物事の関連について relationship と意味が重なることが多い。継続する個人的な付き合いには relationship が一般的。
relations は、diplomatic relations のような外交・組織間の関係によく使う。a working relationship は特定の相手との仕事上の関係を指す。
connection はつながり全般を指す。relationship は、双方の関わり方や、二つの変数がどのように変化するかも表せる。
correlation は統計で特定の種類の関連を指す。relationship の範囲は広く、因果関係や非線形の関係にも使える。

note.en: Close for an emotional connection between people.
note.ja: 人同士の情緒的なつながりを指す場合に近い。

note.en: Close for a link between things or factors.
note.ja: 物事や要因の関連を指す場合に近い。

etymology.en: Formed from relation and -ship, a suffix used for a state, quality, or connection, as in friendship.
etymology.ja: relation（関係）に、状態や関係を表す接尾辞 -ship が付いた語。friendship にも同じ接尾辞が使われている。

equivalents.de: die Beziehung / das Verhältnis / der Zusammenhang
equivalents.it: la relazione / il rapporto / il legame
equivalents.fr: la relation / le lien / le rapport

en: a close relationship with a sibling
a good working relationship
build a relationship with a client
be in a long-term relationship
end a relationship
the relationship between price and demand
a causal relationship
a family relationship
ja: a close relationship with a sibling — きょうだいとの親密な関係
a good working relationship — 良好な仕事上の関係
build a relationship with a client — 依頼人との関係を築く
be in a long-term relationship — 長く交際している
end a relationship — 交際を終える
the relationship between price and demand — 価格と需要の関係
a causal relationship — 因果関係
a family relationship — 家族・親族としての関係

en: We built a good working relationship with the local attorneys over the course of the project.
She's been in a relationship with Alex for three years.
The study found a relationship between commuting time and job satisfaction, but it didn’t establish that one caused the other.
The form asks you to state your relationship to the applicant.
ja: We built a good working relationship with the local attorneys over the course of the project. — その案件を進めるなかで、現地代理人と良好な仕事上の関係を築いた。
She's been in a relationship with Alex for three years. — 彼女はアレックスと3年間交際している。
The study found a relationship between commuting time and job satisfaction, but it didn’t establish that one caused the other. — その研究では通勤時間と仕事の満足度に関連が見られたが、一方が他方の原因だと確認されたわけではなかった。
The form asks you to state your relationship to the applicant. — その書類には、申請者との続柄を記入する欄がある。

patterns: decide / assess / handle + object + case by case

usage.hyphenation: Hyphenate the adjective before a noun, as in a case-by-case review. The adverbial phrase can be written without hyphens, as in We assess requests case by case.
usage.article: The fixed expression includes a: on a case-by-case basis.

en: decided or handled separately according to the circumstances of each case
individually, with the facts of each case taken into account (case by case)
ja: 案件ごとの事情に応じて個別に判断・対応する、案件ごとの
一件ずつ、その事情を考慮して個別に（case by case）

nuance.en: A case-by-case approach gives the decision maker room to take individual circumstances into account. A common set of criteria can still apply to every case. The expression is often used for exceptions, requests, and reviews.
nuance.ja: 一律に結論を出す場面より、個々の事情を見て判断するときに使う。全案件に共通の基準を使いながら、事実に照らして一件ずつ結論を出す場合にも自然。例外を認めるか、申請を承認するかといった場面によく合う。

en: individually. Means separately. Case by case emphasizes taking the circumstances of each case into account.
one by one. Focuses on sequence or handling items singly. Case by case puts the focus on how each decision is made.
at one's discretion. Says who has the authority to decide. On a case-by-case basis says how the decisions are made.
ja: individually は個別に、別々にという意味。case by case は一件ごとの事情を考慮する点を強調する。
one by one は順番に一つずつ扱うことが焦点。case by case は案件ごとの判断のしかたに焦点がある。
at one's discretion は誰の裁量で決めるかを示す。on a case-by-case basis はどのように判断するかを示す。

note.en: A broad equivalent for handling matters separately.
note.ja: 案件を別々に扱う場合の広い言い換え。

etymology.en: Built from case ‘an individual instance’ in the repeated pattern X by X, as in day by day.
etymology.ja: case（個々の案件）を day by day と同じ X by X の形で繰り返した表現。

equivalents.de: von Fall zu Fall / im Einzelfall

en: on a case-by-case basis
a case-by-case assessment
a case-by-case approach
a case-by-case review
consider exceptions case by case
handle requests case by case
ja: on a case-by-case basis — 個々の事情に応じて
a case-by-case assessment — 案件ごとの評価
a case-by-case approach — 個別事情に応じた対応
a case-by-case review — 一件ごとの審査
consider exceptions case by case — 例外を認めるか一件ずつ検討する
handle requests case by case — 依頼を個別に処理する

en: We consider requests for deadline extensions on a case-by-case basis.
The team applies the same criteria to every request but makes its decisions case by case.
A case-by-case review of the damaged items will determine which ones can be repaired.
ja: We consider requests for deadline extensions on a case-by-case basis. — 期限延長の依頼は、個々の事情に応じて検討します。
The team applies the same criteria to every request but makes its decisions case by case. — チームはどの依頼にも同じ基準を適用するが、結論は一件ずつ事情を見て出す。
A case-by-case review of the damaged items will determine which ones can be repaired. — 破損した品物を一つずつ確認し、修理できるものを判断する。

patterns: main clause + in case + subject + verb
in case + subject + verb, + main clause

usage.tense: For a possible future event, the present simple is common after in case: Take a charger in case your battery runs low. In a past narrative, the past is common: I took a charger in case my battery ran low.
usage.complement: In case usually introduces a clause. In case of takes a noun phrase and is common in notices. Just in case can stand alone when the possibility is understood.
usage.regional: Some American English uses in case with the conditional meaning if or in the event that. When the timing of the action matters, if makes a condition clear and as a precaution makes advance preparation clear.

en: because something might happen or might be needed, so an action is taken as a precaution
as a precaution, with the possible situation understood, especially in just in case
if or in the event that, in some uses, especially in American English
ja: ～するかもしれないので、～に備えて、念のため
起こりうることが文脈から分かるときの「念のため」。特に just in case の形
～の場合は、もし～なら。一部の用法で、特に米語

nuance.en: In its precautionary use, in case explains why you act ahead of a possibility. You may also provide information in case someone has not heard it. Just in case makes the precaution explicit. Expressions such as in case you hadn't noticed can sound pointed depending on tone.
nuance.ja: 備えの用法では、起こりうる事態に先回りして行動する理由を示す。相手がまだ知らないかもしれないと思って情報を伝えるときにも使える。just in case は「念のため」という気持ちをはっきり示す。in case you hadn't noticed のような言い方は、口調によっては皮肉っぽく聞こえる。

en: if. Introduces a condition. I'll bring a charger if my phone is low makes bringing it depend on that condition. I'll bring a charger in case my phone runs low expresses preparation.
in case of. Takes a noun, as in in case of fire, and often tells you what to do if an event occurs.
in that case. Refers back to a situation already mentioned and introduces a response or conclusion: In that case, let's reschedule.
so that. Introduces a purpose or intended result. In case introduces a possibility that motivates a precaution.
ja: if は条件を示す。I'll bring a charger if my phone is low. では電池残量が少ないことが持参の条件。I'll bring a charger in case my phone runs low. では残量が減る可能性に備えて持参する。
in case of は in case of fire のように後ろに名詞を取り、事態が起きた際の行動を示す案内でよく使う。
in that case は直前に出た状況を受けて「それなら」と結論や対応を述べる。
so that は目的や意図する結果を示す。in case は備えを取る理由となる可能性を示す。

note.en: A plain equivalent when the possible situation is understood.
note.ja: 備える事態が文脈から分かるときの平易な言い換え。

note.en: A more formal equivalent for the conditional use.
note.ja: 条件を表す用法での改まった言い換え。

etymology.en: Built from in and case, where case means a situation or eventuality.
etymology.ja: in と case（場合、起こりうる事態）からなる表現。

equivalents.it: nel caso in cui / per sicurezza

en: in case it rains
in case you need it
in case you missed it
save a copy just in case
in case of emergency
ja: in case it rains — 雨が降るかもしれないので
in case you need it — 必要になったときに備えて
in case you missed it — 見逃しているかもしれないので
save a copy just in case — 念のためコピーを保存する
in case of emergency — 緊急時には

en: I'll bring a charger in case my phone runs low.
I took a screenshot in case the confirmation page disappeared.
The link should still work, but I saved a copy just in case.
In case you missed yesterday's email, here's the updated schedule.
ja: I'll bring a charger in case my phone runs low. — スマホの電池が減ったときに備えて、充電器を持っていく。
I took a screenshot in case the confirmation page disappeared. — 確認画面が消えても困らないように、スクリーンショットを撮った。
The link should still work, but I saved a copy just in case. — リンクはまだ開けるはずだけど、念のためコピーを保存しておいた。
In case you missed yesterday's email, here's the updated schedule. — 昨日のメールを見逃しているかもしれないので、更新した予定を送ります。

usage.position: Usually used before a noun. In school and admissions contexts, extracurriculars is an informal plural noun meaning extracurricular activities.
usage.spelling: Extracurricular is commonly written as one word. Extra-curricular is also used.

en: outside the regular course of study or curriculum at a school or college
outside someone's usual duties or relationship, sometimes unofficial or secret (often humorous)
ja: 学校や大学の正規の教育課程に含まれない、課外の
通常の職務や関係の外で行われる、非公式の、内緒の（冗談めいた用法）

nuance.en: Extracurricular activities can include clubs, sports, music, or volunteering. The main question is whether the activity is part of the regular curriculum. A school may organize it, and it need not take place after classes or off campus. In informal or humorous use outside school, the word may suggest an unofficial side activity or, in a relationship context, an affair.
nuance.ja: extracurricular activities には部活動、スポーツ、音楽、ボランティアなどが含まれうる。着目するのは正規の教育課程に含まれるかどうか。学校主催、校内開催、昼休みの活動でも課外活動になりうる。学校以外では、非公式な活動を冗談めかして指すことがあり、恋愛の文脈では浮気をほのめかす場合もある。

en: after-school. Tells you when an activity takes place. An extracurricular club can also meet at lunchtime.
elective. A course chosen by the student that can still count toward graduation. An extracurricular activity is outside the regular curriculum.
co-curricular. Often describes activities outside regular classes that are designed to complement what students learn. Institutions vary in how they use the two terms.
ja: after-school は活動が放課後に行われることを示す。extracurricular のクラブは昼休みに活動することもある。
elective は選択科目で、卒業に必要な単位に数えられることもある。extracurricular activity は正規の教育課程の外にある活動。
co-curricular は、正規の授業を補う目的で設ける活動を指すことが多い。extracurricular との区別は学校によって異なる。

note.en: A plain paraphrase in educational contexts.
note.ja: 教育の文脈での平易な言い換え。

etymology.en: Formed from extra- ‘outside’ and curricular ‘relating to a curriculum’.
etymology.ja: extra-（外の）と curricular（教育課程に関する）からなる。

en: extracurricular activities
extracurricular clubs
an extracurricular program
participate in extracurricular activities
list your extracurricular activities
balance schoolwork and extracurricular activities
ja: extracurricular activities — 課外活動
extracurricular clubs — 課外活動のクラブ
an extracurricular program — 課外プログラム
participate in extracurricular activities — 課外活動に参加する
list your extracurricular activities — 自分の課外活動を列挙する
balance schoolwork and extracurricular activities — 学業と課外活動を両立する

en: The school offers extracurricular clubs in music, debate, and robotics.
The chess club meets at lunchtime, so students can take part in an extracurricular activity without staying after school.
The application asks which extracurricular activities you took part in and what your role was.
ja: The school offers extracurricular clubs in music, debate, and robotics. — その学校には、音楽、ディベート、ロボット製作の課外クラブがある。
The chess club meets at lunchtime, so students can take part in an extracurricular activity without staying after school. — チェスクラブは昼休みに集まるので、生徒は放課後に残らず課外活動に参加できる。
The application asks which extracurricular activities you took part in and what your role was. — 出願書類では、どの課外活動に参加し、どんな役割を担ったかが問われる。

usage.object: With a person as the object, vindicate may mean clearing them of blame or showing they were right. With a decision or prediction as the object, it means showing that it was sound or accurate.

en: to show that a person was wrongly blamed or that an accusation against them was unfounded
to show that a disputed judgment, action, or claim was right
ja: 人にかけられた疑いを晴らす、非難が当たらなかったと示す
疑問視されていた判断・行動・主張が正しかったと示す

nuance.en: Vindicate often looks back at an earlier accusation or disagreement. New evidence may clear a person, or later events may bear out a decision that others doubted. To feel vindicated is to feel that events have shown that you were right.
nuance.ja: 以前の非難や意見の対立を振り返る場面でよく使う。新しい証拠で人の疑いが晴れる場合も、その後の経過から、疑問視されていた判断が正しかったと分かる場合もある。feel vindicated は、結果を見て自分が正しかったと感じること。

en: justify. Give reasons that make a decision defensible. Vindicate often involves evidence or events that show a challenged decision was right.
exonerate. Clear someone of blame or responsibility. Vindicate also applies to judgments and predictions that turn out to be right.
validate. Confirm that something is sound, valid, or acceptable. Vindicate often implies earlier criticism, doubt, or blame.
vindictive. An adjective meaning eager to take revenge or get back at someone. Vindicate in its common modern uses means to clear someone or show that someone or something was right.
ja: justify は行動や判断を擁護する理由を示すこと。vindicate は、疑問視された判断が証拠や結果によって正しかったと分かる場面によく合う。
exonerate は人の疑いを晴らす、責任がなかったと明らかにすること。vindicate は、判断や予測が正しかったと示す場合にも使う。
validate は妥当性や有効性などを確認すること。vindicate には、それ以前に批判・疑問・非難があったという含みが出やすい。
vindictive は仕返しをしたがる、執念深いという意味の形容詞。vindicate の現代の主な意味は、疑いを晴らす、正しさを示すこと。

note.en: Close when evidence clears a person of blame.
note.ja: 証拠によって人の疑いが晴れる用法で近い。

note.en: Close when later findings support an earlier claim or judgment.
note.ja: 後から得られた結果が、以前の主張や判断を裏づける場合に近い。

etymology.en: From Latin vindicare, ‘to claim, defend, or avenge’. An early English sense was ‘to rescue or deliver’.
etymology.ja: ラテン語 vindicare（権利を主張する、守る、報復する）に由来する。英語での初期の意味には「救い出す」があった。

equivalents.de: jemanden entlasten / jemandem recht geben / eine Entscheidung bestätigen

en: vindicate a decision
vindicate an earlier warning
