vindicate someone completely
be vindicated by the results
feel vindicated
a chance to vindicate oneself
ja: vindicate a decision — 判断が正しかったと示す
vindicate an earlier warning — 以前の警告が正しかったと裏づける
vindicate someone completely — 人にかけられた疑いを完全に晴らす
be vindicated by the results — 結果によって正しさが裏づけられる
feel vindicated — 自分が正しかったと感じる
a chance to vindicate oneself — 自分への疑いを晴らす機会

en: The test results vindicated our decision to delay the launch.
The maintenance logs vindicated the engineer, who had been blamed for the outage.
She felt vindicated when the independent review confirmed the problems she had warned about.
ja: The test results vindicated our decision to delay the launch. — 試験結果は、発売を延期した私たちの判断が正しかったことを裏づけた。
The maintenance logs vindicated the engineer, who had been blamed for the outage. — 保守記録によって、停止の責任を問われていた技術者の疑いが晴れた。
She felt vindicated when the independent review confirmed the problems she had warned about. — 独立した調査で、以前から警告していた問題が確認され、彼女は自分が正しかったと感じた。

patterns: pave / surface + a road + with macadam

usage.counting: For the material or surfacing, use macadam without an indefinite article, as in paved with macadam. In a macadam road, road is the countable noun.
usage.stress: The main stress is on the second syllable.

en: road surfacing made of compacted layers of broken stone, or the stone used for that surfacing
in some uses, surfacing of this kind bound with tar or asphalt
ja: 砕石を層状に敷いて締め固めた道路舗装、またはその舗装に使う砕石。マカダム舗装
用法によっては、砕石をタールやアスファルトで結合させた舗装

nuance.en: In historical descriptions, macadam often refers to a road made by firmly compacting layers of broken stone. Later forms may use a binder such as tar or asphalt. The original method did not require either binder. The word is especially useful in accounts of road history or in technical descriptions of pavement.
nuance.ja: 道路史では、砕石を重ねて硬く締め固めた舗装を指すことが多い。後にタールやアスファルトで石を結合させる工法も生まれた。もともとの工法では、タールやアスファルトは必要なかった。道路の歴史や舗装の技術的な説明で見かける語。

en: gravel road. A broad term for a road surfaced with gravel. Macadam identifies a specific type of surfacing built up from compacted layers of broken stone.
tarmac. A shortened form of tarmacadam, historically tar-bound macadam. In everyday English it can also refer more broadly to a paved surface, especially an area at an airport.
asphalt. In ordinary road talk, refers to an asphalt-based paving material or surface. Macadam identifies a type of stone-layer construction, which may use asphalt as a binder.
ja: gravel road は砂利敷きの道路を広く指す。macadam は、砕石を層状に敷いて締め固める舗装の種類を指す。
tarmac は tarmacadam の短縮形で、もともとはタールで結合したマカダム舗装。日常語では、空港の舗装された区域などを広く指すこともある。
asphalt は道路について、アスファルトを使った舗装材や路面を指す。macadam は砕石を層状に使う舗装で、結合材としてアスファルトを使うものもある。

note.en: A descriptive paraphrase for traditional macadam.
note.ja: 伝統的なマカダム舗装を説明する言い換え。

etymology.en: Named after John Loudon McAdam, the Scottish engineer associated with the road-building method.
etymology.ja: この道路舗装法を普及させたスコットランドの技術者、ジョン・ラウドン・マカダム（John Loudon McAdam）の名に由来する。

en: a macadam road
a macadam surface
paved with macadam
water-bound macadam
tar-bound macadam
ja: a macadam road — マカダム舗装の道路
a macadam surface — マカダム舗装の路面
paved with macadam — マカダム舗装が施された
water-bound macadam — 水締めマカダム舗装
tar-bound macadam — タールで結合したマカダム舗装

en: An old photograph shows a macadam road running through the village.
The town replaced the old macadam surface with asphalt.
The museum display explains how layers of broken stone were compacted to make a macadam road.
ja: An old photograph shows a macadam road running through the village. — 古い写真には、村を通るマカダム舗装の道路が写っている。
The town replaced the old macadam surface with asphalt. — 町は古いマカダム舗装をアスファルト舗装に替えた。
The museum display explains how layers of broken stone were compacted to make a macadam road. — 博物館の展示では、砕石の層を締め固めてマカダム舗装の道路を造る方法を紹介している。

patterns: it is obvious (to + person) that + clause
it is obvious why / how / which + clause

usage.perspective: Obvious to me names the person who finds it easy to see or understand. Not immediately obvious leaves room for the answer to become clear later.
usage.tone: Calling a point obvious may sound dismissive when someone else has struggled to understand it.

en: easy to notice or recognize
easy to understand, infer, or see as the natural choice
ja: 見てすぐ気づく、目につきやすい
容易に分かる、明らかな、自ずとそうだと分かる

nuance.en: Obvious suggests that little effort is needed to notice something or see why it is true. That judgment can depend on the observer. An obvious choice is a choice that readily suggests itself. Don't be so obvious can tell someone that their intentions are showing too clearly.
nuance.ja: 見たり考えたりしてすぐに分かる、という感覚を表す。何が明らかかは見る人によって違う場合がある。an obvious choice は、すぐに思い浮かぶ自然な選択肢。Don't be so obvious. は、意図があからさまに見えていると伝える言い方にもなる。

en: clear. Can describe a good explanation or something easy to understand. Obvious emphasizes how readily a fact or answer can be seen.
evident. Often suggests that signs or evidence make something clear and sounds somewhat more formal.
conspicuous. Emphasizes standing out and attracting attention. Obvious can describe a conclusion or explanation that is easy to grasp.
apparent. Can mean evident, but can also describe what seems to be true from appearances. Obvious normally expresses a firmer judgment.
ja: clear は説明の分かりやすさや内容の明確さも表す。obvious は、事実や答えがすぐ分かることを強調する。
evident は手掛かりや証拠から明らかだという響きがあり、やや改まっている。
conspicuous は周囲から際立ち、人目を引くことが焦点。obvious はすぐ理解できる結論や説明にも使える。
apparent は明らかという意味のほか、見かけ上そうだという意味にもなる。obvious は通常、より確かな判断を伝える。

note.en: Close when a fact or conclusion is easy to see.
note.ja: 事実や結論がすぐ分かる場合に近い。

note.en: Close when signs or evidence make the point clear.
note.ja: 手掛かりから明らかに分かる場合に近い。

etymology.en: From Latin obvius, ‘in the way’ or ‘readily encountered’, ultimately from ob ‘in front of’ and via ‘way’.
etymology.ja: ラテン語 obvius（行く先にある、すぐ出会う）に由来する。ob（前に）と via（道）にさかのぼる。

en: an obvious choice
an obvious mistake
for obvious reasons
not immediately obvious
painfully obvious
obvious to anyone
ja: an obvious choice — 真っ先に思い浮かぶ選択肢
an obvious mistake — 見ればすぐ分かるミス
for obvious reasons — 理由は言うまでもなく
not immediately obvious — すぐには分からない
painfully obvious — 嫌になるほど明白な、あまりにも露骨な
obvious to anyone — 誰の目にも明らかな

en: It wasn't immediately obvious why the two figures differed.
The station café was the obvious choice for a quick meeting.
It was obvious to me that she wanted to change the subject.
There was an obvious mistake in the date on the first page.
ja: It wasn't immediately obvious why the two figures differed. — なぜ二つの数値が違うのか、すぐには分からなかった。
The station café was the obvious choice for a quick meeting. — 短い打ち合わせなら、駅のカフェが真っ先に思い浮かぶ場所だった。
It was obvious to me that she wanted to change the subject. — 彼女が話題を変えたがっているのは、私には明らかだった。
There was an obvious mistake in the date on the first page. — 最初のページの日付には、見ればすぐ分かる誤りがあった。

usage.position: At the start, Obviously, often frames the whole sentence. In the middle, it commonly follows be or an auxiliary and precedes an ordinary main verb.
usage.tone: A clipped Obviously! or Obviously not! can sound dismissive if the other person did not know the answer.

en: in a way that makes a fact or situation easy to recognize or understand
used to present a point as already known, readily accepted, or apparent to the listener
ja: 見てすぐ分かるほど明らかに、どう見ても
言うまでもなく、当然ながら。相手も知っている、または同意すると思われることを述べるときに使う

nuance.en: In She was obviously upset, the speaker treats her feelings as easy to infer from what they saw or heard. At the start of a sentence, obviously can mark something the speaker treats as common ground. When that assumption is unwelcome, it can sound impatient or condescending. Tone and context matter.
nuance.ja: She was obviously upset. では、見聞きした様子から彼女が動揺しているとすぐ分かった、という話し手の判断を示す。文頭では、話し手が相手も分かっていると考えることを前置きできる。相手にとって明らかでないことを当然のように言うと、いら立ちや上から目線に聞こえることがある。

en: obvious. An adjective, as in an obvious error or It is obvious that something went wrong. Obviously is the adverb.
clearly. Often overlaps with obviously in judgments. In speak clearly, it means in a way that is easy to hear or understand.
apparently. Can mark an inference from appearances or information someone has heard. Obviously usually conveys greater confidence that the point is clear.
of course. Often introduces an expected fact and can also gladly grant a request. Obviously stresses that something should be easy to see or infer.
ja: obvious は形容詞で、an obvious error や It is obvious that ～ の形で使う。obviously は副詞。
clearly は判断を示すときに obviously と重なる。speak clearly では「聞き取りやすく、はっきり話す」という意味。
apparently は見た様子や伝聞をもとに「どうやら」と述べることがある。obviously は通常、その判断が明白だという強い確信を伝える。
of course は予想どおりのことを述べたり、頼みごとに快く応じたりできる。obviously は見れば分かる、考えればすぐ分かるという含みが強い。

note.en: Close when a fact or conclusion is easy to see.
note.ja: 事実や結論が容易に分かると述べる場合に近い。

note.en: Close when observable signs make a conclusion clear.
note.ja: 観察できる手掛かりから結論が明らかな場合に近い。

etymology.en: Formed from obvious and the adverb-forming suffix -ly.
etymology.ja: 形容詞 obvious（明らかな）に、副詞を作る接尾辞 -ly が付いた語。

en: obviously upset
obviously wrong
obviously important
obviously not ready
quite obviously
ja: obviously upset — 明らかに動揺している
obviously wrong — 明らかに間違っている
obviously important — 言うまでもなく重要な
obviously not ready — どう見ても準備ができていない
quite obviously — どう見ても明らかに

en: She was obviously upset, so I gave her a moment before asking what had happened.
Obviously, we need the client's approval before we send the final draft.
The date on the cover is obviously wrong. The report includes figures from the following year.
The room is obviously not big enough for thirty people.
ja: She was obviously upset, so I gave her a moment before asking what had happened. — 彼女は明らかに動揺していたので、少し間を置いてから何があったのか尋ねた。
Obviously, we need the client's approval before we send the final draft. — 当然ですが、最終案を送る前に依頼人の承認が必要です。
The date on the cover is obviously wrong. The report includes figures from the following year. — 表紙の日付は明らかに間違っている。その報告書には翌年の数値が載っている。
The room is obviously not big enough for thirty people. — その部屋は、どう見ても30人が入るには狭すぎる。

grammar.countability: usually countable for a role, feature, event, or function in mathematics or code; also uncountable in expressions such as brain function
patterns: the function of + something + is to + verb

usage.verb: Function is intransitive. The device functions properly means it works as intended. The device functions as a timer describes the role it serves.
usage.dependence: A is a function of B means that A depends on B. In a graph, plot A as a function of B means use B as the input or independent variable.

en: the role or purpose of a person, thing, or system, or a task a device can perform
an organized social event or official occasion
a rule in mathematics assigning one output to each allowed input
a callable piece of code that performs a task and may return a value
to work or operate, or to serve in a particular role
ja: 人・物・仕組みの役割や目的、機器が備える機能
社交行事、式典などの公式な催し
数学で、定義域の各入力に一つの出力を対応させる規則、関数
プログラミングで、呼び出して処理を実行し、場合によっては値を返すコードのまとまり、関数
機能する、作動する、～として役割を果たす

nuance.en: Function can describe the job a part does, as in the function of a filter, or a particular operation a product offers, as in a search function. As a verb, function is slightly more formal than work. A social function often suggests an organized gathering, such as a reception. In ordinary writing, a function of can express dependence without specifying a formula.
nuance.ja: the function of a filter はフィルターが果たす役割を指し、a search function は製品などに備わる検索機能を指す。動詞では work よりやや改まった響きがある。a social function はレセプションなど、企画された社交の催しを指すことが多い。一般の文章でも a function of は、数式を示さず「～によって決まる」と述べるのに使える。

en: role. Often used for a person's responsibilities or the part someone or something plays in a system. Function often emphasizes the task performed.
feature. A capability or characteristic of a product. A function is an operation it can perform; a feature can also be a design detail.
work. The everyday verb for operating or working as intended. Function often appears in technical or more formal descriptions.
event. A broad term for an occurrence or organized occasion. A function is typically a planned social or official gathering.
ja: role は人の役割や、仕組みの中で何を担うかを表しやすい。function は具体的にどんな働きをするかに焦点を当てることが多い。
feature は製品の機能や特徴。function は実行できる処理を指し、feature は外観上の特徴などにも使える。
work は「作動する、うまく動く」の日常的な動詞。function は技術的な説明や改まった文脈によく出る。
event は出来事や催しを広く指す。function は通常、計画された社交行事や公式の催し。

note.en: Close for the intended use or role of something.
note.ja: 物の用途や目的を指す場合に近い。

note.en: Close when a device or system works.
note.ja: 機器やシステムが作動する意味で近い。

etymology.en: From French fonction and Latin functio ‘performance’, from fungi ‘to perform or discharge a duty’.
etymology.ja: フランス語 fonction やラテン語 functio（遂行）に由来し、ラテン語 fungi（務めを果たす）にさかのぼる。

en: the main function of a component
serve a useful function
a search function
function properly
function as a backup
attend a social function
a function of temperature
plot A as a function of B
call a function
ja: the main function of a component — 部品の主な役割
serve a useful function — 有用な役割を果たす
a search function — 検索機能
function properly — 正常に機能する
function as a backup — 予備として機能する
attend a social function — 社交行事に出席する
a function of temperature — 温度に応じて決まる量
plot A as a function of B — Bを横軸にAをグラフにする
call a function — 関数を呼び出す

en: The main function of the valve is to control the flow of water.
The app functions normally even when the phone is offline.
The spare room functions as an office during the week.
We met several of the local attorneys at a function after the conference.
The graph shows battery life as a function of screen brightness.
This function takes a list of prices and returns the total.
ja: The main function of the valve is to control the flow of water. — そのバルブの主な役割は、水の流れを調整することだ。
The app functions normally even when the phone is offline. — スマホがオフラインでも、そのアプリは正常に動く。
The spare room functions as an office during the week. — 空き部屋は平日は仕事部屋として使っている。
We met several of the local attorneys at a function after the conference. — 会議後の懇親会で、現地の弁護士数人と知り合った。
The graph shows battery life as a function of screen brightness. — グラフは、画面の明るさに応じてバッテリーの持ちがどう変わるかを示している。
This function takes a list of prices and returns the total. — この関数は価格のリストを受け取り、合計額を返す。

usage.article: Use mea culpa by itself to acknowledge your own fault. Use a mea culpa for an instance of someone admitting fault.
usage.tone: The standalone phrase can sound wry or self-deprecating in everyday speech. The noun is also used in reporting about public admissions of fault.

en: my fault; an expression used to acknowledge responsibility for a mistake
an admission of fault, often made publicly or in the form of an apology
ja: 私の落ち度です、自分のミスです（自分の責任を認める表現）
自らの非を認める発言や文章、謝罪の表明

nuance.en: Mea culpa focuses on accepting responsibility. Used alone after a minor mistake, it can sound wry or playfully formal. As a noun in a headline or article, a public mea culpa can refer to a serious acknowledgment of failure.
nuance.ja: 自分の非を認め、責任を引き受けることに焦点がある。小さなミスのあとに一言で言うと、少し自嘲的だったり、わざと改まったりした響きになる。記事などの a public mea culpa は、重大な失敗について公に非を認める発言も指せる。

en: my fault. A plain, everyday admission of responsibility. Mea culpa can sound more stylized or wry.
my bad. Very informal and especially common for small mistakes. Mea culpa can be playful, and its noun use also fits serious public statements.
apology. Can express regret or say sorry. A mea culpa specifically involves accepting fault.
admission of fault. A neutral description of accepting blame. A mea culpa can carry a more personal or rhetorical tone.
ja: my fault は、自分の責任を認める日常的で率直な表現。mea culpa は、気取った響きや自嘲が出る場合がある。
my bad は、特に小さなミスに使うくだけた表現。mea culpa も冗談めかして使えるが、名詞では真剣な声明にも使える。
apology は、申し訳ない気持ちを伝える謝罪全般。a mea culpa では自分の非を認めることが中心。
admission of fault は、過失や責任を認めることを中立的に表す。a mea culpa は、個人的な反省を述べたり、言い方に演出を加えたりする響きが出ることがある。

note.en: A direct everyday equivalent when accepting responsibility.
note.ja: 自分の落ち度を認めるときの平易な言い換え。

note.en: A close equivalent for the noun.
note.ja: 名詞としての近い言い換え。

etymology.en: Borrowed from Latin mea culpa, literally ‘through my fault’. The expression is associated with the Confiteor, a traditional Catholic prayer of confession.
etymology.ja: ラテン語 mea culpa（直訳は「私の落ち度によって」）からの借用。カトリックの伝統的な告白の祈り Confiteor で使われる。

equivalents.de: mein Fehler / das Eingeständnis eines Fehlers
equivalents.fr: c’est ma faute / le mea culpa

en: a public mea culpa
issue a mea culpa
publish a mea culpa
a mea culpa for an editorial mistake
a brief mea culpa
ja: a public mea culpa — 公に非を認めること
issue a mea culpa — 自らの非を認める声明を出す
publish a mea culpa — 自らの非を認める文章を公表する
a mea culpa for an editorial mistake — 編集上の誤りについて非を認める文章
a brief mea culpa — 手短に非を認める言葉

en: Mea culpa. I attached the old draft instead of the revised one.
The editor published a mea culpa after readers pointed out the error.
She began the meeting with a brief mea culpa for overlooking the scheduling conflict.
ja: Mea culpa. I attached the old draft instead of the revised one. — 私のミスです。修正版を添付するつもりが、古い草案を添付してしまいました。
The editor published a mea culpa after readers pointed out the error. — 読者が誤りを指摘したあと、編集者は自らの非を認める文章を公表した。
She began the meeting with a brief mea culpa for overlooking the scheduling conflict. — 彼女は、日程の重複を見落とした自分のミスを手短に認めてから、会議を始めた。

usage.article: Use an edifice in the singular. The word is formal and can be literal or figurative.

en: a large or imposing building
an elaborate system of ideas, institutions, or claims viewed as a constructed whole
ja: 大きく堂々とした建物、壮麗な建築物
理論・制度・主張などが積み上げられてできた大きな体系、構築物（比喩）

nuance.en: Edifice is more formal and evocative than building and often draws attention to scale or grandeur. Figuratively, it can suggest a system with many interdependent parts built on a foundation. An edifice of lies suggests that false claims have been built up into an elaborate whole.
nuance.ja: building より改まった描写語で、建物の規模や威容を印象づけることが多い。比喩では、共通の土台の上に、互いに支え合う要素が積み上がった体系を連想させる。an edifice of lies は、いくつもの嘘を重ねて組み立てた虚構を指す。

en: building. The ordinary word for a constructed building of any size. Edifice often suggests scale or an imposing appearance.
structure. Covers many physical constructions and abstract arrangements. Edifice adds the image of a substantial building or an elaborate whole.
framework. Emphasizes the supporting arrangement or set of rules. Edifice often evokes the entire system built on that support.
ja: building は規模を問わず使える一般的な「建物」。edifice は大きさや堂々とした外観を連想させやすい。
structure は建造物や抽象的な構造を広く指す。edifice には、大きな建物や作り込まれた体系全体のイメージがある。
framework は支える枠組みやルールに焦点がある。edifice はその土台の上に築かれた体系全体を連想させる。

note.en: The everyday equivalent in the literal sense.
note.ja: 文字どおりの用法での日常的な言い換え。

note.en: A neutral equivalent for many figurative uses.
note.ja: 多くの比喩用法で使える中立的な言い換え。

etymology.en: From Old French edifice, from Latin aedificium ‘building’, related to aedificare ‘to build’.
etymology.ja: 古フランス語 edifice を経て、ラテン語 aedificium（建物）に由来する。aedificare（建てる）と関係がある。

en: an imposing edifice
a stone edifice
the edifice of a theory
an edifice of lies
the whole edifice collapses
build an edifice on shaky foundations
ja: an imposing edifice — 堂々とした建物
a stone edifice — 石造りの建物
the edifice of a theory — 理論の体系
an edifice of lies — 嘘を積み重ねた虚構
the whole edifice collapses — 体系全体が崩れる
build an edifice on shaky foundations — 危うい土台の上に体系を築く

en: A vast stone edifice overlooks the main square.
The whole edifice of the theory rests on a single assumption.
Once the records were made public, the edifice of lies began to collapse.
ja: A vast stone edifice overlooks the main square. — 中央広場を見下ろすように、巨大な石造りの建物がそびえている。
The whole edifice of the theory rests on a single assumption. — その理論体系の全体が、たった一つの前提に支えられている。
Once the records were made public, the edifice of lies began to collapse. — 記録が公開されると、嘘を積み重ねた虚構は崩れ始めた。

patterns: indulge + a desire / a curiosity / a passion

usage.complements: Use indulge in for an activity or pleasure you allow yourself. Use a direct object for the person you accommodate or the desire or interest you satisfy.

en: to allow yourself to enjoy something, especially a treat or something you might normally limit
to satisfy a desire or give yourself free rein to pursue an interest
to give someone what they want or let them do as they please
ja: 楽しみやぜいたくを自分に許す、思う存分楽しむ（indulge in ～）
欲求や好奇心を満たす、趣味や関心に存分に打ち込む
人の望みを聞き入れる、甘やかす

nuance.en: Indulge in can suggest a little excess, as with a second helping of dessert, or simply the pleasure of making time for something you love. With a person as its object, indulge can imply excessive leniency. Indulge me for a moment is a polite request to hear you out or go along with an idea briefly.
nuance.ja: indulge in は、デザートのおかわりのように少し羽目を外す場面にも、好きなことを楽しむ時間を取る場面にも使える。人を目的語に取る場合は、相手の望みを聞き入れ、文脈によっては「甘やかす」含みがある。Indulge me for a moment. は、相手に「少しだけ話を聞いてください」「ちょっとだけ付き合ってください」と頼む表現。

en: treat yourself to. Focuses on giving yourself a particular reward. Indulge in can also describe spending time on a pleasurable activity.
spoil. Often more critical, implying that giving someone too much may affect their behavior. Indulge can describe granting a single wish.
pamper. Focuses on giving someone special care or comfort. Indulge focuses on granting a wish or satisfying a desire.
ja: treat yourself to は「自分へのご褒美に～を買う・食べる」など、具体的なご褒美に焦点がある。indulge in は、好きな活動に時間を使うことにも使える。
spoil は甘やかしが相手の振る舞いに悪影響を及ぼす含みが強い。indulge は一度だけ願いを聞き入れる場合にも使える。
pamper は手厚い世話やぜいたくなもてなしに、indulge は望みを聞き入れたり欲求を満たしたりすることに焦点がある。

note.en: A common alternative for a specific treat.
note.ja: 具体的なご褒美を楽しむ場合の日常的な言い換え。

note.en: Emphasizes yielding to a desire or request.
note.ja: 欲求や要求に抗わず、受け入れることを強調する。

etymology.en: From Latin indulgēre ‘to be lenient, yield to’. Related English words include indulgence and indulgent.
etymology.ja: ラテン語 indulgēre（寛大に扱う、譲る）に由来する。関連語に indulgence（楽しみを自分に許すこと、甘やかし）と indulgent（甘い、寛大な）がある。

equivalents.fr: s’offrir un plaisir / céder aux caprices de quelqu’un
equivalents.es: darse un capricho / consentir a alguien

en: indulge in a little luxury
indulge in chocolate
indulge in some retail therapy
indulge one’s curiosity
indulge one’s passion for music
indulge a child’s every whim
Indulge me for a moment.
ja: indulge in a little luxury — ちょっとしたぜいたくを楽しむ
indulge in chocolate — チョコレートを心ゆくまで味わう
indulge in some retail therapy — 気晴らしに買い物を楽しむ
indulge one’s curiosity — 好奇心を満たす
indulge one’s passion for music — 音楽に思う存分打ち込む
indulge a child’s every whim — 子どものわがままを何でも聞き入れる
Indulge me for a moment. — 少しだけ付き合ってください。

en: We indulged in a second helping of dessert after dinner.
I went to the flea market to indulge my curiosity about old watches.
Her grandparents indulged her every whim.
Indulge me for a moment. What would happen if we tried it the other way around?
ja: We indulged in a second helping of dessert after dinner. — 夕食後、ついデザートをおかわりした。
I went to the flea market to indulge my curiosity about old watches. — 古い腕時計に前から興味があって、蚤の市に足を運んだ。
Her grandparents indulged her every whim. — 祖父母は彼女のわがままを何でも聞き入れた。
Indulge me for a moment. What would happen if we tried it the other way around? — 少しだけ付き合ってください。逆のやり方を試したら、どうなるでしょうか。

patterns: succumb to + an illness / one’s injuries
succumb to the temptation to + verb

usage.preposition: Use to to introduce the force or cause. Succumb can also stand alone when the cause is clear from context.

note.en: The final b is silent.
note.ja: 語末の b は発音しない。

en: to give way because a force, pressure, or temptation is too strong to resist
to die as a result of an illness or injury
ja: 圧力・誘惑などに屈する、疲労などに負ける
病気やけがが原因で亡くなる

nuance.en: A formal verb that presents the subject as being overcome. Succumb to temptation can sound playfully dramatic when the temptation is something as small as buying a pastry. With an illness or injury, succumb often appears in reports and implies that the person died.
nuance.ja: 何かに抗いきれず押し切られることを表す、やや改まった動詞。お菓子を買う程度の話で succumb to temptation を使うと、大げさな響きが冗談めくこともある。病気・けがが続くと、報道などで「それが原因で亡くなった」という意味になる。

en: give in to. An everyday expression for yielding to pressure or temptation. Succumb to sounds more formal and can suggest being overwhelmed.
indulge in. Focuses on allowing yourself a pleasure. Succumb to temptation focuses on the moment when resistance gives way.
die from. States the cause of death directly. Succumb to an illness or injury is more formal and can evoke a period of struggle.
ja: give in to は、圧力や誘惑に屈するときの日常的な表現。succumb to はより改まっており、抗いきれなかった感じが出やすい。
indulge in は楽しみを自分に許すことに、succumb to temptation は我慢しきれず誘惑に負けることに焦点がある。
die from は死因を直接伝える。succumb to はより改まった言い方で、病気やけがとの闘いを連想させることがある。

note.en: Common in everyday talk about pressure or temptation.
note.ja: 圧力や誘惑に屈する場面で使う日常的な言い換え。

note.en: A more formal alternative when someone gives way under pressure.
note.ja: 圧力に屈する場合の改まった言い換え。

note.en: A direct alternative in the sense of dying from an illness or injury.
note.ja: 病気やけがによる死を直接伝える言い方。

etymology.en: From Old French succomber or Latin succumbere ‘to yield, lie under’, formed from sub- ‘under’ and a verb related to cubare ‘to lie down’.
etymology.ja: 古フランス語 succomber またはラテン語 succumbere（屈する、下に横たわる）に由来。sub-（下に）と、cubare（横たわる）に関連する動詞から成る。

equivalents.de: dem Druck nachgeben / einer Versuchung erliegen / seinen Verletzungen erliegen
equivalents.it: cedere alla pressione / soccombere alle ferite riportate
equivalents.fr: céder à la pression / succomber à ses blessures
equivalents.es: ceder a la presión / sucumbir a sus heridas

en: succumb to temptation
succumb to pressure
succumb to fatigue
succumb to panic
succumb to the temptation to buy something
succumb to an illness
succumb to one’s injuries
ja: succumb to temptation — 誘惑に負ける
succumb to pressure — 圧力に屈する
succumb to fatigue — 疲労に負ける
succumb to panic — パニックに陥る
succumb to the temptation to buy something — 何かを買いたいという誘惑に負ける
succumb to an illness — 病気で亡くなる
succumb to one’s injuries — 負傷がもとで亡くなる

en: I finally succumbed to temptation and bought the vintage watch.
The committee refused to succumb to pressure to rush the vote.
Despite several emergency operations, he succumbed to his injuries two days later.
ja: I finally succumbed to temptation and bought the vintage watch. — 結局、誘惑に負けてそのヴィンテージ腕時計を買った。
The committee refused to succumb to pressure to rush the vote. — 委員会は、採決を急ぐよう求める圧力に屈しなかった。
Despite several emergency operations, he succumbed to his injuries two days later. — 数回の緊急手術を受けたが、彼はそのけががもとで２日後に亡くなった。

grammar.countability: countable for a number written as a decimal; uncountable for the base-ten system
patterns: express / write + a fraction + as a decimal
round + number + to + number + decimal places
convert + number + from decimal to binary

usage.reading: Say point for the decimal separator and usually read the digits after it individually. For example, 3.05 is three point zero five.
usage.precision: To two decimal places means to two digits after the decimal point. In 3.05, the 0 marks the tenths place and the 5 marks the hundredths place.

en: a number written using a decimal point, such as 0.75 or 3.05 (noun)
the base-ten system of representing numbers (uncountable noun)
based on ten or expressed using tenths, hundredths, and so on (adjective)
ja: 小数（名詞）。0.75 や 3.05 のように小数点を使って表した数。
十進表記、十進法（不可算名詞）。
十進法の、小数で表した（形容詞）。

nuance.en: As a noun, a decimal refers to an individual number in expressions such as write 3/4 as a decimal. In decimal refers to base-ten notation and can describe whole numbers too. In reporting measurements, decimal places count the digits after the point, including zeros.
nuance.ja: write 3/4 as a decimal の a decimal は「小数で表した数」。in decimal は「十進表記で」を意味し、整数にも使える。測定値などを示すときの decimal places は、小数点以下の桁数を表し、0 も1桁として数える。

en: decimal point / decimal place. In 3.05, the point is the dot, and the number has two decimal places.
fraction / decimal. The same value can be written as a fraction such as 3/4 or as a decimal such as 0.75.
decimal places / significant figures. The number 0.0042 has four decimal places and two significant figures.
ja: decimal point は小数点。decimal place は小数点以下の桁。3.05 は小数点が一つあり、小数点以下は2桁。
分数 3/4 と小数 0.75 は、同じ値を異なる形で表している。
0.0042 の decimal places（小数点以下の桁数）は4桁、significant figures（有効数字）は2桁。

note.en: A mathematical term for a fraction expressed in decimal notation, or with a denominator that is a power of ten.
note.ja: 小数表記で表した分数や、分母が10の累乗となる分数を指す数学用語。

note.en: An alternative when referring to the numeral system. Use base-ten before a noun, as in base-ten notation.
note.ja: 十進法を指す場合の言い換え。名詞の前では base-ten notation のように書く。

etymology.en: From Latin decimalis, based on decimus ‘tenth’, from decem ‘ten’.
etymology.ja: ラテン語 decimalis に由来する。もとは decimus（第10の）で、decem（10）と同じ語根を持つ。

en: a decimal point
a decimal place
a decimal fraction
a repeating decimal
the decimal system
write a fraction as a decimal
round to two decimal places
convert from binary to decimal
ja: a decimal point — 小数点
a decimal place — 小数点以下の1桁
a decimal fraction — 小数で表した分数、十進分数
a repeating decimal — 循環小数
the decimal system — 十進法
write a fraction as a decimal — 分数を小数で表す
round to two decimal places — 四捨五入して小数第2位まで求める
convert from binary to decimal — 二進表記から十進表記に変換する

en: Read 3.05 as “three point zero five.”
Write seven-eighths as a decimal.
Rounded to two decimal places, 12.346 becomes 12.35.
The binary number 1010 is 10 in decimal.
ja: Read 3.05 as “three point zero five.” — 3.05 は「three point zero five」と読む。
Write seven-eighths as a decimal. — 8分の7を小数で表しなさい。
Rounded to two decimal places, 12.346 becomes 12.35. — 12.346 を四捨五入して小数第2位まで求めると、12.35 になる。
The binary number 1010 is 10 in decimal. — 二進数の 1010 は、十進表記では 10 になる。

usage.preposition: Use intrinsic to when naming the thing whose nature or structure includes the quality. With part, use an intrinsic part of.

en: belonging to the nature of a thing itself or forming a basic part of what it is
arising from interest in or enjoyment of an activity itself, as in intrinsic motivation
ja: 物事そのものの性質に由来する、内在する、本質的な
活動そのものへの興味や楽しさから生じる（intrinsic motivation など）

nuance.en: Intrinsic describes where a quality comes from or how closely it belongs to the thing itself. Intrinsic value can refer to worth something has in its own right, regardless of its usefulness. Intrinsic motivation comes from finding the activity itself interesting or satisfying. Something can be intrinsic and still be undesirable, as in an intrinsic limitation.
nuance.ja: 物事の性質そのものに備わっていることを表す。intrinsic value は、何かの役に立つかどうかとは別に、それ自体が持つ価値を指すことがある。intrinsic motivation（内発的動機づけ）は、活動そのものに面白さや満足を感じて取り組むこと。an intrinsic limitation のように、望ましくない性質にも使う。

en: inherent. A close equivalent for a property that naturally belongs to something, as in inherent risk. Intrinsic also commonly appears in discussions of value and motivation.
essential. Focuses on what is necessary or indispensable. Intrinsic focuses on what belongs to the nature of the thing itself.
extrinsic. Arises from a source outside the thing or activity. A prize can provide extrinsic motivation, while enjoyment of the activity can provide intrinsic motivation.
ja: inherent も「もともと備わっている」という意味で、inherent risk（内在するリスク）などによく使う。intrinsic は value や motivation ともよく組み合わさる。
essential は「不可欠であること」に、intrinsic は「そのものの性質に備わっていること」に焦点がある。
extrinsic は「外からもたらされる」。賞品を目当てに取り組むのは外発的動機づけ、活動そのものが楽しくて取り組むのは内発的動機づけの例。

note.en: A close substitute when describing a property or limitation that naturally belongs to something.
note.ja: 物事にもともと備わっている性質や制約を述べる場合の近い言い換え。

note.en: Useful for describing a feature or limitation built into the design of a system.
note.ja: 仕組みの設計に組み込まれている機能や制約を表すときに使える。

etymology.en: From French intrinsèque, from Latin intrinsecus ‘on the inside, inwardly’.
etymology.ja: フランス語 intrinsèque を経て、ラテン語 intrinsecus（内側で、内向きに）に由来する。

en: intrinsic value
intrinsic motivation
intrinsic interest
an intrinsic property
an intrinsic limitation
an intrinsic part of the process
be intrinsic to the design
ja: intrinsic value — それ自体が持つ価値、内在的価値
intrinsic motivation — 内発的動機づけ
intrinsic interest — それ自体の面白さ
an intrinsic property — 内在的な性質
an intrinsic limitation — 仕組みそのものに由来する制約
an intrinsic part of the process — その過程を構成する本質的な一部
be intrinsic to the design — 設計そのものに備わっている

en: Some uncertainty is intrinsic to estimating how long a project will take.
Her interest in how languages work gives her intrinsic motivation to keep studying.
The collection has intrinsic value even if it never attracts paying visitors.
ja: Some uncertainty is intrinsic to estimating how long a project will take. — プロジェクトにかかる時間を見積もる以上、ある程度の不確実性はつきものだ。
Her interest in how languages work gives her intrinsic motivation to keep studying. — 言語の仕組みそのものが面白いからこそ、彼女は自分から勉強を続けている。
The collection has intrinsic value even if it never attracts paying visitors. — 入場料を払う来館者が一人も来なくても、そのコレクションにはそれ自体の価値がある。

usage.preposition: Use extrinsic to when naming the thing that a factor or influence lies outside. Extrinsic often comes before a noun, especially in academic writing.

en: originating outside something or lying outside its inherent nature
relating to a reward or outcome separate from doing an activity itself, as in extrinsic motivation
ja: 外部から来る、外的要因による、そのものの性質の外にある
活動とは別に得られる報酬や結果に由来する、外発的な（動機づけなど）

nuance.en: Extrinsic is a formal word that draws a boundary around the thing or activity under discussion. A factor can be extrinsic to a task and still have a major effect on how people perform it. In psychology, extrinsic motivation can involve a reward such as a bonus or a personally valued outcome such as earning a qualification.
nuance.ja: 何を基準に「外」とみなすかを意識して使う、やや改まった語。課題そのものの外にある要因でも、成績に大きく影響しうる。心理学の extrinsic motivation（外発的動機づけ）には、賞金のような報酬を目指す場合も、自分にとって大切な資格取得を目指す場合も含まれる。

en: intrinsic. An activity can be intrinsically motivating because it is enjoyable and extrinsically motivating because it leads to a qualification.
external. A broader word for something outside a physical, organizational, or other boundary. Extrinsic often concerns what belongs to the nature of the thing itself.
irrelevant. Means something has no bearing on the issue. An extrinsic factor can be highly relevant, as when room temperature affects test performance.
ja: intrinsic は「内在する、内発的な」。勉強自体が楽しいことは内発的動機、資格が取れることは外発的動機になり、同じ活動に両方がありうる。
external は、物理的・組織的な境界などの「外側」を広く表す。extrinsic は、あるものの性質や活動そのものに含まれるかどうかに焦点を置くことが多い。
irrelevant は「論点と関係がない」という意味。extrinsic な要因でも、室温が試験の成績に影響するように、結果と深く関係することがある。

note.en: A plain-language equivalent in phrases such as external factors and external influences.
note.ja: 外的要因や外部からの影響を表す日常的な言い換え。

note.en: A common alternative before nouns such as influence or pressure.
note.ja: influence や pressure の前で使える一般的な言い換え。

etymology.en: From Latin extrinsecus ‘outwardly, from outside’, ultimately related to exter ‘outer’.
etymology.ja: ラテン語 extrinsecus（外向きに、外から）に由来し、exter（外側の）と関係がある。

en: extrinsic motivation
an extrinsic reward
extrinsic incentives
extrinsic factors
extrinsic influences
be extrinsic to the task
be extrinsically motivated
ja: extrinsic motivation — 外発的動機づけ
an extrinsic reward — 外的報酬
extrinsic incentives — 外的インセンティブ
extrinsic factors — 外的要因
extrinsic influences — 外部からの影響
be extrinsic to the task — 課題そのものの外にある
be extrinsically motivated — 活動とは別の報酬や目的を動機とする

en: Earning a language certificate can provide extrinsic motivation to study, while the pleasure of reading a novel in that language can provide intrinsic motivation.
The bonus is an extrinsic reward for reaching the sales target.
Noise is extrinsic to the task itself, but it can affect how well people perform it.
ja: Earning a language certificate can provide extrinsic motivation to study, while the pleasure of reading a novel in that language can provide intrinsic motivation. — 語学の資格を取ることは外発的な学習動機になり、その言語で小説を読む楽しさは内発的な動機になりうる。
The bonus is an extrinsic reward for reaching the sales target. — そのボーナスは、売上目標を達成したことに対する外的報酬だ。
Noise is extrinsic to the task itself, but it can affect how well people perform it. — 騒音は課題そのものの外にある要因だが、取り組む人の成績に影響することがある。

grammar.countability: usually singular, with the definite article
patterns: be on the brink of + noun / -ing
teeter on the brink of + noun
bring / push + someone or something + to the brink (of + noun)
pull + someone or something + back from the brink

usage.article: The usual form is the brink. Use on for the state of being close, to for movement toward it, and from for movement away from it.
usage.ellipsis: The phrase from the brink can stand on its own when the danger is clear from context.

en: the point at which a significant event or change is about to happen
the very edge of a cliff or steep drop (literary)
ja: 重大な出来事や変化が起きる瀬戸際、寸前
崖など、急に落ち込む場所の縁（文語的）

nuance.en: Brink evokes a threshold that is very close. It often adds a sense of urgency in phrases such as on the brink of collapse, and it can also express anticipation in on the brink of a breakthrough. Teeter on the brink suggests an unstable situation that could tip into danger.
nuance.ja: 重大な変化まであと一歩という切迫感を出す語。on the brink of collapse なら「崩壊寸前」で、on the brink of a breakthrough なら「突破口が開ける寸前」と、好ましい変化にも使える。teeter on the brink は、危ういところで持ちこたえている状態を表す。

en: edge. The ordinary word for a physical boundary, as in the edge of a table. Brink in its literal sense usually evokes a steep drop.
on the verge of. Often interchangeable with on the brink of. Verge is also natural for personal reactions, as in on the verge of tears.
on the cusp of. Often used about the beginning of a new phase or era. Brink is especially natural when a crisis could occur at any moment.
ja: edge は the edge of a table（テーブルの端）のように、物の縁に広く使える。brink を文字どおりに使うと、崖など足元が切れ落ちる場所を連想させやすい。
on the verge of は多くの場面で on the brink of と言い換えられる。on the verge of tears（泣き出しそうで）のように、感情が表に出る寸前にもよく使う。
on the cusp of は新たな段階や時代の入り口を表すことが多い。brink は危機が今にも起こりそうな場面によく合う。

note.en: A close equivalent in the figurative pattern on the verge of.
note.ja: 比喩的な on the brink of に近い表現が on the verge of。

note.en: The usual equivalent for a literal physical boundary.
note.ja: 実際の場所や物の縁を指す一般的な言い換え。

etymology.en: From Middle English brink, a word of Scandinavian origin.
etymology.ja: 中英語 brink に由来する。もとはスカンディナヴィア系の語。

equivalents.de: kurz vor etwas stehen / am Rand eines Abgrunds
equivalents.it: essere sull’orlo di / il ciglio di un precipizio
equivalents.fr: être au bord de / le bord d’un précipice
equivalents.es: estar al borde de / el borde de un precipicio

en: on the brink of collapse
on the brink of bankruptcy
on the brink of extinction
on the brink of a breakthrough
on the brink of making a discovery
teeter on the brink of disaster
pull a company back from the brink
the brink of a cliff
ja: on the brink of collapse — 崩壊寸前で
on the brink of bankruptcy — 倒産寸前で
on the brink of extinction — 絶滅寸前で
on the brink of a breakthrough — 突破口が開ける寸前で
on the brink of making a discovery — 発見する寸前で
teeter on the brink of disaster — 大惨事の瀬戸際にある
pull a company back from the brink — 会社を危機の瀬戸際から救う
the brink of a cliff — 崖の縁

en: The negotiations were on the brink of collapse when both sides agreed to meet again.
After years of testing, the team believes it is on the brink of a breakthrough.
An emergency loan pulled the company back from the brink.
She stopped at the brink of the gorge and looked down.
ja: The negotiations were on the brink of collapse when both sides agreed to meet again. — 交渉が決裂寸前になったところで、双方は再び会うことに合意した。
After years of testing, the team believes it is on the brink of a breakthrough. — 何年も試験を重ね、チームはもう少しで突破口が開けると考えている。
An emergency loan pulled the company back from the brink. — 緊急融資によって、その会社は倒産の瀬戸際から救われた。
She stopped at the brink of the gorge and looked down. — 彼女は峡谷の縁で足を止め、下を見た。

usage.modifier: In terms such as quantum computing, quantum comes before the noun and indicates a connection with quantum physics.
usage.plural: Use quanta when counting discrete units in physics. In legal English, the quantum of damages usually refers to the amount as a whole.

en: a discrete unit of a physical quantity, such as a photon as a quantum of light
an amount, especially the amount of money at issue in a damages claim or award (formal or legal)
ja: 量子。光における光子のように、物理量をとびとびの単位で扱うときの一単位。
量、額。とくに法律英語では損害賠償額。

nuance.en: In physics, a quantum is a discrete unit, and its size depends on the physical system. In a literal quantum jump, a system changes from one quantum state to another. In ordinary figurative use, a quantum leap is a sudden, substantial advance or change. In legal texts, quantum can refer to how much is payable, while liability concerns whether a party is legally responsible.
nuance.ja: 物理学では、量子はとびとびの単位で、その大きさは対象によって異なる。物理学の quantum jump は、ある量子状態から別の量子状態への遷移を指す。比喩の quantum leap は「飛躍的な進歩・大きな変化」。法律文書では、liability が法的責任の有無を指す場面で、quantum は支払うべき金額を指す。

en: quantum / photon. Quantum is the general term for a discrete unit in this sense. A photon is specifically a quantum of electromagnetic radiation.
quantum / amount. Amount is the everyday word for a quantity or sum. In the phrase quantum of damages, quantum gives the same idea a specialist legal register.
quantum leap / breakthrough. Breakthrough emphasizes overcoming a barrier or making a discovery. Quantum leap emphasizes the size or suddenness of the advance.
ja: quantum（量子）はこの意味での一般語。photon（光子）は電磁放射の量子を指す。
amount は「量・額」を広く表す一般語。quantum of damages は損害賠償額を指す法律英語の表現。
breakthrough は障壁を乗り越えることや画期的な発見に、quantum leap は進歩の大きさや急激さに焦点がある。

note.en: Plain-language equivalent in the legal sense.
note.ja: 金額を表す法律用法での平易な言い換え。

note.en: A less emphatic alternative to the figurative phrase quantum leap.
note.ja: 比喩の quantum leap を穏やかに言い換えた表現。

etymology.en: From Latin quantum, the neuter form of quantus ‘how much, how great’. The sense ‘amount’ predates the physics sense.
etymology.ja: ラテン語 quantus（どれほどの量・大きさの）の中性形 quantum に由来する。「量・額」の意味は物理学での用法に先立つ。

equivalents.de: das Quant / die Höhe des Schadensersatzes
equivalents.fr: le quantum / le montant des dommages-intérêts
equivalents.es: el cuanto / la cuantía de la indemnización

en: a quantum of light
quantum mechanics
quantum computing
a quantum state
a quantum jump
a quantum leap in performance
the quantum of damages
assess the quantum of damages
ja: a quantum of light — 光の量子
quantum mechanics — 量子力学
quantum computing — 量子計算
a quantum state — 量子状態
a quantum jump — 量子跳躍（物理）
a quantum leap in performance — 性能の飛躍的な向上
the quantum of damages — 損害賠償額
assess the quantum of damages — 損害賠償額を算定する

en: A photon is a quantum of electromagnetic radiation.
The new manufacturing process was a quantum leap in precision.
The parties agreed on liability but disputed the quantum of damages.
ja: A photon is a quantum of electromagnetic radiation. — 光子は電磁放射の量子である。
The new manufacturing process was a quantum leap in precision. — 新しい製造工程によって、精度が飛躍的に向上した。
The parties agreed on liability but disputed the quantum of damages. — 当事者間で賠償責任については争いがなかったが、損害賠償額については争いがあった。

patterns: have a genetic predisposition to + condition

usage.complement: Use to before a condition (a predisposition to asthma) or an infinitive (a predisposition to avoid conflict). Toward or towards can introduce a type of behavior or an attitude.

en: an existing inclination that makes someone more likely to think, feel, or behave in a particular way
a susceptibility that makes a person more likely to develop a disease or condition
ja: ある考え方・感じ方・行動を取りやすい傾向、もともとの性向
病気や症状が生じやすい素因、かかりやすさ

nuance.en: Predisposition is more formal than tendency. It presents the inclination or susceptibility as already present before the behavior or condition appears. It can arise from prior experience or other factors. Genetic predisposition specifies a genetic contribution to the likelihood of a condition.
nuance.ja: tendency より改まった語で、行動を取ったり病気を発症したりする前から、そうなりやすい傾向や素因があることを表す。過去の経験に由来する傾向にも使える。genetic predisposition は、発症のしやすさに遺伝的要因が関わることを表す。

en: tendency. A broad word for a pattern or inclination, including observed trends. Predisposition presents the inclination as something already present.
susceptibility. Highlights how easily someone may be affected. Predisposition also covers behavioral inclinations such as a tendency to avoid conflict.
risk factor. A characteristic or exposure associated with a higher likelihood of an outcome. A predisposition describes the underlying susceptibility or inclination itself.
ja: tendency は、観察された傾向や癖まで幅広く指す。predisposition は、ある行動や結果につながりやすい性向や素因がすでにあることに焦点を置く。
susceptibility は、病気や影響を受けやすいことに焦点を置く。predisposition は、対立を避けがちといった行動面の傾向にも使える。
risk factor（リスク因子）は、ある結果が起きやすいことと関連する特徴や曝露を指す。predisposition は、本人に備わっている発症のしやすさや性向に焦点を置く。

note.en: A close alternative for an inclination to think or act in a certain way.
note.ja: 特定の考え方や行動を取りやすい傾向を表す言い換え。

note.en: A close alternative in the sense of being prone to a disease or condition.
note.ja: 病気や症状が生じやすいことを表す言い換え。

etymology.en: Combines pre- ‘before’ and disposition ‘inclination or tendency’.
etymology.ja: pre-（前もって）と disposition（性向、傾向）から成る。

en: have a predisposition to avoid conflict
a predisposition toward pessimism
a genetic predisposition
a predisposition to developing a condition
a predisposition to asthma
have a predisposition to question assumptions
ja: have a predisposition to avoid conflict — 対立を避けがちな傾向がある
a predisposition toward pessimism — 悲観的に考えがちな傾向
a genetic predisposition — 遺伝的素因
a predisposition to developing a condition — ある症状や病気を発症しやすい素因
a predisposition to asthma — 喘息を発症しやすい素因
have a predisposition to question assumptions — 前提を疑ってかかる傾向がある

en: Her experience as an examiner gave her a predisposition to look for weaknesses in an argument.
The study looked at whether some participants had a genetic predisposition to asthma.
People with a predisposition to avoid conflict may agree in meetings and raise their concerns later.
ja: Her experience as an examiner gave her a predisposition to look for weaknesses in an argument. — 審査官としての経験から、彼女は議論の弱点を探す傾向が身についた。
The study looked at whether some participants had a genetic predisposition to asthma. — その研究では、一部の参加者に喘息を発症しやすい遺伝的素因があるかどうかを調べた。
People with a predisposition to avoid conflict may agree in meetings and raise their concerns later. — 対立を避けがちな人は、会議では同意して、後から懸念を伝えることがある。

patterns: there is a tendency for + noun + to + verb

usage.infinitive: Use a verb after to in a tendency to exaggerate. Use a noun after toward or towards, as in a tendency toward caution.
usage.subject: Use for to introduce the subject of the action in there is a tendency for prices to rise. Prices tend to rise expresses the same idea more directly.

en: a likelihood of behaving or reacting in a particular way, often based on what typically happens
a general pattern or direction in which something tends to happen or develop
ja: 人や物が特定の行動・反応をしやすいこと、傾向、性向
物事がある方向に動きがちであること、全体的な傾向

nuance.en: Tendency can describe a person's behavior, a material's properties, or a broader pattern. It often summarizes what happens repeatedly and leaves the cause open. A growing tendency suggests that the behavior or change is becoming more common.
nuance.ja: 人の行動、素材の性質、社会全体の動きまで幅広く使える。何度も見られるパターンを表すことが多く、原因は文脈に委ねられる。a growing tendency は、その行動や変化が以前よりよく見られることを表す。

en: predisposition. Emphasizes an underlying inclination or susceptibility already present. Tendency can simply describe a pattern you observe.

trend. Often describes a broader direction of change over time, especially in data or society. Tendency also fits what regularly happens under particular conditions, such as cloth shrinking in hot water.
habit. Describes a regular, learned or established behavior. A tendency can be a looser pattern, such as speaking quickly when nervous.
ja: predisposition は、ある行動や発症につながりやすい性向・素因があらかじめあることに焦点を置く。tendency は、観察されたパターンを述べるだけでも使える。
trend は、データや社会で時間とともに進む大きな変化を表すことが多い。tendency は、高温で洗うと生地が縮みやすいといった、一定の条件下で繰り返し起きることにも使う。
habit は、身についた習慣や癖を指す。tendency は、緊張したときに早口になりやすいといった、特定の状況で現れやすい傾向にも使う。

note.en: A close equivalent for a personal leaning or preference.
note.ja: 個人の性向や好みを述べるときの近い言い換え。

note.en: A close equivalent when describing a wider direction of change.
note.ja: 社会やデータの全体的な変化を述べるときの近い言い換え。

etymology.en: From Medieval Latin tendentia, related to Latin tendere ‘to stretch, direct, or aim’. The verb tend comes from the same source.
etymology.ja: 中世ラテン語 tendentia に由来し、ラテン語 tendere（伸ばす、向ける）と関係がある。動詞 tend も同じラテン語にさかのぼる。

en: have a tendency to exaggerate
show a tendency toward caution
a natural tendency to avoid conflict
a growing tendency to work remotely
a worrying tendency to overlook small errors
a tendency for prices to rise
ja: have a tendency to exaggerate — 大げさに言いがちである
show a tendency toward caution — 慎重になりがちな傾向を示す
a natural tendency to avoid conflict — 対立を避けがちな性向
a growing tendency to work remotely — リモートで働く人が増える傾向
a worrying tendency to overlook small errors — 小さなミスを見落としがちという、気がかりな傾向
a tendency for prices to rise — 価格が上がりやすい傾向

en: I have a tendency to speak too quickly when I’m nervous.
This fabric has a tendency to shrink in hot water.
In this market, there is a tendency for prices to rise before the holidays.
There is a growing tendency among applicants to file their documents electronically.
ja: I have a tendency to speak too quickly when I’m nervous. — 緊張すると、つい早口になってしまう。
This fabric has a tendency to shrink in hot water. — この生地は高温のお湯で洗うと縮みやすい。
In this market, there is a tendency for prices to rise before the holidays. — この市場では、休暇シーズンの前に価格が上がりやすい。
There is a growing tendency among applicants to file their documents electronically. — 出願人の間では、書類を電子的に提出する傾向が強まっている。

grammar.transitivity: intransitive for tendencies; transitive or intransitive for care

usage.complement: After tend, to can introduce an infinitive (tend to forget, meaning ‘often forget’) or a noun phrase (tend to a wound, meaning ‘care for a wound’). The form of the complement helps distinguish the meanings.
usage.negation: Tend not to reply describes a pattern of usually not replying. Don’t tend to reply is also common.

en: to often do something or be likely to behave or happen in a particular way
to move or lean in a particular direction, literally or figuratively
to look after someone or something, or give something the attention it needs
ja: ～しがちである、～する傾向がある、～しやすい
ある方向に向かう、ある立場・性質に傾く
世話をする、手入れをする、必要な処置をする

nuance.en: Tend to is a natural way to express a pattern without making an absolute claim. It works for personal habits, general observations, and tentative judgments, as in I tend to agree. In the care sense, tend often suggests active attention or upkeep, as with a garden, fire, or wound.
nuance.ja: tend to do は、例外もありうる傾向を述べるときに自然な形。個人の癖や一般的な傾向に加え、I tend to agree. のように「どちらかというと同意します」と判断を少し控えめに伝えることもできる。世話をする意味では、庭・火・傷などを実際に手入れしたり処置したりする場面で使う。

en: usually. Focuses on how often something happens. Tend to presents it as a general pattern or inclination and also works in phrases such as I tend to agree.
have a tendency to. A longer noun-based expression with a similar meaning. Tend to is often the simpler choice, while tendency allows modifiers such as a growing tendency.
take care of. A broader everyday expression for looking after someone or dealing with something. Tend is especially natural when describing hands-on care or upkeep.
ja: usually は頻度に焦点がある。tend to は一般的な傾向として述べる表現で、I tend to agree. のように意見を控えめに示すときにも使える。
have a tendency to は、名詞 tendency を使った同じような意味の表現。tend to のほうが簡潔で、名詞を使うと a growing tendency（強まりつつある傾向）のように修飾しやすい。
take care of は、世話や用事の処理まで幅広く表す日常語。tend は、庭の手入れや傷の処置など、手をかけて世話をする場面によく合う。

note.en: A close alternative for a personal leaning, especially with agree or think.
note.ja: agree や think などと合わせて、考えがある方向に傾いていることを表す言い換え。

note.en: An everyday alternative in the care sense.
note.ja: 世話をする意味での日常的な言い換え。

etymology.en: The tendency sense comes via Old French tendre from Latin tendere ‘to stretch, direct’. The care sense developed as a shortening of attend.
etymology.ja: 「傾向がある」の用法は、古フランス語 tendre を経てラテン語 tendere（伸ばす、向ける）に由来する。「世話をする」の用法は attend の短縮形から発達した。

equivalents.de: dazu neigen / pflegen / sich kümmern um

en: tend to agree
tend to overlook details
tend not to reply immediately
tend toward caution
tend a garden
tend a fire
tend to a wound
tend to someone’s needs
ja: tend to agree — どちらかというと同意する
tend to overlook details — 細かい点を見落としがちだ
tend not to reply immediately — すぐには返信しない傾向がある
tend toward caution — 慎重な考え方に傾く
tend a garden — 庭の手入れをする
tend a fire — 火の番をする
tend to a wound — 傷の手当てをする
tend to someone’s needs — 人が必要とすることに気を配る

en: Applicants tend to submit requests close to the deadline.
I tend to agree with your reading of that clause.
My father tends the garden every morning.
A nurse tended to his wound while we waited for the doctor.
ja: Applicants tend to submit requests close to the deadline. — 出願人は期限間際に申請することが多い。
I tend to agree with your reading of that clause. — その条項の解釈については、どちらかといえば私もあなたと同じ考えです。
My father tends the garden every morning. — 父は毎朝、庭の手入れをする。
A nurse tended to his wound while we waited for the doctor. — 医師を待つ間、看護師が彼の傷を手当てした。

usage.subject: In the active form, the subject names a factor, such as prior experience. The object names the person affected. In the passive form, the person becomes the subject.
usage.complement: To can be a preposition (predisposed to injury or to developing a condition) or an infinitive marker (predisposed to trust familiar sources).

en: to make someone more inclined to think, feel, or behave in a particular way
to make someone more susceptible to a disease, injury, or other condition
ja: 人をある考え方・感じ方・行動に傾きやすくする
人を病気やけがなどにかかりやすくする、発症や負傷の可能性を高める

nuance.en: A formal verb that highlights a factor already in place that makes an outcome more likely. A predisposition can come from prior experience, circumstances, or biological factors. Predisposed describes an inclination or susceptibility and leaves the outcome open.
nuance.ja: ある行動や結果が起きやすくなる背景の要因に焦点を置く、改まった動詞。過去の経験、環境、生物学的要因などを主語にできる。be predisposed は性向や素因があることを述べ、実際にその結果が生じるかどうかは文脈に委ねる。

en: tend to. Describes what someone often does or what commonly happens. Predispose highlights a factor that makes the outcome more likely.
cause. Attributes an outcome to a factor. Predispose describes an increase in likelihood or susceptibility.
be prone to. Describes someone or something as liable to experience a problem. Predispose can name the factor responsible for that susceptibility.
ja: tend to は、よく取る行動や起こりがちなことを述べる。predispose は、その行動や結果が起きやすくなる背景の要因に焦点を置く。
cause は、ある要因が結果を引き起こすことを表す。predispose は、その結果が生じやすくなることを表す。
be prone to は、問題が生じやすいことを述べる。predispose を能動態で使うと、何がその起こりやすさにつながるかを主語で示せる。

note.en: A close alternative for a factor that makes someone lean toward a view or action.
note.ja: 人をある見方や行動に傾かせる意味での近い言い換え。

note.en: A plain-language alternative when referring to illness or injury.
note.ja: 病気やけがへのかかりやすさを表す場合の平易な言い換え。

etymology.en: Formed with pre- ‘before’ and dispose ‘incline’. Its history may involve French prédisposer or a back-formation from predisposition.
etymology.ja: pre-（前もって）と dispose（気持ちを傾ける）から成る。フランス語 prédisposer の影響や、名詞 predisposition から動詞が作られた可能性がある。

equivalents.de: zu etwas geneigt machen / für etwas anfälliger machen

en: predispose someone to injury
predispose someone to trust familiar sources
be predisposed to infection
be genetically predisposed to a condition
be predisposed to developing a condition
a predisposing factor
ja: predispose someone to injury — 人がけがをしやすくなる要因となる
predispose someone to trust familiar sources — 人がなじみのある情報源を信頼しやすくなる要因となる
be predisposed to infection — 感染しやすい素因がある
be genetically predisposed to a condition — ある病気や症状が生じやすい遺伝的素因がある
be predisposed to developing a condition — ある病気や症状が生じやすい
a predisposing factor — 発症などを起こしやすくする要因

en: Years of reviewing patent applications predisposed her to look for gaps in the evidence.
A previous ankle injury can predispose an athlete to further injury.
The researchers asked whether some participants were genetically predisposed to developing asthma.
ja: Years of reviewing patent applications predisposed her to look for gaps in the evidence. — 長年にわたって特許出願を審査した経験から、彼女は証拠の穴を探す傾向が身についた。
A previous ankle injury can predispose an athlete to further injury. — 足首をけがしたことがあると、選手は再びけがをしやすくなることがある。
The researchers asked whether some participants were genetically predisposed to developing asthma. — 研究者らは、一部の参加者に喘息を発症しやすい遺伝的素因があったかどうかを調べた。

usage.tone: Often disapproving. With architecture or décor it can evoke impressive scale, sometimes with a suggestion of excess.

en: impressive in intention or scale but excessive, showy, or impractical
very imposing or elaborate in appearance, often in a showy way
ja: 大げさな、仰々しい、規模が大きすぎて現実味に欠ける
壮大で威圧感のある、華美な（建物や内装など）

nuance.en: Grandiose often signals skepticism about the scale, practicality, or self-importance of a plan or claim. A grandiose scheme can sound impressive on paper and be hard to carry out. In descriptions of buildings, the word can emphasize monumentality and may suggest ostentation.
nuance.ja: 計画や主張について使うと、規模が大きすぎる、実現性が乏しい、自分を大きく見せようとしている、といった話し手の批判的な見方が出やすい。建物の描写では、堂々とした規模を表し、文脈によっては見せびらかすような華美さもにじむ。

en: grand. Often expresses admiration for impressive scale or appearance. Grandiose often suggests that the scale or display is excessive.
ambitious. Emphasizes a demanding goal and can convey approval. Grandiose often casts doubt on whether the goal is realistic.
pretentious. Focuses on trying to appear more important or sophisticated. Grandiose often highlights excessive scale or scope.
ja: grand は規模の大きさや外観の立派さを好意的に述べることが多い。grandiose には、規模や見せ方が度を越しているという響きが出やすい。
ambitious は達成の難しい高い目標に焦点があり、肯定的にも使える。grandiose は、その目標に現実味があるか疑う響きが出やすい。
pretentious は、実際以上に立派・洗練されているように見せようとする態度に焦点がある。grandiose は、計画や見せ方の規模の大きさに焦点が来やすい。

note.en: A close alternative for inflated claims or an excessive style.
note.ja: 誇張された主張や大げさな文体を表す近い言い換え。

note.en: Emphasizes conspicuous display in décor or lifestyle.
note.ja: 内装や暮らしぶりで富や華やかさをことさらに見せることを強調する。

etymology.en: From French grandiose, from Italian grandioso, based on grande ‘large, grand’, ultimately from Latin grandis.
etymology.ja: フランス語 grandiose を経て、イタリア語 grandioso（壮大な）に由来する。イタリア語 grande（大きい、壮大な）はラテン語 grandis にさかのぼる。

en: a grandiose scheme
grandiose plans for expansion
a grandiose vision
grandiose claims
grandiose promises
a grandiose building
sound grandiose
ja: a grandiose scheme — 大風呂敷を広げた計画
grandiose plans for expansion — 現実味に欠けるほど大がかりな拡張計画
a grandiose vision — 壮大で実現性の乏しい構想
grandiose claims — 大げさな主張
grandiose promises — 大げさな約束
a grandiose building — 壮麗で威圧感のある建物
sound grandiose — 仰々しく聞こえる

en: They announced a grandiose plan to turn the old station into a luxury hotel, but they had yet to secure funding.
The company made grandiose claims about its software before it had a working prototype.
The hotel lobby was grandiose, with marble columns and a chandelier the size of a small car.
ja: They announced a grandiose plan to turn the old station into a luxury hotel, but they had yet to secure funding. — 彼らは旧駅舎を高級ホテルに改装するという大がかりな構想を発表したが、資金のめどはまだ立っていなかった。
The company made grandiose claims about its software before it had a working prototype. — その会社は、動く試作品もできていないうちから、ソフトウェアについて大げさな宣伝をしていた。
The hotel lobby was grandiose, with marble columns and a chandelier the size of a small car. — ホテルのロビーは仰々しいほど豪華で、大理石の柱が並び、小型車ほどもあるシャンデリアが下がっていた。

usage.article: Use an before ambitious when it precedes a singular countable noun, as in an ambitious project.
usage.for: Ambitious for their children means they want their children to succeed.

en: strongly motivated to achieve success or reach a high position
aiming high and requiring substantial effort, time, or resources to succeed
ja: 向上心がある、成功したいという気持ちが強い、野心的な（人）
目標が高く、実現に大きな努力・時間・資源を要する、意欲的な（計画など）

nuance.en: Ambitious can praise a person's drive or a project's high aims. With a person, the tone can become critical if the context suggests an excessive pursuit of status or power. With a target or deadline, overly ambitious makes clear that the speaker thinks it is too demanding.
nuance.ja: 人については向上心を、計画については目標の高さを肯定的に述べるときにも使える。地位や権力への執着がにじむ文脈なら、人について「野心的な」と訳せる。目標や締切について overly ambitious と言えば、要求水準が高すぎるという評価が明確になる。

en: grandiose. Suggests excessive scale, showiness, or a lack of realism. Ambitious can convey approval of a demanding but achievable goal.
driven. Highlights the strong inner motivation that keeps a person working toward something. Ambitious also describes the plan or goal itself.
challenging. Emphasizes difficulty for the people involved. Ambitious emphasizes the height or scope of what someone is trying to achieve.
ja: grandiose は、規模が大きすぎる、見せ方が仰々しい、現実味に欠けるといった響きが出やすい。ambitious は、難しくても達成可能な高い目標を評価するときにも使える。
driven は、人を行動へと駆り立てる強い意欲を表す。ambitious は人に加え、計画や目標そのものにも使える。
challenging は、取り組む人にとっての難しさに焦点がある。ambitious は、達成しようとする目標の高さや計画の規模に焦点がある。

note.en: A close alternative for a highly motivated person.
note.ja: 強い意欲を持つ人を表す場合の近い言い換え。

note.en: Useful when naming the role someone hopes to attain, as in an aspiring writer.
note.ja: an aspiring writer（作家志望の人）のように、目指している職業や立場を明示するときに使える。

etymology.en: From Old French ambitieux or Latin ambitiosus, from ambitio ‘canvassing for votes’, related to ambire ‘to go around’.
etymology.ja: 古フランス語 ambitieux またはラテン語 ambitiosus に由来する。ラテン語 ambitio は「票を求めて回ること」を指し、ambire（回って歩く）と関係がある。

en: an ambitious young lawyer
a fiercely ambitious manager
set an ambitious target
an ambitious reform plan
an ambitious timetable
overly ambitious
ambitious in scope
be ambitious for one’s children
ja: an ambitious young lawyer — 向上心のある若手弁護士
a fiercely ambitious manager — 強い野心を持つ管理職
set an ambitious target — 高い目標を設定する
an ambitious reform plan — 意欲的な改革案
an ambitious timetable — 達成の難しい工程表
overly ambitious — 目標を高く設定しすぎた
ambitious in scope — 対象範囲が広く意欲的な
be ambitious for one’s children — 子どもの成功を強く願う

en: She’s ambitious and hopes to lead the firm’s international practice one day.
The team set an ambitious target of cutting review time in half within a year.
Finishing by Friday was overly ambitious given the amount of work left.
Her parents were ambitious for her, but she wanted to choose her own career.
ja: She’s ambitious and hopes to lead the firm’s international practice one day. — 彼女は向上心があり、いずれ事務所の国際業務を率いたいと思っている。
The team set an ambitious target of cutting review time in half within a year. — チームは、1年以内にレビュー所要時間を半分にするという高い目標を掲げた。
Finishing by Friday was overly ambitious given the amount of work left. — 残っている作業量を考えると、金曜までに終えるという目標は無理があった。
Her parents were ambitious for her, but she wanted to choose her own career. — 両親は彼女の成功を強く願っていたが、彼女は自分で進路を決めたかった。

grammar.transitivity: intransitive for an engine; transitive when making something inactive

usage.equipment: An idle machine is currently unused or doing no work. An idling engine is still running at low speed.
usage.away: Use idle the afternoon away or idle away the afternoon. With a pronoun, use idle it away.

en: not working, in use, or engaged in activity (adjective)
not seriously meant, aimless, or lacking a factual basis, depending on the noun (adjective)
to run at low speed without driving a vehicle or doing useful work, of an engine (intransitive verb)
to make a facility or equipment inactive, or to pass time without much activity in idle away (transitive verb)
ja: 稼働していない、使われていない、手が空いている（形容詞）
本気でない、これといった目的がない、根拠がない（形容詞）
エンジンがアイドリングする、空転する（自動詞）
設備を休止させる。また idle away で、時間を何となく過ごす（他動詞）

nuance.en: Idle can describe a temporary state. Idle staff may simply have no work to do, though calling someone idle can also criticize them as lazy. Idle curiosity suggests curiosity with no practical purpose. An idle threat is one the speaker is unlikely to carry out, and idle speculation lacks a solid basis.
nuance.ja: idle は一時的に仕事や用途がない状態にも使える。idle staff は仕事が回ってこず手が空いている人を指すこともあるが、人については「怠けている」という批判にもなる。idle curiosity は「ただの好奇心」、idle threat は「実行する気のない脅し」、idle speculation は「根拠の乏しい憶測」。

en: idle / lazy. Idle can describe a person's current inactivity. Lazy judges the person's willingness to make an effort.
idle / dormant. Idle often describes something temporarily unused, such as a spare machine. Dormant suggests inactivity over a period, with the possibility of activity later.
idle / idling. An idle production line is doing no production work. An idling engine is running at low speed without driving the vehicle.
ja: idle は、そのとき何もしていない状態にも使える。lazy は努力する気がないという評価を含む。
idle は、予備の機械などが一時的に使われていない状態によく使う。dormant は、活動がしばらく休止していて、後に再開する可能性を連想させる。
an idle production line は稼働していない生産ライン。an idling engine は、車を走らせずに低い回転数で回っているエンジン。

note.en: A close alternative for something temporarily doing no work.
note.ja: 一時的に活動・稼働していない場合の近い言い換え。

note.en: A close alternative in an empty threat or an empty promise.
note.ja: an empty threat（実行する気のない脅し）や an empty promise（口先だけの約束）で使える。

etymology.en: From Old English īdel ‘empty, useless’, of West Germanic origin. German eitel is related.
etymology.ja: 西ゲルマン系の古英語 īdel（空の、役に立たない）に由来する。ドイツ語 eitel は同系語。

en: sit idle
leave equipment idle
idle a production line
leave the engine idling
an idle threat
out of idle curiosity
idle speculation
idle away the afternoon
ja: sit idle — 使われずにある、何もせずにいる
leave equipment idle — 機器を使わないままにしておく
idle a production line — 生産ラインを休止させる
leave the engine idling — エンジンをアイドリングさせたままにする
an idle threat — 実行する気のない脅し
out of idle curiosity — ただの好奇心から
idle speculation — 根拠の乏しい憶測
idle away the afternoon — 午後をぶらぶらして過ごす

en: The printing press sat idle for a week while we waited for a replacement part.
The driver left the engine idling while she waited outside the hotel.
I asked out of idle curiosity how much the old watch had cost.
We idled away the afternoon in a café by the river.
ja: The printing press sat idle for a week while we waited for a replacement part. — 交換部品を待つ間、印刷機は1週間稼働しなかった。
The driver left the engine idling while she waited outside the hotel. — 運転手はホテルの外で待つ間、エンジンをアイドリングさせたままにしていた。
I asked out of idle curiosity how much the old watch had cost. — ほんの好奇心から、その古い腕時計はいくらだったのかと尋ねた。
We idled away the afternoon in a café by the river. — 川沿いのカフェで、午後をのんびり過ごした。

usage.countability: Use a period of idleness to count a stretch of time.
usage.tone: Enforced idleness emphasizes that circumstances kept someone from working or being active. Out of sheer idleness usually criticizes a lack of effort.

en: the state of doing no work, being inactive, or being out of use
a lack of willingness to work or make an effort (disapproving)
ja: 仕事や活動をしていない状態、無為、設備などが使われていない状態
怠惰、怠け（非難を込めた用法）

nuance.en: Idleness can describe inactivity imposed by circumstances, such as a factory shutdown, or time spent doing very little by choice. It can also imply blame, especially when used to explain why someone failed to do something. The surrounding words help establish the tone.
nuance.ja: 工場の休止などで何もできない状態にも、自分から何もせずに過ごす時間にも使える。やるべきことをしなかった理由として使うと、「怠け」という非難がこもりやすい。日本語では、何が原因で活動していないかに応じて訳し分ける。

en: laziness. Criticizes an unwillingness to make an effort. Idleness can describe the state of being inactive regardless of the reason.
inactivity. A broadly neutral term for a lack of activity. Idleness can bring to mind people with nothing to do or equipment sitting unused.
leisure. Focuses on time available away from work or obligations, including time spent on active hobbies. Idleness focuses on doing little or nothing.
ja: laziness は、努力をしたがらないことへの批判を含む。idleness は、事情があって活動できない状態にも使える。
inactivity は活動がないことを中立的に述べる語。idleness は、手持ち無沙汰な人や、使われずに置かれた設備を連想させることがある。
leisure は仕事や用事から離れた自由時間で、趣味に打ち込む時間も含む。idleness は、何もせずに過ごすことに焦点がある。

note.en: A neutral equivalent for a period without activity or use.
note.ja: 活動や使用が途絶えた状態を中立的に表す言い換え。

note.en: A close equivalent when the context criticizes a lack of effort.
note.ja: 努力不足を非難する文脈での近い言い換え。

etymology.en: Formed from the adjective idle and the noun-forming suffix -ness.
etymology.ja: 形容詞 idle に、状態や性質を表す名詞を作る接尾辞 -ness が付いた語。

equivalents.de: der Müßiggang / die Untätigkeit / die Faulheit
equivalents.es: la inactividad / la ociosidad / la pereza

en: a period of idleness
months of idleness
enforced idleness
out of sheer idleness
a little idleness
return to work after a period of idleness
ja: a period of idleness — 仕事や活動をしていない期間
months of idleness — 何か月もの休止
enforced idleness — 事情があって働いたり活動したりできない状態
out of sheer idleness — ただ怠けて
a little idleness — 少しのんびり何もせずに過ごすこと
return to work after a period of idleness — しばらく仕事を離れた後で復帰する

en: After months of idleness, the old printing press was finally back in use.
The musicians grew restless during the weeks of enforced idleness after the tour was cancelled.
I put off replying to the email out of sheer idleness.
A little idleness on a Sunday afternoon can be surprisingly restorative.
ja: After months of idleness, the old printing press was finally back in use. — 何か月も使われていなかった古い印刷機が、ようやくまた稼働した。
The musicians grew restless during the weeks of enforced idleness after the tour was cancelled. — ツアーが中止になり、何週間も活動できずにいるうちに、演奏家たちは落ち着かなくなった。
I put off replying to the email out of sheer idleness. — ただ面倒くさがって、メールの返信を先延ばしにした。
A little idleness on a Sunday afternoon can be surprisingly restorative. — 日曜の午後を少し何もせずに過ごすと、思いのほか疲れが取れることがある。

grammar.countability: uncountable in the usual emotion sense

usage.prepositions: To my astonishment introduces the unexpected thing that happened. In astonishment describes how someone reacted. At introduces the source of the feeling, as in astonishment at the result.

en: a feeling of very great surprise at something unexpected or hard to believe
ja: 予想外のことに強く驚く気持ち、驚愕、びっくりすること

nuance.en: Astonishment conveys stronger surprise than surprise alone and often works well in narrative. The reaction can be delighted, troubled, or simply incredulous. To my astonishment frames what follows as contrary to the speaker’s expectations.
nuance.ja: 普通の surprise より強い驚きを表し、出来事とその反応を描く文によく合う。うれしい驚き、困惑を伴う驚き、にわかには信じられない気持ちのいずれにも使える。To my astonishment, ～ と置くと、後に続く出来事が自分の予想を外れたことを示せる。

en: surprise. The general word for a reaction to the unexpected. It also refers to the unexpected event itself in a phrase such as a pleasant surprise.
amazement. A close equivalent, often with a sense of wonder. Astonishment often highlights how unexpected or hard to believe something is.
shock. Often suggests distress or a severe emotional jolt. Astonishment also fits happy or amusing surprises.
ja: surprise は予想外のことへの反応を広く表す。a pleasant surprise のように、予想外の出来事そのものも指せる。astonishment は強い驚きという感情に焦点がある。
amazement は近い意味で、感嘆を伴うことも多い。astonishment は、出来事があまりに意外で信じがたいという面を強調しやすい。
shock は動揺や強い精神的衝撃を表すことが多い。astonishment は、うれしいことやおかしなことに強く驚いた場合にも使える。

note.en: A close alternative for a feeling of very great surprise.
note.ja: とても強く驚く気持ちを表す近い言い換え。

note.en: A straightforward alternative that keeps the intensity.
note.ja: 驚きの強さを保った平易な言い換え。

etymology.en: Formed from astonish and the suffix -ment. Astonish is historically related to Old French estoner ‘to stun or daze’.
etymology.ja: astonish（びっくりさせる）に名詞を作る接尾辞 -ment が付いた形。astonish は古フランス語 estoner（ぼう然とさせる）にさかのぼる。

en: to my astonishment
to everyone’s utter astonishment
stare in astonishment
gasp in astonishment
express astonishment at the result
hide one’s astonishment
a look of astonishment
ja: to my astonishment — 驚いたことに
to everyone’s utter astonishment — 誰もが仰天したことに
stare in astonishment — びっくりして見つめる
gasp in astonishment — 驚いて息をのむ
express astonishment at the result — 結果に驚きを示す
hide one’s astonishment — 驚きを隠す
a look of astonishment — 驚いた表情

en: To my astonishment, the watch was still ticking after decades in a drawer.
We watched in astonishment as the pianist started playing the piece again, this time with one hand.
She couldn't hide her astonishment at how quickly the negotiations had ended.
ja: To my astonishment, the watch was still ticking after decades in a drawer. — 驚いたことに、その腕時計は何十年も引き出しに入っていたのに、まだ時を刻んでいた。
We watched in astonishment as the pianist started playing the piece again, this time with one hand. — ピアニストがその曲を今度は片手で弾き始めたので、私たちは驚いて見入った。
She couldn't hide her astonishment at how quickly the negotiations had ended. — 交渉があまりに早く終わったので、彼女は驚きを隠せなかった。

patterns: It astonishes + someone + that / how + clause
What astonishes + someone + is + noun / clause

usage.subject: The thing that causes the surprise is the subject in the active voice. The person who feels it is the object.
usage.participles: Astonished describes the person’s reaction. Astonishing describes what causes that reaction.

en: to surprise someone very greatly, often because something is unexpected or hard to believe
ja: 人をひどく驚かせる、びっくりさせる、仰天させる

nuance.en: Astonish signals a strong reaction and often focuses on how unexpected or hard to believe the cause is. It can describe an impressive achievement or a disturbing discovery. It still astonishes me how … is useful when the same fact continues to seem remarkable.
nuance.ja: surprise より強い反応を表し、予想外だったことや、にわかには信じがたいことによく使う。見事な成果にも、困惑するような発見にも使える。It still astonishes me how … は、今でも驚くほどだと感じる事実を述べるのに使える。

en: surprise. The general verb for making someone react to the unexpected. Astonish signals a more intense reaction.
amaze. A close equivalent that often suggests admiration or wonder. Astonish often emphasizes how unexpected something is.
startle. Often describes a sudden reaction to an immediate stimulus, such as a loud noise. Astonish fits a striking fact or outcome even when the surprise unfolds slowly.
ja: surprise は「驚かせる」を広く表す一般的な動詞。astonish は反応の強さを伝える。
amaze は意味が近く、感心や感嘆を伴うことも多い。astonish は予想を大きく外れたことに焦点が当たりやすい。
startle は、大きな物音などに思わずびくっとする反応によく使う。astonish は、徐々に明らかになった事実や結果への強い驚きにも使える。

note.en: A close alternative for making someone feel great surprise or wonder.
note.ja: 人を強く驚かせたり感嘆させたりする場合の近い言い換え。

note.en: An emphatic alternative for very strong surprise.
note.ja: 非常に強い驚きを表す言い換え。

etymology.en: From Middle English astonien, via Old French estoner ‘to stun or daze’, ultimately related to Latin tonare ‘to thunder’.
etymology.ja: 中英語 astonien と古フランス語 estoner（ぼう然とさせる）を経て、ラテン語 tonare（雷が鳴る）にさかのぼる。

en: astonish the audience
astonish even the experts
It still astonishes me how …
be astonished at the result
be astonished by the accuracy
be astonished to hear the news
an astonishing discovery
ja: astonish the audience — 観客を驚かせる
astonish even the experts — 専門家までも驚かせる
It still astonishes me how … — どれほど～なのか、今でも驚く。
be astonished at the result — 結果に仰天する
be astonished by the accuracy — 精度に驚く
be astonished to hear the news — その知らせを聞いてびっくりする
an astonishing discovery — 驚くべき発見

en: The judges were astonished by how well the youngest contestant played.
It still astonishes me that the watch keeps such accurate time after all these years.
The speed of the recovery astonished even the doctors.
I was astonished to learn that the missing manuscript had been in the library all along.
ja: The judges were astonished by how well the youngest contestant played. — 最年少の出場者の演奏があまりに見事で、審査員たちは驚いた。
It still astonishes me that the watch keeps such accurate time after all these years. — 長い年月がたった今も、その腕時計がこれほど正確に時を刻むことには驚かされる。
The speed of the recovery astonished even the doctors. — 回復の早さには、医師たちさえ驚いた。
I was astonished to learn that the missing manuscript had been in the library all along. — 行方不明だった原稿がずっと図書館にあったと知って、びっくりした。

usage.participles: Astonishing describes what causes the surprise. Astonished describes the person who feels it. The result was astonishing, so we were astonished.
usage.emphasis: Use absolutely, utterly, or truly to emphasize the surprise. Before a number, astonishing draws attention to how unexpected the figure is.

en: so surprising that it is difficult to believe or far beyond what was expected
ja: 驚くべき、びっくりするほどの、にわかには信じがたい

nuance.en: Astonishing emphasizes the strength of the surprise. It can express admiration for an exceptional achievement, disbelief at a high price, or disapproval of a serious oversight. The context determines how the speaker judges what happened.
nuance.ja: 驚きの大きさを強調する。見事な成果への感嘆、高額な値段への驚き、重大な見落としへのあきれなどに使える。何に驚いているかによって、話し手の評価が決まる。

en: surprising. The general word for something unexpected. Astonishing makes the force of the surprise much stronger.
amazing. Often expresses admiration or casual praise. Astonishing puts more emphasis on how hard a fact or result is to believe.
astonished. Describes the reaction of the person experiencing surprise. Astonishing describes what brings about the reaction.
ja: surprising は「予想外の」を広く表す。astonishing は、驚きの大きさを強く伝える。
amazing は感嘆やくだけた称賛にもよく使う。astonishing は、事実や結果がにわかには信じがたいほどだったことを強調しやすい。
astonished は驚いた人の反応、astonishing はその驚きを引き起こす事柄を表す。

note.en: A close equivalent for an exceptionally surprising scale or outcome.
note.ja: 規模や結果が並外れて驚くべき場合の近い言い換え。

note.en: A useful alternative when something deserves notice or admiration.
note.ja: 注目に値するものや感心するようなものを表すときに使える。

etymology.en: The present participle of astonish, used as an adjective. Astonish goes back to Old French estoner ‘to stun or daze’.
etymology.ja: astonish（ひどく驚かせる）の現在分詞が形容詞になった語。astonish は古フランス語 estoner（ぼう然とさせる）にさかのぼる。

en: an astonishing achievement
an astonishing figure
at an astonishing rate
with astonishing accuracy
absolutely astonishing
It’s astonishing how …
find it astonishing that …
ja: an astonishing achievement — 驚くべき成果
an astonishing figure — 驚くべき数字
at an astonishing rate — 驚くほどの速さで
with astonishing accuracy — 驚くほど正確に
absolutely astonishing — 本当に驚くべき
It’s astonishing how … — どれほど～なのか、驚くばかりだ。
find it astonishing that … — ～ということにひどく驚く。

en: It’s astonishing how accurately this mechanical watch still keeps time.
The painting sold for an astonishing three million euros.
I find it astonishing that nobody checked the figures before publishing the report.
ja: It’s astonishing how accurately this mechanical watch still keeps time. — この機械式時計が今でもこれほど正確に時を刻むとは、驚きだ。
The painting sold for an astonishing three million euros. — その絵は、なんと300万ユーロで売れた。
I find it astonishing that nobody checked the figures before publishing the report. — 報告書を公表する前に誰も数字を確認しなかったとは、驚きだ。

usage.tone: Often disapproving, especially when seriousness or good judgment is expected. It can also be playful when describing a small indulgence.
usage.legal: In legal writing, the adjective commonly modifies claim, lawsuit, motion, or appeal.

en: silly or lacking seriousness when seriousness is expected
lacking a serious or useful purpose, especially when judged an unnecessary use of time or money
lacking a reasonably arguable basis in law or fact, as said of a claim or other filing (legal)
ja: 軽薄な、ふざけた、真剣さに欠ける
これといった目的のない、無駄な、取るに足らない
法的または事実上、まともに争いうる根拠を欠く（請求や申立てなどについて）

nuance.en: Frivolous usually conveys the speaker’s judgment that something deserves less time, money, or attention than it is getting, or that someone is treating a serious matter too lightly. In legal English it can be a strong assessment of the basis for a claim or filing. In a phrase like a frivolous little purchase, the tone can be affectionate or self-deprecating.
nuance.ja: 多くの場合、時間やお金をかけるほどのことではない、あるいは真剣に扱うべきことを軽く扱っている、という評価がこもる。法律英語では、請求や申立ての根拠を欠くという強い評価になりうる。a frivolous little purchase のように、自分のちょっとした無駄遣いを冗談めかして言うこともある。

en: trivial. Emphasizes small importance. Frivolous can also criticize the way someone spends time or money or treats a serious subject.
lighthearted. Suggests a cheerful, relaxed tone and is often approving. Frivolous can suggest that the levity is misplaced.
meritless. Describes a claim that lacks merit. Frivolous in legal use commonly implies the stronger judgment that there is no reasonably arguable basis for it.
ja: trivial は重要性が低いことに焦点がある。frivolous は、時間やお金の使い方や、深刻な話題を軽く扱う態度にも批判を込められる。
lighthearted は明るく気楽な調子を表し、好意的に使える。frivolous は、その軽さが場違いだという含みが出やすい。
meritless は請求や主張に理由がないことを表す。法律英語の frivolous は、そもそも合理的に争いうる根拠を欠く、という強い評価を示すことが多い。

note.en: A close alternative for remarks that treat a serious subject too casually.
note.ja: 深刻な話題を軽く扱う発言に使える近い言い換え。

note.en: A close alternative when the main point is a lack of factual or legal support.
note.ja: 事実上または法的な裏付けの欠如に焦点を置く場合の近い言い換え。

etymology.en: From Latin frivolus ‘silly, trifling’, with the English adjective suffix -ous.
etymology.ja: ラテン語 frivolus（くだらない、取るに足らない）に由来し、形容詞の接尾辞 -ous を含む。

en: a frivolous remark
frivolous spending
a frivolous purchase
frivolous entertainment
a frivolous claim
a frivolous appeal
dismiss a motion as frivolous
ja: a frivolous remark — 軽薄な発言
frivolous spending — 無駄遣い
a frivolous purchase — つい買った余計なもの
frivolous entertainment — 気晴らし程度の娯楽
a frivolous claim — 合理的に争いうる根拠を欠く請求
a frivolous appeal — 明らかに根拠を欠く上訴
dismiss a motion as frivolous — 根拠がないとして申立てを退ける

en: His frivolous remarks irritated colleagues who were trying to discuss the safety concerns.
I’m trying to cut back on frivolous purchases, but I couldn’t resist that vintage watch.
The court dismissed the claim as frivolous because it had no arguable legal basis.
