awareness: The everyday choice for knowing about a specific issue, as in raise awareness of online fraud. Consciousness can also refer to subjective experience or shared social awareness.
conscience: Your inner sense of right and wrong. Follow your conscience means to act according to what you believe is right.
ja: conscious：「意識がある、自覚している」という形容詞。She regained consciousness. は意識を取り戻したという変化、She was conscious again. は再び意識がある状態を表す。
awareness：特定の問題を知ってもらうことなら、raise awareness of online fraud（ネット詐欺への注意を喚起する）のように使う。consciousness は主観的な経験や社会に共有される意識も表せる。
conscience：「良心」。follow your conscience は「自分が正しいと思うことに従って行動する」。

note.en: Close when the meaning is knowledge or recognition of an issue.
note.ja: 問題への認識や自覚という意味で近い。

etymology.en: Formed from the adjective conscious and the noun-forming suffix -ness, which denotes a state or quality.
etymology.ja: 形容詞 conscious に、状態や性質を表す名詞をつくる接尾辞 -ness が付いた語。

en: lose consciousness
regain consciousness
drift in and out of consciousness
a state of consciousness
human consciousness
consciousness of one’s own limitations
social consciousness
enter the public consciousness
raise consciousness about an issue
stream of consciousness
ja: lose consciousness — 意識を失う
regain consciousness — 意識を取り戻す
drift in and out of consciousness — 意識が戻ったり途切れたりする
a state of consciousness — 意識の状態
human consciousness — 人間の意識
consciousness of one’s own limitations — 自分の限界についての自覚
social consciousness — 社会問題への意識
enter the public consciousness — 広く世間に意識されるようになる
raise consciousness about an issue — ある問題への意識を高める
stream of consciousness — 意識の流れ、その流れを描く文学技法

en: She briefly lost consciousness and regained it a few seconds later.
The article asks how conscious experience arises and what it can tell us about human consciousness.
The issue entered the public consciousness after the documentary aired.
The campaign helped raise consciousness about barriers faced by people with disabilities.
ja: She briefly lost consciousness and regained it a few seconds later. — 彼女は一時的に意識を失い、数秒後に取り戻した。
The article asks how conscious experience arises and what it can tell us about human consciousness. — その記事は、意識的な経験がどのように生まれ、そこから人間の意識について何が分かるかを問うている。
The issue entered the public consciousness after the documentary aired. — そのドキュメンタリーの放送をきっかけに、その問題が広く世間に意識されるようになった。
The campaign helped raise consciousness about barriers faced by people with disabilities. — その運動は、障害のある人が直面する障壁への社会の意識を高める一助となった。

grammar.countability: uncountable as a noun, usually the unconscious

usage.state: Be unconscious describes a state. Knock someone unconscious means to cause someone to lose consciousness.
usage.awareness: Before a noun such as bias, it describes something that operates outside awareness. Be unconscious of is possible, but be unaware of is often more natural for simply not knowing something.
usage.noun: The unconscious is a term used in psychology and psychoanalysis.

en: (adjective) without consciousness
(adjective) occurring without awareness, or unaware of something
(noun) the part of mental life outside conscious awareness
ja: （形容詞）意識がない、気を失っている
（形容詞）無意識の、～に気づいていない
（名詞）無意識、意識に上らない心の領域

nuance.en: An unconscious person has no conscious awareness at that moment. An unconscious bias can influence a person who is awake and thinking. The adjective describes the bias as operating without the person noticing it.
nuance.ja: an unconscious person は「意識のない人」。unconscious bias は、本人の意識がはっきりしていても、本人が気づかないまま判断に影響する偏りを指す。

en: conscious: She was conscious again describes the state after regaining consciousness.
unaware: Use unaware of for ordinary lack of knowledge, as in I was unaware of the rule.
unintentional: Focuses on lack of intent. An unintentional error can happen even when you are fully aware of what you are doing.
ja: conscious：「意識がある」。She was conscious again. は「彼女は再び意識がある状態だった」。
unaware：単に何かを知らない場合は unaware of が自然。I was unaware of the rule. は「その規則を知らなかった」。
unintentional：「意図しない」。自分が何をしているか分かっていても、意図せず間違えることはある。

note.en: Close in the pattern unconscious of something.
note.ja: unconscious of ～ の「～に気づかない」という意味で近い。

etymology.en: Formed from the negative prefix un- and conscious.
etymology.ja: 否定を表す接頭辞 un- と conscious から成る。

en: be found unconscious
remain unconscious
knock someone unconscious
unconscious bias
an unconscious habit
unconscious of the effect
the unconscious
ja: be found unconscious — 意識を失った状態で発見される
remain unconscious — 意識が戻らない
knock someone unconscious — 人を気絶させる
unconscious bias — 無意識の偏見
an unconscious habit — 無意識の癖
unconscious of the effect — その影響に気づいていない
the unconscious — 無意識の領域

en: He was unconscious when they found him, but he regained consciousness a few minutes later.
Unconscious bias can affect how we assess job applicants.
Tapping my pen during meetings had become an unconscious habit.
The essay explores the role of the unconscious in dreams.
ja: He was unconscious when they found him, but he regained consciousness a few minutes later. — 発見されたとき彼には意識がなかったが、数分後に意識を取り戻した。
Unconscious bias can affect how we assess job applicants. — 無意識の偏見は、採用応募者の評価に影響することがある。
Tapping my pen during meetings had become an unconscious habit. — 会議中にペンをコツコツ鳴らすのが、無意識の癖になっていた。
The essay explores the role of the unconscious in dreams. — その論考は、夢において無意識が果たす役割を探っている。

patterns: a period / an episode of unconsciousness

usage.state: Use unconsciousness to name the state, especially when describing its duration or cause. For the change into that state, lose consciousness is a common choice.
usage.article: In a brief period of unconsciousness, the article a belongs to period.

en: the state of being unconscious, with no awareness of what is happening around you
ja: 意識がない状態、人が気を失っている状態

nuance.en: She lost consciousness marks the moment her awareness was lost. A brief period of unconsciousness refers to the time she spent in that state. In everyday speech, she was unconscious for a few seconds conveys that duration directly.
nuance.ja: She lost consciousness. は「意識を失った」という変化を表す。a brief period of unconsciousness は、その後「意識がなかった短い時間」を指す。日常会話なら She was unconscious for a few seconds.（数秒間、意識がなかった）とも言える。

en: unconscious: The adjective describes the person or their state, as in He was unconscious.
loss of consciousness: Often names the event of losing awareness, as in sudden loss of consciousness. Unconsciousness names the resulting state.
the unconscious: A psychological noun phrase for mental processes or contents outside conscious awareness.
ja: unconscious：形容詞。He was unconscious. のように、その人に意識がなかったことを述べる。
loss of consciousness：sudden loss of consciousness（突然の意識消失）のように、意識を失う出来事を指すことが多い。unconsciousness は意識がない状態そのものを指す。
the unconscious：心理学などで、意識に上らない心の働きや内容を指す「無意識」。

note.en: A plain-language way to refer to the same state.
note.ja: 同じ状態を平易に表す言い方。

etymology.en: Formed from unconscious and the noun-forming suffix -ness.
etymology.ja: 形容詞 unconscious に、状態や性質を表す名詞をつくる接尾辞 -ness が付いた語。

en: a brief period of unconsciousness
an episode of unconsciousness
prolonged unconsciousness
lapse into unconsciousness
a cause of unconsciousness
ja: a brief period of unconsciousness — 短時間、意識がなかったこと
an episode of unconsciousness — 意識を失っていた一時期
prolonged unconsciousness — 長時間にわたる意識消失
lapse into unconsciousness — 意識を失う
a cause of unconsciousness — 意識消失の原因

en: He regained consciousness after a brief period of unconsciousness.
The report noted a brief episode of unconsciousness after the fall.
In the novel, she lapses into unconsciousness before she can finish the sentence.
ja: He regained consciousness after a brief period of unconsciousness. — 彼は短時間意識を失っていたが、その後、意識を取り戻した。
The report noted a brief episode of unconsciousness after the fall. — 報告書には、転倒のあと短時間意識がなかったと記されていた。
In the novel, she lapses into unconsciousness before she can finish the sentence. — 小説の中で、彼女は言い終える前に意識を失う。

usage.beforeNoun: Before a noun, proper can mean suitable, genuine, or substantial enough to count as the thing described.
usage.afterNoun: After a noun, proper refers to the thing in the strict sense, as in the city proper.
usage.social: In socially proper or perfectly proper, it refers to what is considered acceptable or decorous.

en: suitable or correct for a particular purpose or situation
genuine or substantial enough to count as the thing named
socially acceptable or in keeping with expected standards of conduct
(after a noun) considered in its strict sense, excluding surrounding or related parts
(UK informal, before a noun) complete or total, used for emphasis
ja: 用途や状況に合った、適切な、正規の
本格的な、ちゃんとした
礼儀や社会的な規範にかなった
（名詞の後ろで）厳密な意味での～そのもの
（英・くだけた強調）まったくの、すっかり

nuance.en: Proper procedure suggests that there is an established way to do something. A proper meal is a substantial meal that counts as a real meal. The city proper refers to the city within its own boundaries. In informal British English, a proper mess means a complete mess.
nuance.ja: proper procedure は「定められた手順」に沿うことを示唆する。a proper meal は「食事と呼べるだけのちゃんとした食事」。the city proper は周辺地域を除いた「市域そのもの」。英国のくだけた言い方では、a proper mess は「ひどい有り様」と程度を強調する。

en: appropriate: Focuses on fit for the context. An appropriate response suits the situation. Proper channels suggests an established route for raising an issue.
correct: Focuses on accuracy or conformity to a rule. The correct address is the right address. Proper equipment is equipment suitable for the task.
adequate: Means sufficient to meet a need. Adequate training meets the minimum need. Proper training suggests training of the right kind or standard.
ja: appropriate：場面にふさわしいことに焦点がある。an appropriate response は「状況にふさわしい対応」。proper channels は、問題を伝えるための「所定の経路」を示唆する。
correct：事実やルールに照らした正しさに焦点がある。the correct address は「正しい住所」。proper equipment は「作業に適した装備」。
adequate：必要な水準を満たしていることに焦点がある。adequate training は「必要を満たす研修」。proper training は「内容や水準が適切な研修」を示唆する。

note.en: Close when describing equipment or arrangements that fit the purpose.
note.ja: 用途に合う装備や準備について使う場合に近い。

note.en: Close in expressions such as a proper meal or a proper break.
note.ja: a proper meal や a proper break の「ちゃんとした」という意味で近い。

etymology.en: From Old French propre and Latin proprius, ‘one’s own, particular to oneself’. The sense of something belonging to the thing itself is visible in expressions such as the city proper.
etymology.ja: 古フランス語 propre およびラテン語 proprius（自分自身の、固有の）に由来する。the city proper の「市域そのもの」には、対象そのものに属するという意味が見える。

equivalents.de: angemessen / ordnungsgemäß / richtig / im eigentlichen Sinne
equivalents.fr: approprié / en règle / véritable / à proprement parler

go through the proper channels
proper equipment

ja: follow the proper procedure — 所定の手順に従う

proper documentation — 必要な書類、正規の書類
proper training — 適切な研修

a proper name — 固有名

en: Please raise the issue through the proper channels.
I’ve been snacking all day and haven’t had a proper meal.
The figures cover the city proper and exclude the surrounding suburbs.
She wondered whether it was proper to bring up the dispute at dinner.
We made a proper mess of the kitchen trying to bake that cake.
ja: Please raise the issue through the proper channels. — その問題は所定の窓口を通して提起してください。
I’ve been snacking all day and haven’t had a proper meal. — 一日中つまみ食いばかりで、ちゃんとした食事を取っていない。
The figures cover the city proper and exclude the surrounding suburbs. — この数字の対象は市域そのもので、周辺の郊外は含まれていない。
She wondered whether it was proper to bring up the dispute at dinner. — 彼女は、夕食の席でその揉め事を持ち出すのは礼儀にかなうだろうかと思った。
We made a proper mess of the kitchen trying to bake that cake. — あのケーキを焼こうとして、台所をひどく散らかしてしまった。

usage.manner: Often follows an intransitive verb or the object of a transitive verb. It can also come before a past participle, as in a properly completed form.
usage.scope: Properly speaking introduces a more precise use of a term.

en: in the correct or appropriate way
as intended, or to the expected standard
with due care, attention, or completeness
ja: 正しく、適切な方法で
本来どおりに、正常に
きちんと、十分に

nuance.en: What counts as proper depends on the context. Fill in the form properly means to complete it as required. The printer isn’t working properly means it isn’t functioning as expected. I haven’t eaten properly today can mean that you haven’t had a decent meal.
nuance.ja: 何をもって「ちゃんと」とするかは文脈で変わる。fill in the form properly は「所定の要領で用紙に記入する」。The printer isn’t working properly. は「プリンターが正常に動かない」。I haven’t eaten properly today. は「今日はまともな食事を取っていない」という意味で使える。

en: proper: The adjective modifies a noun, as in a proper meal. The adverb properly describes an action or how something functions, as in eat properly.
correctly: Highlights whether something matches the facts or instructions, as in spell a name correctly. Properly also covers whether a task was done with enough care or something works as expected.
thoroughly: Emphasizes depth or completeness. Review a draft thoroughly stresses how closely you examine it. Review it properly emphasizes doing the review to the expected standard.
ja: proper：形容詞。a proper meal は「ちゃんとした食事」。副詞 properly を使う eat properly は「ちゃんと食事を取る」。
correctly：spell a name correctly（名前を正しくつづる）のように、事実や指示との一致に焦点を当てる。properly は、十分な注意を払ったか、本来どおりに機能しているかも表せる。
thoroughly：「徹底的に、隅々まで」。review a draft thoroughly は細部まで確認すること、review it properly は求められる水準で確認することに焦点を当てる。

note.en: Close when something must be done according to instructions.
note.ja: 手順や指示どおりに行う意味で近い。

note.en: Close when behavior should fit the situation.
note.ja: 場にふさわしい振る舞いをする意味で近い。

etymology.en: Formed from proper and the adverb-forming suffix -ly.
etymology.ja: 形容詞 proper に、副詞をつくる接尾辞 -ly が付いた語。

en: work properly
install something properly
fill in a form properly
be properly documented
behave properly
eat properly

behave properly — 場にふさわしく振る舞う

properly speaking — 厳密に言えば

patterns: reduce / prevent / get rid of static cling

usage.noun: Use static cling without an indefinite article when naming the effect. To describe which items stick together, use cling to or stick to.

en: the tendency of clothes or other materials to stick to a surface or to each other because of static electricity
ja: 静電気で衣類が体やほかの衣類にまとわりつくこと、静電気による貼りつき

nuance.en: Static cling names the sticking effect itself. It often comes up when laundry comes out of the dryer or when a skirt sticks to tights. In casual conversation, people may say My skirt is sticking to my tights or blame it on static.
nuance.ja: static cling は、静電気で物が貼りつく現象を指す。乾燥機から出した衣類同士がくっついたり、スカートがタイツにまとわりついたりする場面でよく使う。会話なら My skirt is sticking to my tights. のように、何が何に貼りつくかをそのまま言える。

en: static electricity: The electrical phenomenon that can cause sticking, a spark, or a small shock. Static cling is the sticking effect.
cling to: A verb phrase for sticking or holding closely. It can describe wet fabric sticking to skin, where moisture is the cause.
ja: static electricity：「静電気」。貼りつきや火花、触れたときのピリッとした刺激の原因になる。static cling はそのうち貼りつく現象を指す。
cling to：「～にぴったりくっつく、まとわりつく」。濡れた服が肌に貼りつく場合にも使える。

note.en: A common shorthand for static electricity in laundry contexts, as in There’s a lot of static in these clothes.
note.ja: 洗濯物の話では、静電気を static と略して言うことがある。

etymology.en: Static refers to static electricity, and cling names the sticking effect.
etymology.ja: static は static electricity（静電気）、cling は「くっつくこと、まとわりつき」を表す。

en: reduce static cling
prevent static cling
get rid of static cling
static cling in laundry
cling to your tights
ja: reduce static cling — 静電気による貼りつきを抑える
prevent static cling — 静電気によるまとわりつきを防ぐ
get rid of static cling — 静電気によるまとわりつきを解消する
static cling in laundry — 洗濯物の静電気による貼りつき
cling to your tights — タイツにまとわりつく

en: Static cling was so bad that two socks stuck to the inside of my sweater.
My skirt keeps sticking to my tights. I think it’s static.
This spray is designed to reduce static cling in clothes.
ja: Static cling was so bad that two socks stuck to the inside of my sweater. — 静電気でひどくまとわりついて、靴下が２枚、セーターの内側に貼りついていた。
My skirt keeps sticking to my tights. I think it’s static. — スカートが何度もタイツにまとわりつく。たぶん静電気だ。
This spray is designed to reduce static cling in clothes. — このスプレーは、衣類が静電気でまとわりつくのを抑えるためのものです。

usage.noun: Static electricity is uncountable. Use a static shock to refer to one instance of getting a shock.

en: electric charge that builds up on an object and can discharge suddenly
ja: 静電気。物体にたまった電荷のことで、急に放電することがある。

nuance.en: Static electricity names the buildup of charge. A static shock is what you feel when some of that charge discharges through you. In everyday conversation, static alone often means static electricity.
nuance.ja: static electricity は物体にたまった電荷を指す。static shock は、その電荷が体を通って放電したときのピリッとした刺激。日常会話では static だけで「静電気」を表すことも多い。

en: static cling: The sticking of clothes or other materials due to static electricity.
static shock: A brief shock caused by static discharge. Use get a static shock for a single incident.
electric current: The flow of electric charge. A static discharge can produce a brief current.
ja: static cling：静電気で衣類などが貼りつく現象。
static shock：静電気の放電で感じる刺激。一度ピリッとしたことは get a static shock と言える。
electric current：電荷の流れ、電流。静電気の放電でも、一時的に電流が流れる。

note.en: A common short form in everyday contexts such as laundry and clothing.
note.ja: 洗濯物や衣類などの話でよく使われる略し方。

etymology.en: A compound of static and electricity. Static describes the charge buildup before discharge.
etymology.ja: static（静的な）と electricity（電気）の組み合わせ。static は、放電する前に電荷がたまっている状態を表す。

en: a buildup of static electricity
generate static electricity
static electricity builds up
discharge static electricity
get a static shock
ja: a buildup of static electricity — 静電気の蓄積
generate static electricity — 静電気を発生させる
static electricity builds up — 静電気がたまる
discharge static electricity — 静電気を放電する
get a static shock — 静電気でピリッとする

en: I got a static shock when I touched the metal doorknob.
Rubbing a balloon against your hair can generate static electricity.
Static electricity can make your clothes stick together when you take them out of the dryer.
ja: I got a static shock when I touched the metal doorknob. — 金属のドアノブに触れたら、静電気でピリッとした。
Rubbing a balloon against your hair can generate static electricity. — 風船を髪の毛にこすりつけると、静電気が発生することがある。
Static electricity can make your clothes stick together when you take them out of the dryer. — 乾燥機から出した服が、静電気でくっつくことがある。

usage.adjective: Use before a noun or after be, stay, or remain.
usage.noun: Use static without an indefinite article for radio noise or static electricity. A burst of static describes a short burst of noise.

en: (adjective) staying in the same position or remaining unchanged
(noun) crackling or hissing noise caused by interference in a signal
(noun) static electricity, especially in everyday speech
ja: （形容詞）動かない、変化しない、静的な
（名詞）ラジオなどの信号に混じるザーッ、バリバリという雑音
（名詞）静電気。日常会話での略称

nuance.en: Prices remained static means they stayed at the same level. A static image is still. In the expression static electricity, static refers to charge that has built up. As a noun, static can mean either the charge or the noise, depending on what you are talking about.
nuance.ja: Prices remained static. は「価格が同じ水準のままだった」。a static image は「動きのない画像」。static electricity の static は、電荷がたまっている状態を表す。名詞の static は文脈によって「静電気」や「ザザーッという雑音」になる。

en: stationary: Focuses on physical position. A stationary car is not moving. Static can describe things such as prices or design as well.
stagnant: Usually implies a lack of movement or growth that is undesirable. Sales remained static simply says they did not change. Sales were stagnant suggests a lack of progress.
static cling: The sticking effect caused by static electricity. Static on its own can name the charge behind the effect.
ja: stationary：物理的に動いていないことに焦点がある。a stationary car は「停止している車」。static は価格やデザインなどの変化の有無も表す。
stagnant：「停滞した」。変化や成長がないことを問題として捉える含みが出やすい。Sales remained static. は「売上が横ばいだった」という記述。
static cling：静電気による貼りつき。static 単独では、その原因となる静電気を指すことがある。

note.en: Close when describing a level, condition, or arrangement that stays the same.
note.ja: 水準や状態、配置が変化しないという意味で近い。

note.en: A broader term for disruption of a signal. Static is the noise you can hear.
note.ja: interference は信号の妨害を広く指す。static は耳に聞こえる雑音を指す。

etymology.en: The adjective is related to the idea of standing still. The electrical noun is short for static electricity.
etymology.ja: 形容詞の根にあるのは「じっと立っている、動かない」という考え方。静電気を指す名詞用法は static electricity を縮めたもの。

grammar.countability: countable as a noun, also commonly plural dynamics
patterns: the dynamic between A and B

usage.adjective: Before a noun, dynamic can mean energetic or changing in response to events or inputs.
usage.noun: A dynamic can describe a particular pattern of interaction. The plural dynamics often refers to several interacting forces or patterns.

en: (adjective) energetic, active, and able to make things happen
(adjective) changing or responding to conditions
(noun) a pattern of interaction or an influence that shapes how people or things interact
ja: （形容詞）活力のある、精力的な
（形容詞）変化する、状況に応じて変わる、動的な
（名詞）人や物事の相互作用、関係の中で働く力やそのパターン

nuance.en: A dynamic leader brings energy and initiative. Dynamic pricing changes in response to conditions such as demand. The dynamic between two people describes how they interact, including patterns such as who takes the lead.
nuance.ja: a dynamic leader は活力があり、自ら物事を進めるリーダー。dynamic pricing は需要などに応じて価格を変える仕組み。the dynamic between two people は、どちらが主導権を握るかなど、二人がどう影響し合うかを表す。

en: static: Staying the same or still. A static display stays fixed. A dynamic display can update as its inputs change.
energetic: Highlights energy and activity. Dynamic can also suggest initiative or the ability to drive change.
relationship: A broad term for a connection between people or groups. Dynamic focuses on how they interact within that relationship.
ja: static：動かない、変化しない。a static display は表示が固定されている。a dynamic display は入力などに応じて表示が変わりうる。
energetic：活力があることに焦点がある。dynamic には自ら動き、変化を起こすという含みも出る。
relationship：人や集団のつながりを広く指す。dynamic はその関係の中でどう影響し合うかに焦点がある。

note.en: Close when describing a person or team.
note.ja: 人やチームの活力を表す場合に近い。

note.en: Close when describing conditions that evolve over time.
note.ja: 時間とともに変化する状況を表す場合に近い。

etymology.en: Ultimately from Greek dynamis, meaning power or force.
etymology.ja: 「力」を表すギリシャ語 dynamis にさかのぼる。

word: like taking candy from a baby

patterns: it is / was like taking candy from a baby
verb-ing + be + like taking candy from a baby
as easy as taking candy from a baby

usage.register: Informal, especially American English. Often used to sum up how easily something was done, including a win over an opponent.
usage.form: After like, use taking. In this expression, candy is uncountable and a modifies baby.

en: extremely easy to do, often because there is little or no resistance
ja: いとも簡単にできる、拍子抜けするほどたやすい、朝飯前だ

nuance.en: The image is of taking candy from someone who can do little to stop you. It can sound playful when describing a game and boastful or dismissive when describing a real opponent. It can also describe taking advantage of someone who is easy to deceive.
nuance.ja: 赤ん坊からお菓子を取り上げるように、抵抗をほとんど受けずにできるというたとえ。ゲームの話なら冗談めいて聞こえるが、実際の対戦相手について言うと、自慢げだったり、相手を見下していたりするように響くことがある。だましやすい相手につけ込む場面でも使える。

en: a piece of cake: Says a task was very easy, often in a lighthearted way. Like taking candy from a baby can also suggest that an opponent could put up little resistance.
a walk in the park: Often describes a task or experience that takes little effort or causes little trouble.
ja: a piece of cake：「朝飯前だ」。作業の簡単さを気軽に言う表現。like taking candy from a baby には、相手がほとんど抵抗できなかったという含みも出る。
a walk in the park：「楽なこと」。手間や苦労がほとんどない作業や経験についてよく使う。

note.en: A common informal expression for something very easy.
note.ja: 「とても簡単なこと」を表す口語表現。

etymology.en: The idiom draws on the image of how little effort it would take to take candy away from a baby.
etymology.ja: 赤ん坊からお菓子を取り上げるのにほとんど労力が要らない、というたとえ。

en: It was like taking candy from a baby.
Winning was like taking candy from a baby.
as easy as taking candy from a baby
ja: It was like taking candy from a baby. — いとも簡単だった。
Winning was like taking candy from a baby. — 勝つのは朝飯前だった。
as easy as taking candy from a baby — 拍子抜けするほど簡単な

en: I thought the final round would be tough, but it was like taking candy from a baby.
Once I spotted the pattern, solving the puzzle was like taking candy from a baby.
To the con artist, getting people to trust him was like taking candy from a baby.
ja: I thought the final round would be tough, but it was like taking candy from a baby. — 最終ラウンドは苦戦すると思っていたけれど、拍子抜けするほど簡単だった。
Once I spotted the pattern, solving the puzzle was like taking candy from a baby. — パターンに気づいたら、そのパズルを解くのは朝飯前だった。
To the con artist, getting people to trust him was like taking candy from a baby. — その詐欺師にとって、人を信用させるのはいともたやすいことだった。

usage.adverb: Often comes after the verb or its object. Stay overnight has no object, and leave the dough overnight has the dough as its object.
usage.adjective: Usually comes before a noun, as in an overnight flight or an overnight success.
usage.verb: Can mean to stay somewhere for a night or, especially in US shipping, to send something for next-day delivery.

en: (adverb / adjective) for one night or during the night
(adverb / adjective) with arrival or delivery by the next day
(adverb / adjective) very quickly or suddenly, sometimes figuratively
(verb) to stay somewhere for a night, or to send something for next-day delivery
ja: （副詞・形容詞）一晩、夜の間に、一泊の
（副詞・形容詞）翌日までに、翌日着の
（副詞・形容詞）一夜にして、急に、あっという間に
（動詞）一泊する、翌日着で送る

nuance.en: Stay overnight describes spending the night somewhere. It snowed overnight means that snow fell during the night. An overnight delivery is scheduled for the next day. In Nothing will change overnight, overnight means very quickly and need not refer to a literal night.
nuance.ja: stay overnight は「一泊する」。It snowed overnight. は「夜の間に雪が降った」。overnight delivery は「翌日配達」。Nothing will change overnight. の overnight は比喩的に「すぐには」を表し、実際に一晩という時間を示すとは限らない。

en: all night: Emphasizes that an activity or state continued throughout the night. It rained overnight leaves the duration of the rain open. It rained all night says it continued through the night.
the next day: Identifies when something happened. Overnight often highlights the interval, speed or delivery arrangement that brings something to the next day.
suddenly: Highlights an abrupt change. Overnight can emphasize how little time a development took, as in become an overnight success.
ja: all night：「一晩中」。It rained overnight. は夜の間に雨が降ったというだけで、降り続いた時間は分からない。It rained all night. は夜通し降ったという意味。
the next day：「その翌日」。出来事がいつ起きたかを示す。overnight は、翌日までの時間の短さや翌日着の手配を表すことがある。
suddenly：「突然」。変化の急さを強調する。overnight は an overnight success（あっという間の成功）のように、結果が出るまでの短さにも焦点を当てる。

note.en: Close when an event happens between evening and morning.
note.ja: 出来事が夜の間に起きたことを表す場合に近い。

note.en: Close in the figurative sense.
note.ja: 「あっという間に」という比喩的な用法で近い。

etymology.en: A compound of over and night, referring to the span from one evening into the following morning.
etymology.ja: over と night の複合語。夜をまたいで翌朝に至る時間を表す。

usage.noun: Use a household for one person living alone or a group living together as one domestic unit.
usage.modifier: Before a noun, household can mean related to the home, its occupants, or everyday domestic use.

en: (noun) one person living alone or a group of people living together as a domestic unit
(adjective) connected with the home or the people who live in it, or intended for use in the home
ja: （名詞）世帯。一人暮らしの人、または一緒に暮らす人たちを生活の単位として捉えたもの
（形容詞）家庭の、家計の、家庭用の

nuance.en: Household looks at who lives together as a unit. A person living alone can be a one-person household, and a household may include people who are unrelated. Household income and per household are common when counting or comparing domestic units. Household chores are jobs done around the home. A household name is a person, brand, or other name widely recognized by the public.
nuance.ja: household は、一緒に暮らす人たちを生活の単位として捉える。単身世帯もあり、血縁関係のない人を含むこともある。household income（世帯収入）や per household（一世帯あたり）は、世帯単位で数えたり比較したりするときによく使う。household chores は「日常の家事」。a household name は、世間に広く知られている人やブランドなどを指す。

en: family: Focuses on family ties, which can extend across several households. Household focuses on a living arrangement or domestic unit.

home: Often refers to the place where someone lives. Home insurance is insurance connected with the property or its contents. Household expenses are the living expenses of the people in the household.
domestic: Can mean connected with home life or, in expressions such as domestic flights, within one country. Household income is tied specifically to a domestic unit.
ja: family：親族や家族としてのつながりに焦点がある。一つの family が複数の household に分かれて暮らすこともある。household は生活の単位としての世帯に焦点がある。
home：暮らす場所を指すことが多い。home insurance は住宅や家財に関する保険。household expenses は世帯の生活費。
domestic：「家庭の」のほか、domestic flights（国内便）のように「国内の」という意味もある。household income は「世帯収入」。

note.en: Close when modifying a noun related to home life or home use.
note.ja: 家庭生活や家庭での用途に関する語を修飾するときに近い。

etymology.en: A compound of house and hold, referring to a home and the people belonging to it.
etymology.ja: house と hold の複合語。家と、そこに属する人々を指す語。

grammar.countability: countable, often plural for routine duties
patterns: something is / feels like a chore
make something less of a chore

usage.routine: Use chores in the plural for routine duties collectively. Use a chore for an individual job or for an activity that feels tedious.

en: a small job that needs doing regularly, especially around the home
a task that feels tedious, unpleasant, or burdensome
ja: 定期的にこなす雑用、特に日常の家事
面倒で気の進まない作業、骨の折れる用事

nuance.en: Household chores groups together recurring jobs such as doing laundry or taking out the trash. It can be a neutral label. Calling something a chore emphasizes how tedious it feels, even when it has nothing to do with housework.
nuance.ja: household chores は、洗濯やゴミ出しなど繰り返し行う家事の総称で、中立的にも使える。何かを a chore と呼ぶと、その作業が億劫だという気持ちがにじむ。家事以外の作業についても使える。

en: task: A broad word for a piece of work. Chore often suggests routine upkeep or something you find tedious.
housework: An uncountable word for work done to look after a home. Chore is countable and can name one of the individual jobs.
errand: Often a short trip to do something, such as picking up a prescription. A chore can be done at home, like folding laundry.
ja: task：作業一般を指す。chore は日々の維持に必要な仕事や、面倒に感じる作業を指すことが多い。
housework：家を維持するための仕事をまとめて指す不可算名詞。chore は可算名詞で、個々の作業も数えられる。
errand：処方薬を受け取りに行くなど、外出を伴うちょっとした用事。chore は洗濯物をたたむなど、家の中でする作業にも使える。

note.en: Close for a recurring job that needs to be done.
note.ja: 繰り返しこなす必要がある仕事を表す場合に近い。

etymology.en: A variant of char, an older word for an odd job. Its earlier forms included Middle English cherre and Old English cerr, meaning a turn or occasion.
etymology.ja: 「ちょっとした仕事」を指した古い語 char の異形。中英語 cherre を経て、「順番、機会」などを表す古英語 cerr にさかのぼる。

usage.noun: Often denotes a wood managed by regularly cutting back trees. It may also refer more generally to a small wood or thicket.
usage.verb: Transitive. A species or area can be the object, as in coppice the hazel or coppice part of the woodland.

en: (noun) a small wood or stand, especially one managed by repeatedly cutting back trees to obtain new growth and wood
(verb) to cut a tree or shrub back close to the ground so that new shoots grow from the base
ja: （名詞）小さな雑木林。特に、木を周期的に切り戻し、株からの新芽を育てて木材を得る林
（動詞）木や低木を地際まで切り戻し、株から新芽を出させる。萌芽更新を行う

nuance.en: In woodland management, coppicing leaves a living stump called a stool. New shoots grow from it and can be harvested later. A hazel coppice is a stand of hazel managed in this way.
nuance.ja: 林の管理では、切り戻した後に生きた株（stool）を残し、そこから伸びた新しい枝や幹を後に収穫する。a hazel coppice は、この方法で管理するハシバミの林。

en: copse: A general word for a small group of trees or a small wood. Coppice, especially in forestry, often implies repeated cutting and regrowth.
pollard: To cut back a tree higher up on the trunk so that new shoots grow above ground. Coppicing cuts close to ground level.
prune: A general term for trimming or removing parts of a plant. Coppice names a particular way of cutting for regrowth from the base.
ja: copse：小さな林や木立を広く指す。coppice は林業では、繰り返し切って新芽を育てる管理を含意することが多い。
pollard：幹の高い位置で切り戻し、地面から離れた位置に新しい枝を出させる。coppice は地際で切り戻す。
prune：枝などを切る、剪定するという広い表現。coppice は株元から再生させるための特定の切り方を指す。

note.en: Close for a small wood in the general noun sense.
note.ja: 名詞で小さな林を広く指す場合に近い。

etymology.en: From Old French copeiz or coupeiz, referring to a wood where trees had been cut. The English word copse developed as a shortened form of coppice.
etymology.ja: 木を伐った林を指す古フランス語 copeiz または coupeiz に由来する。英語の copse は coppice の短縮形から生まれた。
